DAMGHANI:v1p249/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p249/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p249/r1.claim: Samāʾ can mean clouds; this is the second face shown in the excerpt.
DAMGHANI:v1p249/r1.anchor: السماء السحاب قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p291#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p291#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p291#2/r1.claim: The call to worship is followed by creation as proof that God deserves worship; the warning against partners follows because the creation evidence establishes that He has no partner in worship or creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p291#2/r1.anchor: إلى آخره بوصف هو دليل استحقاقه للعبادة

STUDYQURAN:2:22/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:22/r1.speaker: The Prophet
STUDYQURAN:2:22/r1.claim: The Prophet was asked about the greatest sin in God's sight and replied that it is setting up equals to God despite His having created you.
STUDYQURAN:2:22/r1.anchor: the Prophet was asked, “O Messenger of God, what is the greatest sin in the Sight of God?”

STUDYQURAN:2:22/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:22/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:22/r2.claim: Thamarāt means natural produce usable as food and can also symbolize spiritual sustenance for the soul.
STUDYQURAN:2:22/r2.anchor: here is understood in both the most general sense of natural produce

STUDYQURAN:2:22/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:22/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:22/r3.claim: The earth-and-sky imagery has parallels in 21:31–32, 50:6–7, and 79:27–31.
STUDYQURAN:2:22/r3.anchor: Earth and sky imagery similar to that mentioned in this verse can be found in 21:31–32; 50:6–7; 79:27–31.

TAB-FULL:v1p388/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p388/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p388/r1.claim: Mentioning the earth as a favor reminds people of God’s blessings and calls them to obey; He shows compassion and completes His favor so they may be guided, without needing their worship.
TAB-FULL:v1p388/r1.anchor: يذكر ربنا جل ذكره بذلك من قيله زيادة نعمه عندهم وآلائه لديهم، ليذكروا أياديه عندهم فينيبوا إلى طاعته

TAB-FULL:v1p388/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p388/r2.speaker: السدي، أبو مالك، أبو صالح، ابن عباس، مرة، ابن مسعود، وناس من أصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p388/r2.claim: The report transmitted from al-Suddī and these authorities says earth is a bed people walk upon, a resting place and settled abode.
TAB-FULL:v1p388/r2.anchor: عن السدي، في خبر ذكره، عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس

TAB-FULL:v1p388/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p388/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p388/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses the earth as a bed spread out for people.
TAB-FULL:v1p388/r3.anchor: عن قتادة: " {الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا} [البقرة: 22] قال: مهادا لكم "

TAB-FULL:v1p388/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p388/r4.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v1p388/r4.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas glosses the earth as a bed.
TAB-FULL:v1p388/r4.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس: " {الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا} [البقرة: 22] أي مهادا "

TAB-FULL:v1p389/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r1.claim: The sky is named for its height above earth and its inhabitants; anything above another thing is a sky to what lies below, as with a house roof.
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r1.anchor: وإنما سميت السماء سماء لعلوها على الأرض وعلى سكانها من خلقه، وكل شيء كان فوق شيء آخر فهو لما تحته سماء

TAB-FULL:v1p389/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r2.claim: A roof is called a sky because it is elevated above the house; سما فلان لفلان means he rose above or confronted him from above.
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r2.anchor: ولذلك قيل لسقف البيت سماؤه، لأنه فوقه مرتفع عليه ولذلك قيل: سما فلان لفلان

TAB-FULL:v1p389/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r3.speaker: الفرزدق
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r3.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s use of سمونا witnesses the sense of rising or going up above.
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r3.anchor: كما قال الفرزدق: [البحر الطويل] سمونا لنجران اليماني وأهله

TAB-FULL:v1p389/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r4.speaker: النابغة الذبياني
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r4.claim: Al-Nābigha’s phrase سمت لي نظرة means a glance rose or appeared, supporting the sense of elevation.
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r4.anchor: وكما قال نابغة بني ذبيان: [البحر الوافر] سمت لي نظرة فرأيت منها

TAB-FULL:v1p389/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r5.speaker: السدي، أبو مالك، أبو صالح، ابن عباس، مرة، ابن مسعود، وناس من أصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r5.claim: The report transmitted from al-Suddī and these authorities describes the sky as a dome-shaped structure and roof over earth.
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r5.anchor: عن السدي، في خبر ذكره، عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود

TAB-FULL:v1p389/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r6.claim: Qatāda says God made the sky a ceiling for people.
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r6.anchor: عن قتادة: " في قول الله {والسماء بناء} [البقرة: 22] قال: جعل السماء سقفا لك "

TAB-FULL:v1p389/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r7.claim: God names earth and sky among His favors because they provide food, livelihood, and the basis of worldly life; their Creator deserves obedience, gratitude, and worship instead of idols.
TAB-FULL:v1p389/r7.anchor: لأن منهما أقواتهم وأرزاقهم ومعايشهم، وبهما قوام دنياهم، فأعلمهم أن الذي خلقهما

TAB-FULL:v1p390/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p390/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p390/r1.claim: God alone created people, provides for them, and sustains them, unlike the rivals they associate with Him.
TAB-FULL:v1p390/r1.anchor: وأنه هو الذي خلقهم وهو الذي يرزقهم ويكفلهم دون من جعلوه له ندا وعدلا

TAB-FULL:v1p390/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p390/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p390/r2.claim: He has no equal, and no other being benefits, harms, creates, or provides for them.
TAB-FULL:v1p390/r2.anchor: وأنه لا ند له ولا عدل، ولا لهم نافع ولا ضار ولا خالق ولا رازق سواه

TAB-FULL:v1p391/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r1.claim: An andād is an equal, counterpart, or likeness; Ḥassān ibn Thābit’s verse uses ند in that sense.
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r1.anchor: والند: العدل والمثل، كما قال حسان بن ثابت: [البحر الوافر] أتهجوه ولست له بند

TAB-FULL:v1p391/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses the andād as equals.
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: " {فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا} [البقرة: 22] أي عدلاء "

TAB-FULL:v1p391/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r3.claim: Mujāhid also glosses the andād as equals.
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا} [البقرة: 22] أي عدلاء "

TAB-FULL:v1p391/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r4.speaker: السدي، أبو مالك، أبو صالح، ابن عباس، مرة، ابن مسعود، وناس من أصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r4.claim: The report transmitted from al-Suddī and these authorities identifies as andād people obeyed in disobedience to God.
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r4.anchor: عن السدي، عن خبر ذكره عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود

TAB-FULL:v1p391/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the andād are the gods people set beside God and treated as they treated Him.
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد " في قول الله: {فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا} [البقرة: 22] قال: الأنداد: الآلهة التي جعلوها معه

TAB-FULL:v1p391/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r6.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in al-Ḍaḥḥāk’s report, glosses them as likenesses.
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، " في قوله: {فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا} [البقرة: 22] قال: أشباها "

TAB-FULL:v1p391/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r7.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r7.claim: ʿIkrima gives as an example saying that without one’s dog a thief would enter or the dog would bark, attributing power to a creature.
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة: " {فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا} [البقرة: 22] أي تقولوا: لولا كلبنا لدخل علينا اللص الدار

TAB-FULL:v1p391/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r8.claim: God forbids associating or worshipping anything besides Him, or taking a created being as His partner in obedience.
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r8.anchor: فنهاهم الله تعالى أن يشركوا به شيئا وأن يعبدوا غيره، أو يتخذوا له ندا وعدلا في الطاعة

TAB-FULL:v1p391/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r9.claim: Since God alone created, owns, feeds, and blesses them, and they know every blessing comes from Him, they must devote worship and obedience to Him alone.
TAB-FULL:v1p391/r9.anchor: كما لا شريك لي في خلقكم وفي رزقكم الذي أرزقكم، وملكي إياكم، ونعمتي التي أنعمتها عليكم

TAB-FULL:v1p393/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p393/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p393/r1.claim: One reported view takes the warning to address all polytheists, including Arab idolaters and disbelievers among the People of the two scriptures.
TAB-FULL:v1p393/r1.anchor: ذكر من قال: عني بها جميع عبدة الأوثان من العرب وكفار أهل الكتابين

TAB-FULL:v1p393/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p393/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p393/r2.claim: The warning addressed disbelievers and hypocrites: do not associate powerless partners when you know God alone sustains you and the Messenger's monotheism is true.
TAB-FULL:v1p393/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " نزل ذلك في الفريقين جميعا من الكفار والمنافقين

TAB-FULL:v1p393/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p393/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p393/r3.claim: People know God created them and the heavens and earth, yet still assign Him partners.
TAB-FULL:v1p393/r3.anchor: في قوله: " {وأنتم تعلمون} [البقرة: 22] أي تعلمون أن الله خلقكم وخلق السموات والأرض

TAB-FULL:v1p393/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p393/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p393/r4.claim: Mujahid restricts the address to the People of Scripture, who know from the Torah and Gospel that God is one and has no counterpart.
TAB-FULL:v1p393/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا وأنتم تعلمون} [البقرة: 22] أنه إله واحد في التوراة والإنجيل

TAB-FULL:v1p393/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p393/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p393/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects limiting the address to the People of Scripture: Arabs also acknowledged God as creator and provider while associating others in worship, as the Qur'an says.
TAB-FULL:v1p393/r5.anchor: قد أخبر في كتابه عنها أنها كانت تقر بوحدانية، غير أنها كانت تشرك في عبادته

TAB-FULL:v1p395/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p395/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p395/r1.claim: The address is general: every accountable person who knows God's oneness and sole creative power, Arab or non-Arab, literate or unlettered, is forbidden to associate partners.
TAB-FULL:v1p395/r1.anchor: من أنه يعني بذلك كل مكلف عالم بوحدانية الله، وأنه لا شريك له في خلقه

TABATABAI:2:21-25/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25/r3.claim: Andād is the plural of nidd, meaning an equal or counterpart and matching mithl in form and sense.
TABATABAI:2:21-25/r3.anchor: الأنداد جمع ند كمثل، وزنا ومعنى

TABATABAI:2:21-25/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25/r4.claim: The clause “while you know” is left unrestricted and functions circumstantially with the prohibition against making peers for God.
TABATABAI:2:21-25/r4.anchor: وعدم تقييد قوله تعالى { وأنتم تعلمون } بقيد خاص وجعله حالا من قوله تعالى { فلا تجعلوا }

TABATABAI:2:21-25/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25/r5.claim: The unrestricted condition sharply reinforces the ban: whatever knowledge people possess, they must not associate equals with the God who created them and their forebears and ordered their sustenance.
TABATABAI:2:21-25/r5.anchor: يفيد التأكيد البالغ في النهي بأن الإنسان وله علم ما، كيفما كان لا يجوز له أن يتخذ لله سبحانه أندادا

TABRISI:2:22/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r1.speaker: جماعة من القراء
TABRISI:2:22/r1.claim: A group of readers assimilates جَعَلَ لَكُمُ as جعلكم, joining identical adjacent letters amid frequent vowel movements.
TABRISI:2:22/r1.anchor: أدغم جماعة من القراء قوله جعل لكم فقالوا جعلكم

TABRISI:2:22/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r2.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:2:22/r2.claim: Most readers pronounce the two words separately because they are distinct words; fuller arguments belong to specialist qirāʾāt books.
TABRISI:2:22/r2.anchor: ومن أظهر وعليه أكثر القراء فلأنهما منفصلان من كلمتين

TABRISI:2:22/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:22/r3.claim: جعل, خلق, and إحداث are near-synonyms for making, creating, or bringing about.

TABRISI:2:22/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:22/r4.claim: الأرض ordinarily means earth, but can also name an animal’s legs; the cited poem uses it in this latter sense.
TABRISI:2:22/r4.anchor: والأرض هي المعروفة والأرض قوائم الدابة ومنه قول الشاعر

TABRISI:2:22/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:22/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās uses الأرض for trembling, in the saying “Has the earth shaken, or am I ill?”
TABRISI:2:22/r5.anchor: وفي كلام ابن عباس أزلزلت الأرض أم بي أرض

TABRISI:2:22/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:22/r6.claim: فراش, بساط, and مهاد all denote a spread or resting place.

TABRISI:2:22/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:22/r7.claim: The sky is named سماء because it is above the earth; whatever is above something is its sky.
TABRISI:2:22/r7.anchor: وسمى السماء سماء لعلوها على الأرض وكل شيء كان فوق شيء

TABRISI:2:22/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:22/r8.claim: سما فلان لفلان means rising toward or above someone; al-Farazdaq’s سمونا illustrates it.
TABRISI:2:22/r8.anchor: وسما فلان لفلان إذا قصد نحوه عاليا عليه قال الفرزدق

TABRISI:2:22/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r9.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:22/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj says anything rising above the earth is a building or structure.
TABRISI:2:22/r9.anchor: قال الزجاج كل ما علا الأرض فهو بناء

TABRISI:2:22/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:22/r10.claim: The root of ماء is موه; its plural is أمواه and its diminutive مويه.
TABRISI:2:22/r10.anchor: والماء أصله موه وجمعه أمواه وتصغيره مويه

TABRISI:2:22/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:22/r11.claim: “From the sky” means from the sky’s direction; a poem’s “from you” similarly means from your direction.
TABRISI:2:22/r11.anchor: وأنزل من السماء أي من ناحية السماء قال الشاعر

TABRISI:2:22/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:22/r12.claim: ند means an equal or counterpart; Ḥassān ibn Thābit’s verse uses it for a match.
TABRISI:2:22/r12.anchor: والند المثل والعدل قال حسان بن ثابت

TABRISI:2:22/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:22/r13.claim: Jarīr’s verse uses نديد for an equal; another reported meaning of ند is an opposite.

TABRISI:2:22/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:22/r14.claim: After commanding worship and acknowledgment of His favor, God enumerates blessings so people infer worship is due to their giver.
TABRISI:2:22/r14.anchor: معنى هذه الآية يتعلق بما قبلها لأنه تعالى أمرهم بعبادته والاعتراف بنعمته ثم عدد لهم صنوف نعمه

TABRISI:2:22/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:22/r15.claim: God made earth a spread where people can settle, lie down, and act; this requires a broad, stable surface.
TABRISI:2:22/r15.anchor: أي بساطا يمكنكم أن تستقروا عليها وتفترشوها وتتصرفوا فيها

TABRISI:2:22/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:22/r16.claim: The sky is a raised, constructed roof.

TABRISI:2:22/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:22/r17.claim: God sends rain from clouds and brings fruit as provision, gift, possession, and nourishment, showing that He—not idols—is creator and provider.
TABRISI:2:22/r17.anchor: أي عطاء لكم وملكا وغذاء لكم

TABRISI:2:22/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:22/r18.claim: Having named His blessings, God rebukes people for setting rivals despite knowing the truth.
TABRISI:2:22/r18.anchor: ثم زجرهم عن أن يجعلوا له ندا مع علمهم بأن ذلك كما أخبرهم به

TABRISI:2:22/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:22/r19.claim: One reading is that they know idols gave none of these blessings and can neither harm nor benefit.
TABRISI:2:22/r19.anchor: أنكم تعلمون أن الأصنام التي تعبدونها لم تنعم عليكم بهذه النعم

TABRISI:2:22/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:22/r20.claim: Alternatively, knowing and discerning make people accountable, bind them to consider the evidence, and leave no excuse for missing the truth.
TABRISI:2:22/r20.anchor: أنكم تعقلون وتميزون ومن كان بهذه الصفة فقد استوفى شرائط التكليف

TABRISI:2:22/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r21.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
TABRISI:2:22/r21.claim: Mujāhid and others take the addressees to be specifically the People of the Torah and Gospel, who know this from their scriptures.
TABRISI:2:22/r21.anchor: ما قاله مجاهد وغيره أن المراد بذلك أهل التوراة والإنجيل دون غيرهم

TABRISI:2:22/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r22.speaker: الشريف الأجل المرتضى
TABRISI:2:22/r22.claim: Al-Murtaḍā reports Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī’s argument that describing earth as a spread and elsewhere as a carpet refutes astrologers’ spherical-earth view.
TABRISI:2:22/r22.anchor: وقال الشريف الأجل المرتضى قدس الله روحه: استدل أبو علي الجبائي

TABRISI:2:22/r23.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:22/r23.speaker: الشريف الأجل المرتضى
TABRISI:2:22/r23.claim: Al-Murtaḍā rejects that inference: the blessing requires only some accessible places to be level; the whole earth need not be flat, and astrologers accept level inhabited surfaces.
TABRISI:2:22/r23.anchor: قال وهذا القدر لا يدل لأنه يكفي من النعمة علينا أن يكون في الأرض بسائط

THALABI:v1p166#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p166#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p166#2/r6.claim: The earth is a spread carpet, place of residence, and place of sleep; heaven is a raised, protected roof.
THALABI:v1p166#2/r6.anchor: الأرض فراشا بساطا ومقاما ومناما. والسماء بناء سقفا مرفوعا محفوظا

THALABI:v1p166#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p166#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p166#2/r7.claim: Here heaven means the clouds, and the water is rain.
THALABI:v1p166#2/r7.anchor: وأنزل من السماء: من السحاب. ماء وهو المطر

THALABI:v1p166#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p166#2/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p166#2/r8.claim: Rain brings out kinds of fruit and varieties of plants.
THALABI:v1p166#2/r8.anchor: فأخرج به من الثمرات من ألوان الثمرات وأنواع النبات

THALABI:v1p166#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p166#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p166#2/r9.claim: The provision is food for people and fodder for their animals.

THALABI:v1p166#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p166#2/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p166#2/r10.anchor: فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا أي أمثالا [وأعدالا]

THALABI:v1p166#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p166#2/r11.speaker: ابن المسيقع
THALABI:v1p166#2/r11.claim: Ibn al-Musayyiʿ reads the word in the singular, nidd.
THALABI:v1p166#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن المسيقع: ندا على الواحد

THALABI:v1p166#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p166#2/r12.speaker: جرير
THALABI:v1p166#2/r12.claim: Jarir's line uses nidd for a peer or counterpart, as evidence for the word's sense.
THALABI:v1p166#2/r12.anchor: أتيما تجعلون إلي ندا … وما تيم لذي حسب

THALABI:v1p166#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p166#2/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p166#2/r13.claim: The addressees know that God is one and created these things.
THALABI:v1p166#2/r13.anchor: وأنتم تعلمون إنه واحد وأنه خالق هذه الأشياء

THALABI:v1p166#2/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p166#2/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v1p166#2/r14.claim: Ibn Masud explains the peers as men obeyed in disobedience to God.
THALABI:v1p166#2/r14.anchor: قال ابن مسعود في قوله: فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا قال: أكفاء من الرجال تطيعوهم في معصية الله

THALABI:v1p166#2/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p166#2/r15.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v1p166#2/r15.claim: Ikrima gives as an example a man saying that without their dog a thief would have entered the house.
THALABI:v1p166#2/r15.anchor: وقال عكرمة: هو قول الرجل: لولا كلبنا لدخل اللص دارنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r1.claim: Earth is feminine and has plurals أرضون، أرضات, and a reported أروض.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r2.claim: The sound masculine plural is explained as compensation for an understood feminine ة omitted from أرض, as with other feminine nouns whose ending is elided.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r2.anchor: وكانت (الأرض) مؤنثة، وكأن فيها (هاء) مرادة، وكأن تقديرها: (أرضة) فلما حذفت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r3.claim: A non-rational feminine noun receiving this plural is given a special privilege; similar cases include سنين and عضين.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r3.anchor: وإذا أدخل شيء مما (¬4) ليس مذكرا عاقلا في هذا النوع من الجمع، فهو حظ ناله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r4.claim: The rā is opened in أرضين to give the form some broken-plural character; the sound plural is generally used for carefully marked, important nouns.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r4.anchor: وفتحوا (الراء) (¬6) في (أرضين) ليدخل الكلمة ضرب من التكسير، استيحاشا من أن يوفوه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r5.claim: Ta marbūṭa can act like a root consonant, as in عرقوة and ترقوة, preserving the preceding wāw that otherwise changes to yāʾ at word-end.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p221/r5.anchor: أن العرب قد [أجرت] (¬3) (هاء التأنيث) مجرى (¬4) لام الفعل في أماكن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r1.claim: The earth is made a bed by being spread flat, not rough and thick so that people could not settle on it; compare its description as a carpet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {فراشا} الأرض فراش الأنام على معنى أنها فرشت لهم، أي (¬9): بسطت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r2.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r2.claim: Al-Azhari derives ماء from ماه on the pattern of قاه, with the difficult hāʾ transformed into a long vowel.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r3.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r3.claim: Al-Layth says the long vowel in ماء replaces a deleted hāʾ, evidenced by its diminutive مويه and forms such as مويهة.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r3.anchor: قال الليث: والمدة في (الماء) خلف (¬5) من (هاء) محذوفة، ويدل على أن الأصل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r4.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r4.claim: Al-Asmaʿi records ماهت البئر for a well becoming abundant in water, with the forms تماه and تموه.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r4.anchor: وقال (¬8) الأصمعي: ماهت البئر، وهي تماه [وتموه موها إذا كثر ماؤها (¬9)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r5.speaker: ابن بزرج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r5.claim: Ibn Barzakh records موهت السماء for abundant rain; forms of the root also describe a well filling and seepage appearing in earth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r5.anchor: ابن بزرج (¬1): موهت السماء، أي: سالت (¬2) ماء كثيرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r6.claim: The relational adjective is ماهي for some, مائي for others; water has plurals مياه and أمواه, illustrated in a poem naming wells.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r6.anchor: والنسبة إلى الماء (ماهي) (¬6)، وغيره (¬7) يقول: مائي (¬8). وجمع الماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r7.claim: Because rain descends from clouds, من السماء can ellipsize 'the direction of heaven'; alternatively السماء itself can mean clouds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p224/r7.anchor: فإن قيل: كيف قال: {وأنزل من السماء}، والماء ينزل من السحاب؟ قيل: هذا من باب حذف المضاف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r1.claim: ثمرات is the plural of ثمرة, originally tree produce, then extended to anything beneficial derived beyond the principal wealth or asset.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r1.anchor: الثمرات: جمع (الثمرة) وهي حمل الشجرة (¬5) في الأصل، ثم صارت اسما لكل (¬6)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r2.claim: Examples include milk showing butter and al-Nadr's term for the curd that forms during churning; the root also describes blessed wealth and intelligence that guides its owner.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r2.anchor: يقال: لبن مثمر (¬1) إذا ظهر زبده (¬2)، وقال النضر (¬3): هو [الثمير]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r3.claim: The exegetes take the fruits here to mean all beneficial things that grow from the earth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون في معنى الثمرات في هذه الآية: أراد جميع ما ينتفع به مما يخرج من الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r4.speaker: شمر عن الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r4.claim: Shamir quoting al-Akhfash defines nidd as an opposite or a likeness, an equal and counterpart.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r4.anchor: روى شمر عن الأخفش قال: (الند) الضد والشبه. أي: لا تجعلوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r5.speaker: لبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r5.claim: Labīd's word نديدتي witnesses the sense of a rival or peer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r5.anchor: وأنشد للبيد (¬1): لكيما (¬2) يكون السندري نديدتي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r6.speaker: أبو الهيثم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r6.claim: Abu al-Haytham uses ندي and نديدي for an opponent pursuing an independent, contrary course, emphasizing a peer who opposes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r6.anchor: وقال أبو الهيثم: يقال للرجل إذا خالفك فأردت وجها تذهب فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r7.speaker: حسان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r7.claim: Hassan's line calls an opponent no peer, meaning not equal in any of his qualities.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r7.anchor: قال حسان: أتهجوه ولست له بند

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r8.claim: The core sense is an adversarial peer, from nadda, to flee; it later broadened to any equal even without opposition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r8.anchor: فحقيقة (الند) المثل المناوئ، وأصله من قولهم: (ند) إذا نفر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r9.claim: Jarir's verse uses ندا to mean an equal: Taym make a peer of the poet despite not matching him in rank.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r9.anchor: أتيما يجعلون إلي ندا ... وما تيم لذي حسب نديد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r10.speaker: ابن عباس، والسدي عن ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi, reporting Ibn Masud, understand the rivals as human equivalents obeyed in disobedience to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس، والسدي فيما ذكره عن ابن مسعود: معناه لا تجعلوا لله أكفاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the rivals as the deities people set up alongside God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r11.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: الأنداد الآلهة (¬6) التي جعلوها معه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r12.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r12.claim: Abu Ishaq treats the prohibition as an argument from their admission that God created them: the rivals cannot create, whereas God is the Creator.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r12.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: هذا احتجاج عليهم لإقرارهم بأن الله خالقهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p231/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p231/r1.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p231/r1.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says this limited knowledge does not conflict with calling idolaters ignorant in 39:64: they know their idols did not create their provisions and surroundings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p231/r1.anchor: قال ابن (¬3) الأنباري: قوله: {وأنتم تعلمون}، (¬4) لا تتنافى مع قوله: {قل أفغير الله تأمروني أعبد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p231/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p231/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p231/r2.claim: They know their idols did not raise heaven, spread earth beneath them, or provide sustenance; this knowledge makes the proof decisive because they knowingly pursue what is false.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p231/r2.anchor: لأن هذا العلم الذي وصفهم به في هذه الآية لا يزيل عنهم الجهل؛ لأنه أراد: وأنتم تعلمون أن الأنداد التي تعبدونها

QASHANI:2:21-22/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:21-22/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:21-22/r5.claim: The listed acts establish that only their maker deserves worship; knowingly attributing an act to another makes that other seem a rival worthy of worship.
QASHANI:2:21-22/r5.anchor: هو الذي فعل هذه الأفعال، فلا تحق العبادة إلا له، ولا تنبغي أن تجعل لغيره

QASHANI:2:21-22/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:21-22/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:21-22/r6.claim: Worshippers worship the maker, whose manifestation appears in created form; each knows God only to the extent of the divinity found within, and these people found only the voluntary agent.
QASHANI:2:21-22/r6.anchor: وربهم هو المتجلي في صورة الصنع، إذ كل عابد لا يعبد إلا ما يعرفه

QASHANI:2:21-22/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:21-22/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:21-22/r7.claim: In the inward analogy, souls are earth, spirits are sky, knowledge of unity of acts is rain, and surrender, obedience, good works, and virtues are the resulting growth that yields certainties, states, and stations such as patience, gratitude, and reliance.
QASHANI:2:21-22/r7.anchor: مهد لهم أراضي نفوسهم، وبنى عليها سموات أرواحهم، وأنزل من تلك السموات ماء علم توحيد الأفعال

QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r1.claim: Islam requires both testimonies: unity alone hides differentiation and becomes determinism leading to heresy and antinomianism, while attributing acts only to the Messenger hides unity and becomes dualism; Islam joins both and regards the Messenger as the manifestation of divine acts.
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r1.anchor: بين قولنا: لا إله إلا الله، وبين قولنا: محمد رسول الله، واعتقاد مظهريته

QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r2.claim: Created acts relate to divine acts as body to spirit: spirit is their source but acts through the body, just as God originates acts that appear through creatures.
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r2.anchor: فكما أن مصدر الفعل هو الروح ولا يتم إلا بالجسد، فكذلك مبدئ الفعل هو الحق

QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r3.claim: A messenger is necessary because veiled, distant creatures cannot receive divine knowledge directly; a mediator combines a spirit witnessing the divine presence with a human nature among people, receives divine words, and conveys them to people who accept him through shared nature.
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r3.anchor: فيجب وجود واسطة يجانس بروحه الشاهدة للحق الحضرة الإلهية، وبنفسه المخالطة للخلق الرتبة البشرية

QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r4.claim: The Messenger receives the divine words in his heart and conveys them through his purified self to humankind.
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r4.anchor: ليتلقى قلبه من روحه الكلمات الربانية، ويلقي إلى نفسه القدسية، ويقبل منه الخلق

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:22-23/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:22-23/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:22-23/r1.claim: God made earth a spread-out resting place, not rough and too coarse for settling.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:22-23/r1.anchor: { الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا } بساطا، لم يجعلها حزنة غليظة لا يمكن الاستقرار عليها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:22-23/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:22-23/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:22-23/r2.anchor: { والسماء بناء } سقفا { وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرج به من الثمرات }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:22-23/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:22-23/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:22-23/r3.claim: Rain produces fruits, meaning all useful produce that trees bring out of the earth.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:22-23/r3.anchor: { وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرج به من الثمرات } يعني: حمل الأشجار جميع ما ينتفع به مما يخرج من الأرض

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:22-23/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:22-23/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:22-23/r4.claim: The equals are worshipped idols; they know these do not create while God is the Creator, an argument for divine oneness.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:22-23/r4.anchor: { فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا }: أمثالا من الأصنام التي تعبدونها { وأنتم تعلمون } أنهم لا يخلقون، والله هو الخالق

ELMALILI:2:21/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:21/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:21/r13.claim: God made the earth a bed: He created and raised people there and provided the conditions for their comfort, rest, waking, and everyday life.
ELMALILI:2:21/r13.anchor: şu altınızdaki arzı size bir döşek yapmış, sizi orada yaratmış, yetiştirmiş, üzerinde her türlü rahatınız esbâbını temin etmiş

ELMALILI:2:21/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:21/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:21/r14.claim: If the earth were taken from beneath people, even their elaborate beds and palaces would be useless; rich and poor share the same earthly bed and dwelling.
ELMALILI:2:21/r14.anchor: o altınızdan alınıvermiş olsa nerede karar ederdiniz? Kâşânelere yığdığınız kaba döşekler neye yarardı?

ELMALILI:2:21/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:21/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:21/r15.claim: God made the decorated vault of heaven a vast, magnificent building containing the earthly bed, so all people live in one house and lie on one bed under the same Lord.
ELMALILI:2:21/r15.anchor: başınız üstündeki müzeyyen gök kubbeyi de bu döşeği ihtivâ eden büyük muhteşem bir bina yapmış.

ELMALILI:2:21/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:21/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:21/r16.claim: The wording presents heaven as encompassing earth, with earth like a bed inside a building; 21:32's description of heaven as a protected roof is another aspect, not a reason to read this building as merely a roof.
ELMALILI:2:21/r16.anchor: buyurulmuş olması burada binanın sakf ile tefsîrini îcab etmez

ELMALILI:2:22/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r1.claim: The explicit مِنَ ٱلسَّمَاءِ rather than the pronoun مِنْهُ signals that the intended heaven is not the previously mentioned one.
ELMALILI:2:22/r1.anchor: Burada zamir ile مِنْهُ demek lâzım gelirken zâhir olarak مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ buyurulması, bundan murad evvelki semâ olmadığına işarettir.

ELMALILI:2:22/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r2.claim: Anything above something is its samāʾ; even the ceiling of a house can be called samāʾ, so this refers to water descending from above, from clouds in the sky's direction.
ELMALILI:2:22/r2.anchor: Zira herhangi bir şeyin fevkinde olan şey altındakinin semâsıdır. Hatta evin tavanına bile “semâ” denilir.

ELMALILI:2:22/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r3.claim: God sends water from clouds and, through it, brings people sustenance from fruits and crops.
ELMALILI:2:22/r3.anchor: de bu su sebebiyle size türlü meyvelerden, mahsullerden rızık çıkarmaktadır

ELMALILI:2:22/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r4.claim: People drink this water and receive their share of the fruits, grains, and other produce it enables to grow while they live on earth under heaven.
ELMALILI:2:22/r4.anchor: bu sudan içer ve bu sayede yetişen meyvelerden, hubûbât ve sâir fevâkihten kısmetlenirsiniz.

ELMALILI:2:22/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r5.claim: These familiar signs are already known to people and require no further reading or deep philosophy; they show what a merciful Lord their Lord is.
ELMALILI:2:22/r5.anchor: Siz bu saydıklarımızı hep bilirsiniz, bunları bilmek için başkaca okumaya veya derin felsefeler yapmaya hiç de lüzum yoktur.

ELMALILI:2:22/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r6.claim: Since people know these signs and know that none besides the Creator can be God, they must not invent equals or partners for the one true object of worship, but worship the unpartnered Creator and Lord.
ELMALILI:2:22/r6.anchor: siz bunları ve hâlıktan başka Allah olamayacağını

ELMALILI:2:22/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r7.claim: Andād is the plural of nidd and has the same meaning as mithl and amthāl: a likeness or equal.
ELMALILI:2:22/r7.anchor: “Endâd”, “nidd”in cem‘idir. “Misil” ve “emsâl” gibi ki mânaları birdir.

ELMALILI:2:22/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r8.claim: The use of jaʿl shows that any likeness attributed to God is fabricated, not true, and therefore false.
ELMALILI:2:22/r8.anchor: جعل (ca‘l) tâbiri gösteriyor ki Allah’a hangi şeyden olursa olsun misil tasavvur olunursa uydurma olur, hak olmaz bâtıl olur.

ELMALILI:2:22/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r9.claim: Knowingly setting up partners means one cannot be among the protected muttaqīn and instead becomes a stubborn unbeliever.
ELMALILI:2:22/r9.anchor: Allah’a hangi şeyden olursa olsun misil tasavvur olunursa uydurma olur, hak olmaz bâtıl olur.

ELMALILI:2:22/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r10.claim: After the universal call to worship and divine oneness, Elmalılı anticipates the objection that God's command, the messenger's prophethood, and the Qur'an's divine origin are doubtful or unknown.
ELMALILI:2:22/r10.anchor: Buna karşı birtakım insanlar: “Evet Allah belli amma bize böyle emrettiği ve peygamber gönderdiği ve Muhammedü’l-Emîn’in peygamber ve Kur’ân’ın kelâmullah olduğu ne mâlum?

ELMALILI:2:22/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r11.claim: To answer doubters, God follows the call to oneness with a public challenge, presenting the Qur'an as an everlasting divine proof and miracle establishing the Messenger's prophethood.
ELMALILI:2:22/r11.anchor: umûmî olan bu da‘vet-i tevhîd ve ubûdiyeti müte‘âkib Resûlünün nübüvvetini ve ona bahşettiği Kur’ân’ın burhân-ı ilâhî olan لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ bir mu‘cize-i ebediye olduğunu

ELMALILI:2:22/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r12.claim: Material, time-bound miracles have limited force beyond their time and setting and later hearers can dismiss them; people chiefly benefit from religion by following enduring, rational laws and knowledge.
ELMALILI:2:22/r12.anchor: maddî ve zamânî olan mucizelerin kuvveti ve fâidesi umûmî değildir. Onun kuvveti bulunduğu zamana ve muhîte münhasır kalır

ELMALILI:2:22/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r13.claim: Miracles are special divine aid in moments of distress, while guidance aims to deliver people from distress; therefore the most important miracle is eternal and of rational, scientific value: the Qur'an.
ELMALILI:2:22/r13.anchor: Hidâyetten gaye ise ıztırardan tahlîstir. Binâen‘aleyh mucizenin en mühimi ebedî, aklî ve ilmî kıymeti hâiz olan mucizedir.

ELMALILI:2:22/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r14.claim: God assured His Messenger that no person, or all people together, can imitate the Qur'an; even the greatest writers, sages, and poets fail, and challengers have repeatedly been defeated.
ELMALILI:2:22/r14.anchor: Kur’ân’ı hiçbir insan, hatta bütün insanlar tanzir edemezler. Bu bizzat va‘d ü ta‘ahhüd-i ilâhî tahtındadır.

ELMALILI:2:22/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r15.claim: Elmalılı says challengers are defeated either because God immediately binds their capacity or because He never gave it; centuries of history confirm the Qur'an's challenge.
ELMALILI:2:22/r15.anchor: Kur’an ile tehaddîye kalkıştıkları zaman mağlub olagelmişler, hiçbir şey yapamamışlardır.

ELMALILI:2:22/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r16.claim: Elmalılı recounts Napoleon claiming to love Muhammad as a great commander but to surpass him; Napoleon's pride began to collapse at Acre and faded, while France could not heal the wounds he opened.
ELMALILI:2:22/r16.anchor: “Ben Muhammed’i severim, o da benim gibi büyük bir kumandan idi fakat ben daha büyüğüm” demişti. Bu gururu, bu tehaddîye kıyâmı nihâyet Akka kalesinden

ELMALILI:2:22/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:22/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:22/r17.claim: Elmalılı concludes that the Qur'an's challenge is the eternal law and proof of both the Qur'an and Muhammad's prophethood, offered in response to human doubt.
ELMALILI:2:22/r17.anchor: Hâsılı sırr-ı tehaddî Kur’ân’ın ve nübüvvet-i Muhammediyenin ebedî bir kanunu ve burhânıdır.

QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r4.claim: God reminds people of His gifts: a raised sky as roof, a spread earth as bed, and plants brought forth by rain as collected provision.
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r4.anchor: تعرف إليهم بذكر ما من به عليهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r5.claim: God frees people from dependence on their peers by supplying necessities: the sky shelters them, the earth beds them, lawful things provide, obedience is their trade, worship their occupation, remembrance their companion, and God their trustee.

QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r6.claim: Do not attach the heart to creatures for needs: God alone originates creation, and imagining a creature independently causing benefit, harm, good, or evil is shirk.
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r6.anchor: فإن الحق سبحانه وتعالى متوحد بالإبداع

QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r7.claim: A needy person cannot properly be asked to meet another’s need; reliance by the needy on the needy, or the weak on the weak, deepens poverty and does not remove distress.
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r7.anchor: أن من له حاجة في نفسه لا يصلح

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r1.claim: God did not leave people after creating them: he supplied material and spiritual needs through a cosmic order, continually sustaining and overseeing it as a manifestation of his name al-Qayyum.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r1.anchor: Allah Teâlâ kullarını yaratıp kendi hallerine bırakmamış; onların yaratılış amaçlarına doğru ilerleyebilmeleri için maddî ve mânevî ihtiyaçlarını karşılamış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r2.claim: The earth is made suitable for human habitation, rest, peace, and production.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r2.anchor: Yeryüzünü insanların burada oturmalarına, istirahat etmelerine, huzur bulmalarına ve üretim yapmalarına uygun kılmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r3.claim: Sama encompasses, from any point on earth, the visible and invisible expanses above and some of the created beings there; see the commentary on 2:29.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r3.anchor: Yerkürenin her noktasından yukarıya doğru bakıldığında görülen ve görülemeyen bütün uzaklıkların ve yaratılmış varlıkların bir kısmı “sema”dır (bk. 29. âyetin tefsiri).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r4.claim: The universe has a finely balanced, wise, and robust structure that preserves equilibrium and protects people on earth from harm caused by celestial bodies and events in the sky.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r4.anchor: Uzayda sağlam, ince, dengeli ve hikmetli bir düzen ve yapı oluşturulmuştur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r5.claim: Properly used human capacities for knowledge and further discovery can readily lead to recognizing the creator's existence and oneness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r5.anchor: İnsanlara verilen bilgi edinme ve bilgiden yeni bilgilere ulaşma kabiliyeti doğru kullanıldığı takdirde yaratıcı Allah’ın varlık ve birliğine kolayca ulaşmak mümkündür.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r6.claim: Despite that potential knowledge, associating partners with God, worshipping or obeying other beings, or believing everything arose by itself or chance is knowing shirk and denial because it contradicts human nature and innate potential knowledge.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:22/r6.anchor: bu inanç ve anlayış (inkâr ve şirk) insanın fıtrat ve tabiatına (potansiyel bilgisine) ters düşmektedir

BURHAN:v3p100/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p100/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p100/r6.claim: God reports the purposes and benefits built into creation and command, including the earth as a resting place, houses as shelter, and spouses for comfort.
BURHAN:v3p100/r6.anchor: إخباره عن الحكم والغايات التني جعلها في خلقه وأمره

BURHAN:v3p456/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p456/r6.speaker: أبو علي
BURHAN:v3p456/r6.claim: Abu Ali says “building” denotes a raised structure, so it is paired antithetically with the earth as a bed.
BURHAN:v3p456/r6.anchor: قال أبو علي في الحجة لما كان البناء رفعا للمبنى قوبل بالفراش

BURHAN:v4p130/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p130/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p130/r2.claim: A fourth sense of jaʿala is to transform something from one state into another; it takes two objects, as in physical transformations.
BURHAN:v4p130/r2.anchor: الرابع بمعنى النقل من حال إلى حال والتصيير فيتعدى إلى مفعولين اما حسا

BURHAN:v3p164/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p164/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p164/r9.claim: Objects are often omitted at verse endings, including “while you know” and “while you recite the Book”; omission asserts the verb for its subject without restricting its object.
BURHAN:v3p164/r9.anchor: وكثيرا ما يعترى الحذف في رءوس الآى نحو

BURHAN:v4p132/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p132/r3.speaker: منهم
BURHAN:v4p132/r3.claim: Some take “make rivals for God” to mean naming idols as rivals, while also implying belief, since the unbelievers would not name them so without believing it.

BURHAN:v4p436/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p436/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p436/r5.claim: Resumptive coordination and circumstantial waw occur together, as in “while you know,” “while you recite the Book,” and the other cited clauses.
BURHAN:v4p436/r5.anchor: وقد يجتمعان نحو ﴿ فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا وأنتم تعلمون ﴾

SULAMI:v1p52#6/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p52#6/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p52#6/r1.claim: The verse teaches the path of spiritual poverty: earth is a place to tread, sky a covering, water wholesome, and plants food; do not worship creatures for worldly needs, since God provides necessities without making you indebted to anyone.
SULAMI:v1p52#6/r1.anchor: أعلمكم في هذه الآية سبيل الفقر بأن يجعل الأرض وطئا والسماء غطاء والماء طيبا

ITQAN:v2p469/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p469/r1.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v2p469/r1.claim: Al-Raghib says ja‘ala is broader than fa‘ala and sana‘a: it can mean become, create, form one thing from another, make something take a state, or judge something to be so; 2:22 uses the state-making sense.
ITQAN:v2p469/r1.anchor: قال الراغب لفظ عام في الأفعال كلها وهو أعم من فعل وصنع وسائر أخواتها ويتصرف على خمسة أوجه

ITQAN:v3p202/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p202/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p202/r1.claim: Qur’anic causal explanation makes rulings easier to accept and more compelling; it is often an implicit answer to a question raised by the preceding clause, and may state creation’s purpose.
ITQAN:v3p202/r1.anchor: وفائدته التقرير والأبلغية فإن النفوس أبعث على قبول الأحكام المعللة من غيرها وغالب التعليل في القرآن على تقدير جواب سؤال

ITQAN:v3p255/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p255/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p255/r1.claim: Antithesis (tibaq) joins opposites and may be literal or figurative, verbal or semantic, and positive or negative; the segment also defines hidden antithesis and counterpoint.
ITQAN:v3p255/r1.anchor: وتسمى الطباق الجمع بين متضادين في الجملة وهو قسمان حقيقي ومجازي والثاني يسمى التكافؤ وكل منهما إما لفظي أو معنوي

ITQAN:v3p255/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p255/r2.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
ITQAN:v3p255/r2.claim: Abu ‘Ali al-Farisi treats ‘earth as a bed, heaven as a structure’ as semantic antithesis: a raised structure contrasts with a spread bed.
ITQAN:v3p255/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي لما كان البناء رفعا للمبني قوبل بالفراش الذي هو على خلاف البناء

ITQAN:v3p255/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p255/r6.speaker: ابن أبي الإصبع
ITQAN:v3p255/r6.claim: Ibn Abi al-Isba‘ defines counterpoint as naming two or more terms and then their opposites in the same order.
ITQAN:v3p255/r6.anchor: قال ابن أبي الإصبع والفرق بين الطباق والمقابلة من وجهين

ITQAN:v1p225/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p225/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p225/r6.claim: A breath stop may be licensed in a long passage even when the following clause depends on what precedes; resuming is unnecessary if that clause is independently understandable.
ITQAN:v1p225/r6.anchor: والمرخص ضرورة ما لا يستغني ما بعده عما قبله لكنه يرخص لانقطاع النفس وطول الكلام

ITQAN:v1p229#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p229#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p229#3/r1.claim: In long passages, stories, parenthetical clauses, and recitations combining readings, pauses may be licensed where they would otherwise be disallowed; al-Sajawandi calls this necessity-licensed stopping.
ITQAN:v1p229#3/r1.anchor: يغتفر في طول الفواصل والقصص والجمل المعترضة ونحو ذلك

TUSTARI:2:22/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:22/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:22/r1.claim: Sahl glosses the word for rivals as opposites.

TUSTARI:2:22/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:22/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:22/r2.claim: The greatest rival to God is the commanding soul, which pursues its desires and hopes without God's guidance.
TUSTARI:2:22/r2.anchor: فأكبر الأضداد النفس الأمارة بالسوء المتطلعة إلى حظوظها ومناها بغير هدى من الله

DAMGHANI:v1p69/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p69/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p69/r1.claim: Basṭ can mean a bed or spread-out surface; Noah's verse describes the earth as bedding or a resting place.
DAMGHANI:v1p69/r1.anchor: الرابع : البسط يعني به المهد والفرش كقوله تعالى في سورة نوح

DAMGHANI:v1p69/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p69/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p69/r11.claim: The entry also lists two senses of baṭsh: punishment and strength.
DAMGHANI:v1p69/r11.anchor: ب ط ش على وجهين العقوبة . القوة

DAMGHANI:v1p353/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p353/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p353/r5.claim: Firāsh means a rug or bedding; the earth is described as a spread-out surface.
DAMGHANI:v1p353/r5.anchor: هو الذي جعل لكم الارض فراشا يعني بساطا ونحوه

AKHFASH:v1p56/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p56/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p56/r3.claim: The initial alif is hamzat qaṭʿ because it remains in the diminutive form anīdād; the singular of andād is nidd, meaning an equal or counterpart.
AKHFASH:v1p56/r3.anchor: فقطع الالف لانه اسم تثبت الالف فيه في التصغير

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43/r1.claim: Andād are partners or equals; Arabic calls one thing the nad or nadīd of another.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43/r1.anchor: أندادا} أي: شركاء أمثالا. يقال: هذا ند هذا ونديده (2) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43/r2.claim: He explains knowing here as understanding or reasoning.

NAHHAS:v1p197/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r13.claim: Alladhī may modify rabbikum directly or modify alladhī khalaqakum; an adjective can qualify another adjective because they share the same referent.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r13.anchor: الذي نعت لربكم وإن شئت كان نعتا للذي خلقكم وصلح أن يقال نعت للنعت

NAHHAS:v1p197/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r14.claim: Other parses make alladhī accusative with tattaqūn, an explicative “I mean,” or the predicate of an omitted subject.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r14.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون منصوبا بتتقون ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى أعني وأن يكون في موضع رفع

NAHHAS:v1p197/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r15.claim: Assimilation in lakum is possible because the consonants are alike and intervening vowels are numerous, but keeping them distinct is better because they are separate words.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r15.anchor: ويجوز جعل لكم مدغما لأن الحرفين مثلان قد كثرت الحركات وترك الإدغام أجود لأنها من كلمتين

NAHHAS:v1p197/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r16.claim: The earth and the sky are the two objects of jaʿala.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r16.anchor: مفعولان لجعل ( والسماء بناء ) عطف والسماء تكون جمعا

NAHHAS:v1p197/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r17.claim: Samāʾ can be a collective plural of samāwa or samāʾa, or a feminine singular; its masculine usage is irregular, and several plural forms are attested.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r17.anchor: والسماء تكون جمعا لسماوة وسماءة وتكون واحدة مؤنثة مثل عناق وتذكيرها شاذ

NAHHAS:v1p197/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r18.claim: When samāʾ means rain or a roof, it is masculine in ordinary usage; its plurals include asmiyah and sumiyy.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r18.anchor: وسماء المطر مذكر وكذلك السقف في المستعمل وجمعها أسمية وسمي وسمي

NAHHAS:v1p197/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r19.claim: Bināʾ may be shortened and can denote a plural of binya or a verbal noun; bunā is also given as a plural of binya.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r19.anchor: وبناء يقصر على أنه جمع بنية ومصدر ويقال بني جمع بنية

NAHHAS:v1p197/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r20.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r20.claim: At pause, the long form has five pronunciations: the preferred one keeps hamza between two alifs; it may be lightened or deleted, with the following alif then removed, or a length added or yā substituted.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r20.anchor: خمس لغات أجودها و السماء بناء بهمزة بين ألفين ويجوز تخفيف الهمزة

NAHHAS:v1p197/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r21.speaker: البصريون
NAHHAS:v1p197/r21.claim: The Basrans compare the yā-substitution form banāyā to khaṭāyā.

NAHHAS:v1p197/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r22.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v1p197/r22.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the hamza returns to its original yāʾ because that is the word’s underlying form.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r22.anchor: والفراء يقول ردت الهمزة إلى أصلها لأن أصلها الياء

NAHHAS:v1p197/r23.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r23.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r23.claim: Māʾ derives from mawh: the moving wāw becomes alif, then hāʾ is replaced by hamza because it is stronger and closer to alif; the final alif represents tanwīn.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r23.anchor: والأصل في ماء موه قلبت الواو ألفا لتحركها وتحرك ما قبلها فقلت ماه

NAHHAS:v1p197/r24.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r24.speaker: أبو الحسن علي
NAHHAS:v1p197/r24.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī says Basrans allow spelling the word with two alifs only, or with three.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r24.anchor: قال أبو الحسن علي لا يجوز أن يكتب إلا بألفين عند البصريين وإن شئت بثلاث

NAHHAS:v1p197/r25.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r25.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r25.claim: In plural and diminutive forms, the word returns to its base: muwayh, amwāh, and miyāh, analogous to ajmāl and jimāl.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r25.anchor: فإذا جمعوا أو صغروا ردوا إلى الأصل فقالوا مويه وأمواه ومياه مثل أجمال وجمال

NAHHAS:v1p197/r26.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r26.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r26.claim: Thamarāt is the plural of thamra; thamar also occurs with plural patterns like shajar, khashab, badan, and thimār like ākām.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r26.anchor: جمع ثمرة ويقال ثمر مثل شجر ويقال ثمر مثل خشب ويقال ثمر مثل بدن

NAHHAS:v1p197/r27.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r27.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r27.anchor: مفعول ( فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا ) تجعلوا جزم بالنهي

NAHHAS:v1p197/r28.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r28.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r28.claim: The prohibition makes tajʿalū jussive with its nūn deleted; andādan is the first object and li-llāh the second.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r28.anchor: تجعلوا جزم بالنهي فلذلك حذفت منه النون أندادا مفعول أول

NAHHAS:v1p197/r29.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r29.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r29.claim: Antum is a subject and taʿlamūn its predicate; the clause is circumstantial.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r29.anchor: مبتدأ ( تعلمون ) فعل مستقبل في موضع الخبر والجملة في موضع الحال

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r1.claim: Of five accusative analyses for الذي, al-Samīn regards نصب على القطع as clearest.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r1.anchor: النصب من خمسة أوجه، أظهرها: أن يكون نصبه على القطع

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r2.claim: Another accusative analysis makes الذي an adjective of ربكم.

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r3.claim: Another accusative analysis makes الذي a بدل of ربكم.

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqāʾ begins with parsing الذي as the object of تتقون.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r4.anchor: الرابع: أنه مفعول " تتقون " وبه بدأ أبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r5.claim: A fifth analysis makes the relative adjective modify an adjective; normally adjectives do not themselves take adjectives unless an obstacle requires it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r5.anchor: الخامس: أنه نعت النعت أي: الموصول الأول، لكن المختار أن النعت لا ينعت

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r6.claim: An exception is made when something blocks the normal analysis; ذو الجمة in يا أيها الفارس ذو الجمة modifies الفارس.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r6.anchor: إلا أن يمنع مانع فيكون نعتا للنعت نحو قولهم: " يا أيها الفارس ذو الجمة "

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r7.claim: For رفع, the sounder analysis supplies a deleted subject: هو الذي جعل.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r7.anchor: أحدهما وهو الأصح أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي: هو الذي جعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r8.claim: Another رفع analysis makes الذي the subject and فلا تجعلوا its predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r8.anchor: والثاني أنه مبتدأ وخبره قوله بعد ذلك: " فلا تجعلوا "

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r9.claim: Al-Samīn objects that its relative clause is past, unlike a conditional clause licensing فاء, and that the analysis lacks a linker.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r9.anchor: أن صلته ماضية فلم يشبه الشرط فلا تزاد في خبره الفاء، الثاني: عدم الرابط

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r10.claim: The missing link can be supplied only by al-Akhfash's view that a repeated apparent name with the same referent links a clause, as in Zayd/AʿAbd Allāh.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r10.anchor: إلا أن يقال بمذهب الأخفش وهو أن يجعل الربط مكرر الاسم الظاهر إذا كان بمعناه

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r11.claim: If جعل means make or render, it governs two objects: الأرض first and فراشا second.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r11.anchor: أن تكون بمعنى صير فتتعدى لمفعولين فيكون " الأرض " مفعولا أول، و " فراشا " مفعولا ثانيا

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r12.claim: If جعل means create, it governs الأرض alone and فراشا is a circumstantial accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r12.anchor: الثاني: أن تكون بمعنى " خلق " فتتعدى لواحد وهو " الأرض " ويكون " فراشا " حالا

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r13.claim: السماء بناء coordinates with الأرض فراشا under either analysis of جعل.

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r14.claim: لكم attaches to جعل and means the making is for your benefit.

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r15.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r15.claim: فراش means something spread out to be trodden or sat upon.

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r16.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r16.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r16.claim: بناء is the verbal noun of بنيت; its final yāʾ becomes hamza after an extra alif, and it can also mean the built thing.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r16.anchor: والبناء مصدر بنيت، وإنما قلبت الياء همزة لتطرفها بعد ألف زائدة

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r17.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r17.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r17.claim: أنزل coordinates with جعل; من السماء attaches to it and marks the point of origin.

SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r18.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r18.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r18.claim: Alternatively من السماء attaches to an omitted element as a circumstantial phrase from ماء; a fronted modifier of an indefinite is construed as حال and partitive, with مياه omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22/r18.anchor: على أن يكون حالا من " ما " لأن صفة النكرة إذا قدمت عليها نصبت حالا

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r1.claim: ماء derives from موه, supported by ماهت الركية تموه; its plurals are مياه and أمواه.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r1.anchor: وأصل ماء موه بدليل قولهم: " ماهت الركية تموه " وفي جمعه: مياه وأمواه

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r2.claim: The diminutive مويه changes as its yāʾ is vocalized and the preceding vowel opens, and the weak ending is resolved by replacing هاء with hamza for strength.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r2.anchor: وفي تصغيره: مويه، فتحركت الياء وانفتح ما قبلها فقلبت ألفا

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r3.claim: فأخرج coordinates sequentially with أنزل; به attaches to it and باء marks causation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r3.anchor: وقوله: " فأخرج " عطف على " أنزل " مرتب عليه، و " به " متعلق به، والباء فيه للسببية

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r4.claim: من الثمرات attaches to أخرج and من is partitive.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r4.anchor: و " من الثمرات " متعلق به أيضا، ومن هنا للتبعيض

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r5.claim: Taking من as extra is unlikely: it would be extra in an affirmative before a definite, rejected by Basrans and Kufans except al-Akhfash, and wrongly imply all fruits are sustenance.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r5.anchor: وأبعد من جعلها زائدة لوجهين، أحدهما: زيادتها في الواجب

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes من الثمرات as بيان of جنس; al-Samīn objects that no earlier item is clarified and supposes he means بيان for رزقا semantically.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r6.anchor: وجعلها الزمخشري لبيان الجنس، وفيه نظر، إذ لم يتقدم ما يبين هذا

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r7.claim: The apparent parsing makes رزقا the direct object of أخرج.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r7.anchor: و " رزقا " ظاهره أنه مفعول به، ناصبه " أخرج "

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, من الثمرات is the object, meaning some water brings out some fruits; رزقا may then be حال meaning المرزوق.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r8.anchor: والتقدير: فأخرج ببعض الماء بعض الثمرات

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r9.claim: Under that alternative, رزقا may instead be a purpose verbal noun; the conditions for its accusative use are met.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r9.anchor: أن يكون مصدرا منصوبا على المفعول من أجله، وفيه شروط النصب موجودة

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r10.claim: Both ماء and رزقا are indefinite to convey partiality: some water yields some fruits as some of people's provision, since fruits are not all their sustenance.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r10.anchor: وإنما نكر " ماء " و " رزقا " ليفيد التبعيض

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r11.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r11.claim: Abu al-Baqāʾ allows من الثمرات as a circumstantial phrase modifying رزقا, since it would be an adjective if placed after it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r11.anchor: وأجاز أبو البقاء أن يكون " من الثمرات " حالا من " رزقا "

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says الثمرات stands for الثمر or الثمار, a small plural used for a large plural, as in جنات and قروء.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r12.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري " من الثمرات " واقعا موقع الثمر أو الثمار

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r13.claim: No substitution is needed: definite sound plurals with generic أل can denote abundance; the criticism of Ḥassān ibn Thābit's الجفنات and أسياف is mistaken.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#2/r13.anchor: ولا حاجة تدعو إلى هذا لأن جمع السلامة المحلى بأل التي للعموم يقع للكثرة

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r1.claim: Ḥassān ibn Thābit's poem uses الجفنات and أسياف; critics say he should have used the more laudatory large plurals الجفان and سيوف, but al-Samīn rejects that criticism because definite plurals can express abundance.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r1.anchor: كان ينبغي أن يقول: الجفان: وسيوفنا

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r2.claim: لكم may attach to أخرج or modify رزقا if it means the thing provided; with رزقا as verbal noun, the pronoun is its object and the lām reinforces it, as in تأديبا له.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r2.anchor: و " لكم " يحتمل التعلق ب " أخرج " ، ويحتمل التعلق بمحذوف

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r3.claim: The فاء gives the prohibition a causal relation to the manifest signs just described.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r3.anchor: الفاء للتسبب، تسبب عن إيجاد هذه الآيات الباهرة النهي عن اتخاذكم الأنداد

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r4.claim: لا is prohibitive and تجعلوا is jussive, marked by deletion of its nūn.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r4.anchor: و " لا " ناهية و " تجعلوا " مجزوم بها، علامة جزمه حذف النون

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r5.claim: Here تجعلوا means make or turn into.

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r6.claim: Abu al-Baqāʾ allows تجعلوا to mean name or call.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r6.anchor: وأجاز أبو البقاء أن تكون بمعنى تسموا

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r7.claim: On either meaning of تجعلوا it takes two objects: أندادا is first, and the preceding prepositional phrase is second and must precede it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r7.anchor: وعلى القولين فيتعدى لاثنين أولهما: أندادا، وثانيهما: الجار والمجرور قبله

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqāʾ calls أندادا a plural of ند and نديد; al-Samīn doubts نديد because أفعال is unattested for فعيل meaning فاعل.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r8.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " أندادا جمع ند ونديد " وفي جعله جمع نديد نظر

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r9.claim: ند means a comparable rival, whether like, opposite, or different.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r9.anchor: والند: المقاوم المضاهي، سواء كان [مثلا] أو ضدا أو خلافا

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r10.claim: Abū ʿUbayda defines ند as an opposite.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r10.anchor: وقيل: هو/ الضد عن أبي عبيدة

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r11.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r11.claim: Ḥassān ibn Thābit's لست له بند uses ند for a match or equal.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r11.anchor: قال حسان: 266 أتهجوه ولست له بند

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says ند means counterpart used only for a contrary counterpart; Jarīr's line witnesses rival, and ناددت means opposed or competed with, from ندود, fleeing.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r12.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " الند المثل، ولا يقال إلا للند المخالف، قال جرير

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r13.speaker: لبيد
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r13.claim: Labīd uses نديدتي as an intensive form meaning my rival or equal.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r13.anchor: ويقال " نديدة " على المبالغة، قال لبيد: 269 لكيلا يكون السندري نديدتي

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r14.claim: ند with fatḥa also means a raised mound or perfume; the latter usage is non-Arabic.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r14.anchor: وأما الند بفتح النون فهو التل المرتفع، والند الطيب أيضا، ليس بعربي

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r15.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r15.claim: The prohibition links semantically to اعبدوا because worship fundamentally entails monotheism.

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r16.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r16.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r16.claim: If الذي is predicate of an omitted subject, the prohibition can attach to it: the signs testify to oneness, so no rivals should be assigned to God.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r16.anchor: ويجوز أن يتعلق ب " الذي " إذا جعلته خبر مبتدأ محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r17.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r17.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r17.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī links فلا تجعلوا to لعلكم, treating it like a منصوب verb after implicit أن in فأطلع; creation is to make people fear punishment and not liken God to creation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r17.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " يتعلق ب " لعلكم " على أن ينتصب " تجعلوا " انتصاب

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r18.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r18.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r18.claim: Al-Samīn notes Basran grammarians do not permit al-Zamakhsharī's analysis of a منصوب verb after لعلكم.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#3/r18.anchor: وهذا لا يجيزه البصريون، وسيأتي تأويل " فأطلع " ونظائره

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#4/r1.claim: وأنتم تعلمون is a nominal clause functioning as حال; its object is omitted either because it means you are knowledgeable or because بطلان ذلك is understood.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#4/r1.anchor: ومفعول العلم متروك لأن المعنى: وأنتم من أهل العلم

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#4/r2.claim: One analysis treats أن as pronoun and ت as address marker; another treats ت as pronoun and أن as a support element.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#4/r2.anchor: قيل: أن، والتاء حرف خطاب يتغير بحسب المخاطب. وقيل: بل التاء هي الاسم

SAMIN-DURR:2:22#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#4/r3.claim: A third analysis treats all of أنتم as a separate nominative pronoun; its mīm follows the same vowel and pause patterns as هم.
SAMIN-DURR:2:22#4/r3.anchor: بل هو ضمير برمته وهو ضمير رفع منفصل، وحكم ميمه بالنسبة إلى السكون والحركة

ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r1.claim: The earth as firāsh is a spread-out resting place, neither rugged nor so hard and thick that settling on it is impossible.
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r1.anchor: معناه وطاء، لم يجعلها حزنة غليظة لا يمكن الاستقرار عليها

ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r2.claim: Bināʾ names anything raised above the earth; here it means God made the sky a roof.

ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r3.claim: Both assimilation and clear pronunciation are possible in jaʿala lakum; most readers use clear pronunciation because the words are separate.
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r3.anchor: ويجوز في قوله: (جعل لكم الأرض) وجهان: الإدغام والإظهار، تقول: جعل لكم

ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r4.claim: Andād means counterparts or equals; God argues that people who know idols do not create must not make them God's peers.
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r4.anchor: لا تجعلوا لله أمثالا وأنتم تعلمون أنهم لا يخلقون والله الخالق

ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r5.claim: The Arab lexemes nidd and nadīd mean a peer; Jarīr's verse supplies evidence for nidd.
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r5.anchor: قال جرير: أتيما تجعلون إلي ندا

ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r6.claim: This verse and the one before it establish God's oneness; the following challenge to produce a sūra establishes the Prophet's truth, and rayb means doubt.
ZAJJAJ:v1p99/r6.anchor: فهذه الآية والتي قبلها احتجاج عليهم في تثبيت توحيد الله عز وجل. ثم احتج عليهم فيما يلي هذه الآية

ASAD-NOTES:2:21#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:21#n13/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:21#n13/r1.claim: Andād is plural of nidd, literally 'compeers'; Asad says a free rendering is needed to convey the phrase's meaning.
ASAD-NOTES:2:21#n13/r1.anchor: "do not give God any compeers" (andad, pl. of nidd )

ASAD-NOTES:2:21#n13/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:21#n13/r2.speaker: all commentators
ASAD-NOTES:2:21#n13/r2.claim: Commentators agree that the term includes worshipped objects credited with divine qualities, whether deities in their own right or saints said to possess divine or semi-divine powers.
ASAD-NOTES:2:21#n13/r2.anchor: There is full agreement among all commentators that this term implies any object of adoration

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p357/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p357/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p357/r1.claim: The transmitted gloss gives andād as likenesses and counterparts; Labīd and Ḥassān’s verses are cited as Arabic usage evidence.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p357/r1.anchor: قال: الأشباه والأمثال. وشاهده قول لبيد:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p357/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p357/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p357/r2.claim: The author connects the term with occurrences in Fuṣṣilat, al-Baqara, Ibrāhīm, al-Zumar, and Sabaʾ, all framed as rebuke or prohibition.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r1.claim: The six cited occurrences of the word all express reproach or prohibition; the author says the Qur’an has no other form from this word family.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r1.anchor: الآيات الست، على وجه النكير والنهي، وليس في القرآن غيرها من المادة.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to gloss andād as equals; other lexicons record the competing gloss “opposites.”
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r2.anchor: وحكى ابن الأنباري عن ابن عباس: أندادا أعدالا، وعن أبي عبيدة: أضدادا.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda interprets andād as opposites; al-Azharī attributes both reported interpretations to Ibn al-Sikkīt and al-Akhfash.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r3.anchor: وعن أبي عبيدة: أضدادا. وحكى الأزهري القولين عن ابن السكيت والأخفش.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r4.speaker: أبو حاتم السجستاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r4.claim: Abū Ḥātim says Arabs agree that a nidd is a thing’s like, counterpart, or equal, and that he knows of no disagreement.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r4.anchor: اجتمعت العرب على أن نِدَّ الشيء مِثْله وشِبهُه وعِدله، ولا أعلمهم اختلفوا في ذلك.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r5.speaker: النبي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r5.claim: In a report from Ibn Masʿūd, the Prophet names making rivals for God despite His creating the person as the greatest sin; Ibn Ḥajar glosses nidd as peer or counterpart.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r5.anchor: حديث عبد الله بن مسعود، قال: سألت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r6.speaker: ابن حجر
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r6.claim: Ibn Ḥajar explains andād as the plural of nidd, meaning a counterpart or peer.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r6.anchor: قال ابن حجر: جمع نِدّ، وهو النظير.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r7.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya glosses nidd as an equal; al-Ḍaḥḥāk, transmitting from Ibn ʿAbbās, gives likenesses and counterparts.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r7.anchor: وروى ابن أبي حاتم من طريق أبي العالية قال:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r8.speaker: القرطبي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r8.claim: Al-Qurṭubī glosses andād as peers and equals and cites the two poetic witnesses.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r8.anchor: وحكاه القرطبي عن ابن عباس، وغيره، وقال: أندادا: أكفاء ونظراء.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r9.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r9.claim: Al-Rāghib distinguishes nidd, similarity in essence, from the broader mithl; shibh concerns quality, musāwī quantity, and shakl measure or area.
