BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r9.anchor: أن الند يقال فيما يشارك في الجوهر، والشبه فيما يشارك في الكيفية فقط، والمساوي فيما يشارك في الكمية فقط

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r10.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r10.speaker: ابن الأثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r10.claim: Ibn al-Athīr describes a nidd as a counterpart that opposes, rivals, differs from, and distances itself from the thing.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p358/r10.anchor: الأنداد جمع ندّ، وهو مثل الشيء الذي يضادّه في أموره وينادّه، أي يخالفه وينأى عنه.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p72/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p72/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p72/r3.claim: At a pause, the lengthened reading retains an alif for tanwin; the author derives the alifs in māʾ from its root form and cites its plural amwāh.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p72/r3.anchor: فالحجة لمن مد وأثبت الألف أن الأصل في الاسم ثلاث الفات فالأصل في ماء موه فقلبت من الواو ألفا لتحركها

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p72/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p72/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p72/r4.claim: The shortened reading drops the compensatory alif at pause by analogy with nominative and genitive endings, where loss of the vowel also removes tanwin; the script has one alif.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p72/r4.anchor: والحجة لمن قصر وطرح الألف أن يقول الوقف يزيل الحركة في الرفع والخفض فاذا زالت الحركة في الرفع والخفض سقط التنوين

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p72/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p72/r5.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p72/r5.claim: The same pause alternatives apply to accusative indefinite forms such as duʿāʾ and nidāʾ: retain the alif of tanwin with lengthening, or drop it and shorten.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p72/r5.anchor: من الممدود المنصوب المنون يقرأعند الوقف عليه باثبات الألف عوضا من التنوين وبالمد على الأصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r10.claim: Firāsh is a spread or bedding one sits, sleeps, and moves upon.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r10.anchor: الفراش: الوطاء الذي يقعد عليه وينام ويتقلب عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r11.claim: Bināʾ is a verbal noun but can mean a transported dwelling such as a house, dome, tent, or canopy; Arab abniya are tents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r11.anchor: البناء: مصدر، وقد براد به المنقول من بيت أو قبة أو خباء أو طراف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r12.claim: Water is familiar; one account calls it a flowing substance that sustains animal life, and the supplied fragment cuts off during the further description.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r12.anchor: الماء: معروف، وقال بعضهم: هو جوهر سيال به قوام الحيوان ووزنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r1.claim: The morphology of ماء is related to فعل, with its alif from wāw and hamza replacing hāʾ, as مويه، مياه، أمواه indicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r1.anchor: وألفه منقلبة من واو وهمزته بدل من هاء يدل عليه: مويه، ومياه، وأمواه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r2.claim: ثمره is what a tree produces that is edible or fragrant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r2.anchor: الثمرة: ما تخرجه الشجرة من مطعوم أو مشموم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r3.claim: A ند is a resisting counterpart or peer, whether similar, opposite, or otherwise different.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r3.anchor: الند: المقاوم المضاهي مثلا كان أو ضدا أو خلافا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة والمفضل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Mufaddal define ند as an opposite; Ibn Atiyya says this restriction is illustrative, not exhaustive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة والمفضل: الند: الضد، قال ابن عطية، وهذا التخصيص تمثيل لا حصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r5.speaker: غيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r5.claim: Another authority defines ند as a hostile opposite that resists, deriving the word from flight.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r5.anchor: وقال غيره: الند: الضد المبغض المناوي من الندود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r6.speaker: المهدوي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r6.claim: Al-Mahdawi defines ند as an equal or counterpart, the position of the linguists other than Abu Ubayda.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r6.anchor: وقال المهدوي: الند: الكفؤ والمثل، هذا مذهب أهل اللغة سوى أبي عبيدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says ند means an equal, used only for a counterpart that differs from the Creator.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري: الند: المثل، ولا يقال إلا للمثل المخالف للبارىء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r8.speaker: جرير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r8.claim: Jarir's verse uses نديد for an equal counterpart, evidence for the sense of ند.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r8.anchor: قال جرير: أتيما تجعلون إلي ندا ... وما تيم لذي حسب نديد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r9.claim: Saying God has neither ند nor ضد denies both anything that can take His place and anything opposed to Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r9.anchor: ومعنى قولهم: ليس لله ند ولا ضد، نفى ما يسد مسد ونفى ما ينافيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r9.claim: The relative الذي جعل can be nominative or accusative; the nominative analyses continue in the next segment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r9.anchor: والموصول الثاني في قوله: الذي جعل يجوز رفعه ونصبه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r1.claim: An adjective may itself be modified only when it cannot agree directly with its described noun; the example is يا أيها الفارس ذو الجمة.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r1.anchor: إلا إن كان ذلك النعت لا يمكن تبعيته للمنعوت، فيكون إذ ذاك نعتا للنعت الأول، نحو قولك: يا أيها الفارس ذو الجمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r2.claim: Abu al-Hasan permits a repeated-subject construction using a person's alternate name; Abū Ḥayyān says Sibawayh disallows it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r2.anchor: ولا نعرف إجازة ذلك إلا عن أبي الحسن. أجاز أن تقول: زيد قام أبو عمرو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r3.claim: The accusative can detach as praise or describe ربكم, the referent of الذي خلقكم; he prefers adjectives to modify the same noun unless impossible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r3.anchor: والذي نختاره أن النعت لا ينعت، بل النعوت كلها راجعة إلى منعوت واحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r4.speaker: مكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r4.claim: Abu Muhammad Makki allows the accusative by supplying أعني, but Abū Ḥayyān says the prior expression is unambiguous and needs no insertion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r4.anchor: وأجاز أبو محمد مكي نصبه بإضمار أعني، وما قبله ليس بملتبس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r5.speaker: مكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls Makki's further proposal to govern الذي by تتقون a gross parsing unworthy of the Qur'an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r5.anchor: وأجاز أيضا نصبه بتتقون، وهو إعراب غث ينزه القرآن عن مثله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r6.claim: The absence of a coordinating wāw before الذي keeps this and the prior description attached to one referent; conjunction would suggest a different referent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r6.anchor: وإنما أتى بقوله الذي دون واو لتكون هذه الصفة وما قبلها راجعين إلى موصوف واحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r7.claim: جعل means “made into,” taking الأرض and فراشا as two objects, with لكم attached to جعل.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r7.anchor: وجعل: بمعنى صير، لذلك نصبت الأرض. وفراشا، ولكم متعلق بجعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r8.claim: Others parse فراشا and بناء as circumstantial accusatives, treating جعل as “created” with one object and varying the verb for eloquence, as in 6:1.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r8.anchor: وأجاز بعضهم أن ينتصب فراشا وبناء على الحال، على أن يكون جعل بمعنى خلق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r9.claim: Abu Amr assimilates the lām of جعل into the lām of لكم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r9.anchor: وأدغم أبو عمرو لام جعل في لام لكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r10.claim: The article on الأرض may designate prepared, level parts suitable as a bed, or all earth as a place for animals to settle and dwell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r10.anchor: والألف واللام في الأرض يجوز أن تكون للجنس الخاص، فيكون المراد أرضا مخصوصة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r11.claim: On the universal reading, lowlands, mountains, houses, and animal or bird shelters make earth a resting place; it is a favor to creatures or to people through animals prepared for their use.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p157/r11.anchor: والجبال والحزون مستقر لبعض الآدميين بيوتا أو حصونا ومنازل، أو لبعض الحيوانات وحشا وطيرا يفترشون منها أوكارا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r1.speaker: طلحة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r1.claim: Talha reads مهادا; the segment continues his reading from the previous segment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r1.anchor: مهادا. والفراش، والمهاد، والبساط، والقرار، والوطاء نظائر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r2.claim: Fراش, مهاد, بساط, قرار, and وطأ are near-synonyms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r2.anchor: والفراش، والمهاد، والبساط، والقرار، والوطاء نظائر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r3.speaker: بعض المنجمين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r3.claim: Some astronomers infer that earth is flat rather than spherical from its being made like a bed, and argue seas could not remain on a sphere.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r3.anchor: وقد استدل بعض المنجمين بقوله: جعل لكم الأرض فراشا على أن الأرض مبسوطة لا كرية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects the inference: the verse describes earth's use as a bed but establishes neither a flat nor spherical shape; its vast size permits that use either way.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r4.anchor: أما استدلاله بالآية فلا حجة له في ذلك، لأن الآية لا تدل على أن الأرض مسطحة ولا كرية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari argues that if people can spread bedding on a mountain, itself an earthly peg, they can do so more easily on broad earth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وإذا كان يعني الافتراش سهلا في الجبل، وهو وتد من أوتاد الأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r6.speaker: قائلون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r6.claim: The reply to the sea argument is that a sphere may have a level region for water, held by God's command rather than physical theory.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r6.anchor: قالوا: لأنه يجوز أن تكون كرية ويكون في جزء منها منسطح يصلح للاستقرار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r7.claim: A stationary sphere could hold water on part of its surface; on a rotating sphere, water would ordinarily be unable to stay fixed, an issue for astronomy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بعض الشكل الكري مقرا للماء إذا كان ذلك الشكل ثابتا غير دائر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r8.claim: The sky is compared to a built dome over earth, as a house's roof is a construction; Ibn Abbas and others report this explanation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r8.anchor: والسماء للأرض كالسقف، روي هذا عن ابن عباس وجماعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r9.claim: Calling the sky a building conveys firmness, craft, and protection, displaying divine power and wisdom: despite its vastness, it has no foundation or pillars but is held by God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r9.anchor: لكن البناء أبلغ في الإحكام وأتقن في الصنعة وأمنع لوصول الأذى إلى من تحته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r10.claim: Another explanation says the sky is called a building because its parts hold together like a building.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p158/r10.anchor: وقيل: سميت بناء لتماسكها كما يتماسك البناء بعضه ببعض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r1.claim: السماء in the rain phrase may mean clouds or familiar heaven; if clouds, the occurrences share only the sense of height, while explicit repetition suits the second reading because it begins a self-sufficient relative clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يراد به السحاب، ويجوز أن يراد به السماء المعروفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r2.claim: من may attach to أنزل as point of origin, or modify ماء as a fronted circumstantial phrase with partitive sense and an omitted noun: من مياه السماء.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r2.anchor: ومن متعلقة بأنزل وهي لابتداء الغاية، ويحتمل أن تتعلق بمحذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r3.claim: ماء is indefinite because what descended was not the totality of water.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r3.anchor: ونكر. ماء لأن المنزل لم يكن عاما فتدخل عليه الألف واللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r4.claim: به refers to water and the preposition marks causation, but only figuratively: God creates directly and makes accompanying events operate like causes by convention.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r4.anchor: والهاء في به عائدة إلى الماء، والباء معناها السببية. فالماء سبب للخروج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r5.claim: God wisely brings things through successive stages; witnessing wondrous change and gradual development increases the observer's reverence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r5.anchor: لأن في كل طور مشاهدة أمر من عجيب التنقل وغريب التدريج تزيد المتأمل تعظيما للباري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r6.claim: من is partitive, the article marks a generic category, and the plural ثمرات reflects the diversity of types; there is no need to treat it as a substitute for ثمر or ثمار.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r6.anchor: من الثمرات: من للتبعيض، والألف واللام في الثمرات لتعريف الجنس وجمع لاختلاف أنواعه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats الثمرات as a plural standing for the collective singular ثمر or plural ثمار; Abū Ḥayyān says the generic definite plural already covers the category.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r7.anchor: على ما ذهب إليه الزمخشري، لأن هذا من الجمع المحلى بالألف واللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r8.claim: He notes that grammarians refuted criticism of Hassan's use of a definite low-count plural, since the definite article makes it exhaustive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p159/r8.anchor: ولذلك رد المحققون على من نقد على حسان قوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r1.claim: من is not extra: grammarians do not otherwise allow it in affirmative constructions, and an exhaustive reading wrongly makes every fruit provision; partitive force fits the facts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r1.anchor: وأبعد من جعل من زائدة، وجعل الألف واللام للاستغراق لوجهين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r2.claim: Indefinite water, partitive fruit, and indefinite provision fit partial benefits: some water produces some fruits, and only some provision consists of fruit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r2.anchor: وناسب في الآية تنكير الماء وكون من دالة على التبعيض وتنكير الرزق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r3.claim: من الثمرات may be أخرج's object with رزقا circumstantial or a purpose complement; alternatively it attaches to أخرج and رزقا is its object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r3.anchor: ومن الثمرات يحتمل أن يكون في موضع المفعول به بأخرج، ويكون على هذا رزقا منصوبا على الحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r4.speaker: ابن السميفع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r4.claim: Ibn al-Sumayfa reads من الثمرة in the singular, using الثمرة collectively for fruits, like speaking of a garden's fruit or a poem's word.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميفع: من الثمرة على التوحيد، يريد به الجمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r5.claim: If رزق is a verbal noun, the kaf is its object with the lām understood; if it means provisioned goods, لكم modifies omitted كائنا, or attaches to أخرج.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r5.anchor: ولكم: إن أريد بالرزق المصدر كانت الكاف مفعولا به واللام منوية لتعدي المصدر إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r6.claim: The passage gives five signs: creating the addressees and their forebears, then earth as a bed, heaven as a building, and rain and fruit; humans come first as familiar, earth before sky, and effects after causes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r6.anchor: وانتهى عند قوله: رزقا لكم ذكر خمسة أنواع من الدلائل: اثنين من الأنفس خلقهم وخلق من قبلهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r7.claim: Another explanation puts accountable humans first because life, ability, desire, and reason are prerequisites for benefiting from the heavens, earth, water, and fruit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r7.anchor: وقيل: قدم المكلفين لأن خلقهم أحياء قادرين أصل لجميع النعم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r8.speaker: من قال السماء أفضل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r8.claim: Those who consider the heavens superior cite the angels' worship there and the absence of any place where God was disobeyed; the excerpt starts citing Adam after his disobedience but ends before the quotation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r8.anchor: ومن قال السماء أفضل قال: لأنها متعبد الملائكة وما فيها من بقعة عصى الله فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r1.claim: One case for heaven's superiority points to its precedence over earth in many verses, its Throne, Footstool, Preserved Tablet and Pen, and its being the direction of supplication.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r1.anchor: ولتقديم السماء على الأرض في أكثر الآيات، ولأن فيها العرش والكرسي واللوح المحفوظ والقلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r2.speaker: من قال الأرض أفضل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r2.claim: Those preferring earth argue that God blessed places on it, prophets were made from it, and it serves as mosque and purifier.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r2.anchor: ومن قال الأرض أفضل قال: لأن الله وصف منها بقاعا بالبركة، ولأن الأنبياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r3.claim: Calling idols rivals is figurative: people share divinity's name and an outward form of worship with God, but resemble him only in that specified respect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r3.anchor: ظاهره أنه نهى عن اتخاذ الأنداد، وسموا أندادا على جهة المجاز من حيث أشركوهم معه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r4.claim: The polytheists worshipped idols to draw near to God, while calling him the god of gods and lord of lords; they did not worship idols for themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r4.anchor: والعبادة صورة لا حقيقة لأنهم لم يكونوا يعبدونهم لذواتهم بل للتقرب إلى الله تعالى، وكانوا يسمون الله إله الآلهة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r5.claim: The plural prohibition matches their actual practice of assigning God many rivals; Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl's poem asks whether one or a thousand lords should be worshipped.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r5.anchor: ولذلك قال زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r6.speaker: زيد بن علي بن محمد بن السميفع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa read ند in the singular; under negation it is generic, not a command to avoid only one rival.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r6.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي بن محمد بن السميفع: ندا على التوحيد، وهو مفرد في سياق النهي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r7.claim: The prohibition most naturally attaches to the command to worship the Lord: worship entails affirming God's unity and devoting worship to him alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r7.anchor: وهذا النهي متعلق بالأمر في قوله: اعبدوا ربكم، أي فوحدوه وأخلصوا له العبادة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari attaches the prohibition to لعل, parses تجعلوا as subjunctive after a hope, and understands creation as aimed at fear of God's punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r8.anchor: قال الزمخشري: متعلق بلعل، على أن ينتصب تجعلوا انتصاب فأطلع في قوله: لعلي أبلغ الأسباب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r9.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects al-Zamakhshari's parsing because Basran grammarians do not allow a subjunctive as the answer to hope; only Kufans analogize it to an interrogative answer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r9.anchor: فهذا التخريج الذي أخرجه الزمخشري لا يجوز على مذهب البصريين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r10.claim: He also objects that this parsing makes human creation serve the purpose of fearing punishment, which follows al-Zamakhshari's previously discussed Muʿtazilite doctrine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r10.anchor: وفي كلامه تعليق لعلكم تتقون بخلقكم، ألا ترى إلى تقديره أي خلقكم لكي تتقوا وتخافوا عقابه؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r11.claim: Another possible parse connects the prohibition to الذي, treated as the predicate of an omitted subject: he is the one who made these signs, so do not set up rivals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون متعلقا بالذي إذا جعلته خبر مبتدأ محذوف، أي هو الذي جعل لكم هذه الآيات العظيمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r1.claim: The clause is circumstantial; its omitted object is deliberate, since the point is to establish that the addressees possess knowledge and discernment, making idolatry especially unfit for them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r1.anchor: وأنتم تعلمون: جملة حالية، وفيها من التحريك إلى ترك الأنداد وإفراد الله بالوحدانية ما لا يخفى،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains the word for discernment as specifying knowledge to a thing, and takes تعلمون to mean تعقلون, understanding.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r2.anchor: والتمييز تخصيص العلم بشيء، قال معناه ابن قتيبة، لأنه فسر تعلمون بمعنى تعقلون،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada and Muqatil understand the omitted knowledge as awareness that God made the heavens, sent down water and performed the acts just described.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو محذوف اختصارا تقديره: وأنتم تعلمون أنه خلق السموات وأنزل الماء، وفعل ما شرحه في هذه الآيات. ومعنى هذا مروي عن ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r4.claim: A second interpretation attributed to Ibn Abbas is that the matter was not stated in the Torah and Gospel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r4.anchor: أو أنتم تعلمون أنه ليس ذلك في كتابيكم التوراة والإنجيل. وروي ذلك أيضا عن ابن عباس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r5.claim: Mujahid takes the implied knowledge to be that God has no rival.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r5.anchor: أو أنه لا ند له، قاله مجاهد، أو أنتم تعلمون أنه لا يقدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r6.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r6.claim: Ali ibn Ubayd Allah says they know that no one else can perform the acts God has just described.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r6.anchor: أو أنتم تعلمون أنه لا يقدر على فعل ما ذكره أحد سواه، ذكره علي بن عبيد الله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r7.speaker: أبو محمد بن الخشاب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r7.claim: Abu Muhammad ibn al-Khashab interprets the implied knowledge as awareness that the idols are stones.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r7.anchor: أو وأنتم تعلمون أنها حجارة، قاله أبو محمد بن الخشاب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers two readings: they know the difference between God and idols, or know idols cannot do what God does, as the cited challenge to the partners asks.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r8.anchor: قالهما الزمخشري والمخاطب بقوله: فلا تجعلوا ظاهره أنه للناس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r9.speaker: ابن فورك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r9.claim: Ibn Furak allows the addressees to be believers: they are warned not to apostatize into idolatry after learning that divine unity means freedom from ignorance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r9.anchor: قال ابن فورك: ويحتمل أن يكون الخطاب للمؤمنين، المعنى: فلا ترتدوا أيها المؤمنون وتجعلوا لله أندادا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r10.speaker: أبو محمد ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya says God's blessings suffice people without any creature; one who makes himself dependent on another through greed, hope or worldly desire takes on something of a rival.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r10.anchor: قال أبو محمد بن عطية، هذه الآية تعطي أن الله تعالى أغنى الإنسان بنعمه هذه عن كل مخلوق،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r11.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects Ibn Atiyya's construction: unlike ظن, أعطى cannot take أن and its clause as a substitute for its two objects.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p162/r11.anchor: وقول أبي محمد يعطي أن الله أغنى الإنسان، خطأ في التركيب، لأن أعطى لا تنوب أن ومعمولاها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r1.claim: Some exegetes say these creations are singled out because they invite reflection, display benefits in both lives, and prove the Creator's existence, power, wisdom, life, will and exclusive creation and governance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r1.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين: اختص تعالى بهذه المخلوقات وهي: الخلقة البشرية، والبنيتان الأرضية والسماوية، لأنها محل الاعتبار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r4.claim: The sequence can also put the beneficiary before the gifts, since God made these things as benefits for Adam's children and prepared them as blessings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r4.anchor: ولأنه تعالى خلق هذه الأشياء منافع لبني آدم وأعدها نعما يمتن بها عليهم، وذكر المنعم عليه يتقدم على ذكر النعمة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r5.claim: After creating people, God gave them a place to settle, sit, sleep and conduct their livelihoods, including level land for settlement and cultivation, rough ground for refuge, and mountains to steady the earth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r5.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى لما عرفهم أنه خالقهم أخبرهم أنه جعل لهم مكانا يستقرون عليه، إذ كانت حكمته اقتضت ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r6.claim: God then made a protective covering like a tent above them, held without pillars or ropes, so minds would recognize its extraordinary wisdom as beyond human power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r6.anchor: ثم لما من عليهم بالمستقر أخبرهم بجعل ما يقيهم ويظلهم، وجعله كالخيمة المضروبة عليهم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r7.claim: Rain is the supreme blessing: it is the material of life and the cause of the earth stirring with vegetation and many kinds of fruit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r7.anchor: ثم نبههم على النعمة العظمى، وهي إنزال المطر الذي هو مادة الحياة وسبب اهتزاز الأرض بالنبات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r1.claim: Earth is mentioned before the greater sky because familiar roofs and buildings rest on foundations; alternatively, earth was created first, or the order rises from lower to higher.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r1.anchor: لأن السقف والبنيان، فيما يعهد، لا بد له من أساس وعمد مستقر على الأرض، فبدأ بذكرها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r2.claim: The two verses' craft, wisdom and clear proofs show that God alone creates and provides; rivals neither create nor provide, and can neither benefit nor harm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r2.anchor: وقد تضمنت هاتان الآيتان من بدائع الصنعة، ودقائق الحكمة، وظهور البراهين، ما اقتضى تعالى أنه المنفرد بالإيجاد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r3.speaker: بعض أصحاب الإشارات
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r3.claim: An allusive reading compares earth to a mother and sky to a father, rain to semen descending from the father, and fruit to a child born from the mother; the analogy teaches that God truly creates both offspring and fruit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r3.anchor: قال بعض أصحاب الإشارات: لما امتن تعالى عليهم بأنه خلقهم والذين من قبلهم، ضرب لهم مثلا يرشدهم إلى معرفة كيفية خلقهم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r4.speaker: بعض أصحاب الإشارات
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r4.claim: The allusion concludes that recognition of God as the real creator should lead people to single him out in divinity and worship, bringing them to guidance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r4.anchor: فإذا أوضح ذلك لهم أفردوه بالإلهية، وخصوه بالعبادة، وحصلت لهم الهداية.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r6.claim: The long interruption objection can be eased by treating the following phrase as parenthetical, or by making الذي the subject with فلا تجعلوا as predicate; this parsing remains less likely despite al-Baydawi’s apparent preference.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r6.anchor: ومع هذا لا شك في مرجوحية هذا الوجه وإن أشعر كلام مولانا البيضاوي بأرجحيته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r1.claim: الذي may be accusative as an adjective or apposition to ربكم, or detached with an implied verb of specification or praise; Abu al-Baqa’s analysis as object of تتقون is rejected as weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r1.anchor: الموصول إما منصوب على أنه نعت ربكم أو بدل منه أو مقطوع بتقدير أخص أو أمدح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa’s parsing of الذي as the object of تتقون is, in al-Alusi’s judgment, an unworthy and feeble analysis of the Qur’an.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r2.anchor: وكونه مفعول تتقون كما قاله أبو البقاء إعراب غث ينزه القرآن عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r3.claim: It may instead be nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject or as a subject whose predicate is فلا تجعلوا; the fāʾ can introduce a predicate after a past relative clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r3.anchor: وإما مرفوع على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف أو مبتدأ أخبره جملة ( فلا تجعلوا ) والفاء قد تدخل في خبر الموصول بالماضي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r4.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash allows an overt noun to serve as the linking pronoun in the relative construction; an imperative can be predicate through the standard interpretive account.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r4.anchor: والاسم الظاهر يقوم مقام الرابط عند الأخفش والإنشاء يقع خبرا بالتأويل المشهور

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r5.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the still more far-fetched proposal that الذي begins a clause whose predicate is رزقا لكم, understood with an omitted يرزق.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r5.anchor: وأبرد من يخ قول من زعم أنه مبتدأ أخبره ( رزقا لكم ) بتقدير يرزق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r6.claim: جعل can mean ‘turned into,’ taking two objects, or ‘brought into existence,’ with the second accusative as a circumstantial phrase meaning the earth was created spread out for people.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r7.claim: The earth is like a bed because people can sit and sleep on it: God raised parts above water and made its firmness intermediate between hardness and softness for easy use.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r7.anchor: ومعنى تصييرها ( فراشا ) أي كالفراش في صحة القعود والنوم عليها أنه سبحانه جعل بعضها بارزا عن الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r8.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the earth was created before heaven without being spread, then spread out after heaven’s creation; this makes the sense of transformation explicit.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r8.anchor: وإن صح ما نقل عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن الأرض خلقت قبل خلق السماء غير مدحوة فدحيت بعد خلقها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r9.claim: Al-Alusi rejects explaining the transformed state by comparison with the Flood as ignorance’s confused waves; such an account is not common knowledge required by the description.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r9.anchor: والذهاب إلى الطوفان واعتبار التصيير بالقياس إليه من اضطراب أمواج الجهل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r10.claim: Earth’s sphericity does not conflict with its being a spread bed: a sphere is so large that each portion is like a flat surface for use.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r10.anchor: ولا ينافي كرويتها كونها ( فراشا ) لأن الكرة إذا عظمت كان كل قطعة منها كالسطح في افتراشه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r11.claim: Using جعل here after خلق earlier reflects the different context or simply varies the expression, as in the cited verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187/r11.anchor: وعبر سبحانه هنا بجعل وفيما تقدم بخلق لاختلاف المقام أو تفننا في التعبير

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r1.claim: Fronting لكم hastens the good news that the coming object benefits the audience, builds anticipation, or preserves balanced phrasing when the postponed material is long.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r1.anchor: وتقديم المفعول الغير الصريح لتعجيل المسرة ببيان كون ما يعقبه من منافع المخاطبين أو للتشويق إلى ما يأتي بعده

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r2.claim: The singular السماء matches الأرض; explicit pluralization adds little, though the singular may denote all heavens collectively or each layer and direction.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r2.anchor: واختار سبحانه لفظ السماء على السموات موافقة للفظ الأرض وليس في التصريح بتعددها هنا كثير نفع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r3.claim: بناء is originally a verbal noun used for a constructed thing; heaven is pictured as a dome or as a roof over earth, a description also reported from Ibn Abbas.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r3.anchor: والبناء في الأصل مصدر اطلق على المبني بيتا كان أو قبة أو خباء أو طرفا ومنه بنى أهله أو على أهله خلافا للحريري

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas is cited for understanding heaven as a roof over the earth; سقف البيت is also called بناء.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r4.anchor: أو أنها كالسقف للأرض ويقال لسقف البيت بناء وروي هذا عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r5.speaker: الحريري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r5.claim: Al-Hariri disputes the usage in بنى أهله / على أهله; al-Alusi explains that people pitched a new tent for the bride when they married.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r5.anchor: خلافا للحريري لأنهم كانوا إذا تزوجوا ضربوا خباء جديدا ليدخلوا على العروس فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r6.claim: Earth is mentioned before heaven because people need and benefit from it more, it is their first post-creation home, it gives an ascent from lower to higher, its creation precedes heaven in many verses, or it is nobler as the prophets’ dwelling; the last claim is disputed.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r6.anchor: وقدم سبحانه حال الأرض لما أن احتياجهم إليها وانتفاعهم بها أكثر وأظهر أو لأنه تعالى لما ذكر خلقهم ناسب أن يعقبه بذكر أول ما يحتاجونه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r7.speaker: يريد الشامي وطلحة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r7.claim: The reading attributed to Yezid al-Shami is بساطا and Talha reads مهادا, both synonyms for a spread or resting place.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ يريد الشامي بساطا وطلحة مهادا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r8.claim: Abu Amr assimilates the lām of جعل into the lām of لكم.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r8.anchor: وأدغم أبو عمرو لام جعل في لام لكم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r9.claim: The clause beginning وأنزل coordinates with جعل; the first من marks origin and attaches to أنزل or introduces a fronted circumstantial phrase from the object, with fronting creating anticipation and cohesion or enabling the circumstantial reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r9.anchor: فأخرج به من الثمرات رزقا لكم عطف على جعل و ( من ) الأولى للإبتداء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r10.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r10.claim: Al-Bahr says that on the second grammatical analysis من is partitive; the excerpt ends before the explanation continues.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p187#2/r10.anchor: في البحر أن ( من ) على هذا للتبعيض

ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r1.claim: He takes heaven as the upper direction or clouds; identifying it with the specific celestial sphere is also possible given God's power.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r1.anchor: والمراد من السماء جهة العلو أو السحاب وإرادة الفلك المخصوص بناء على الظواهر غير بعيدة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r2.claim: The common account is that the sun raises wet vapor from seas and dry vapor from land; their condensation produces clouds and precipitation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r2.anchor: الشمس إذا سامتت بعض البحار والبراري أثارت من البحار بخارا رطبا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r3.claim: Vapor condenses in the upper air: mild cold yields rain, severe cold snow or hail, and vapor that does not condense remains mist.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r3.anchor: فإذا صعد البخار إلى طبقة الهواء الثالثة تكاثف فإن لم يكن البرد قويا أجتمع وتقاطر لثقله بالتكاثف فالمجتمع سحاب والمتقاطر مطر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r4.claim: On that account, water's descent from heaven means it arises through heavenly causes and ethereal influences, so heaven is its figurative source.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r4.anchor: يراد بالنزول من السماء نشؤوه من أسباب سماوية وتأثيرات أثيرية فهي مبدأ مجازي له

ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r5.claim: Everything in the lower world descends from the repositories of divine will and power, directly or through means, according to wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r5.anchor: كل ما في هذا العالم السفلي نازل من عرش الإرادة وسماء القدرة حسبما تقتضيه الحكمة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r6.claim: One who knows God as being in heaven in the intended, fitting sense, while maintaining transcendence, may call the universe's origin that heaven.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r6.anchor: من علم أن الله سبحانه في السماءعلى المعنى الذي أراده وبالوصف الذي يليق به مع التنزيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r7.claim: Some define water as a flowing substance on which animal life depends; the word is on the pattern faʿl, with its alif from wāw and hamza substituting for hāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r7.anchor: جوهر سيال به قوام الحيوان ووزنه فعل وألفه منقلبة عن واو وهمزته بدل من هاء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r8.claim: The tanwīn on water indicates an unspecified portion.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r9.claim: God repeatedly singles out water as descending from heaven to honor it for its abundant benefit and blessing.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r9.anchor: وخصه سبحانه بالنزول من السماء في كثير من الآيات تنويها بشأنه لكثرة منفعته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r10.claim: If the second min is partitive, some fruits remain ungrown; rizqan is a causal verbal noun for producing, and lakum is attached to rizq as its object.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r10.anchor: إما للتبعيض إذ كم من ثمرة لم تخرج بعد فرزقا حينئذ بالمعنى المصدري مفعول له لأخرج

ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r11.claim: Alternatively, min explains the kind: provided sustenance is the object of produce, lakum qualifies it, and the fronted fruit phrase becomes circumstantial.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r11.anchor: وإما للتبيين فرزق بمعنى مرزوق مفعول لأخرج و ( لكم ) صفته وقد كان ( من الثمرات ) صفته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and many others allow the explanatory phrase to precede what it explains; al-Durr al-Maṣūn's author and others disallow that order.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r12.anchor: في تقديم البيان على المبين خلاف فجوزه الزمخشري والكثيرون ومنعه صاحب الدر المصون وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r13.claim: Treating min as initial-source by supplying an omitted mention of fruits, or glossing fruits as seeds, is strained and unhelpful.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r13.anchor: واحتمال جعلها ابتدائية بتقدير من ذكر الثمرات أو تفسير الثمرات بالبذر تعسف لا ثمرة فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r14.claim: The definite article on fruits can mark either the genus or exhaustive inclusion; taking min as extra would entail that every produced fruit is sustenance for people, which is false.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r14.anchor: وأل في ( الثمرات ) إما للجنس أو للاستغراق وجعلها له ( ومن ) زائدة ليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r15.claim: The paucity plural is apt: worldly produce is tiny beside Paradise's fruits and the unseen stores, or its fruit kinds are few in how much of each is eaten.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r15.anchor: للإيماء إلى أن ما برز في رياض الوجود بفيض مياه الجود كالقليل بل أقل بقليل بالنسبة لثمار الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r16.speaker: الإمام البيضاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r16.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī and others say the plural can convey abundance because it is a plural of thamara, like thimār; the feminine ending can mark an abstract unit.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p188/r16.anchor: وما ذكر الإمام البيضاوي وغيره من أنه ساغ هذا الجمع هنا لأنه أراد بالثمرات جمع ثمرة أريد بها الكثرة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r1.speaker: ابن السميقع
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r1.claim: Ibn al-Sumayqa reads the phrase in the singular, min al-thamara, supporting the use of the feminine singular for a collective fruit sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r1.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة ابن السميقع من الثمرة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r2.claim: The cited phrase “I harvested your garden's fruit” uses the feminine ending as an abstract unit, not a strictly singular unit.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r2.anchor: أدركت ثمرة بستانك وليست التاء للوحدة الحقيقية بل للوحدة الاعتبارية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r3.claim: Others justify the plural by saying plural forms can substitute for one another, as in the cited verses about gardens and three qurūʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r3.anchor: لأن الجموع يتعاور بعضها موقع بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r4.speaker: الشهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r4.claim: Al-Shihāb considers it imperfect to argue that the definite article removes the plural's paucity sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r4.anchor: أو لأنها لما كانت محلاة باللام خرجت عن حد القلة لا يخلو صفاؤه عن كدر كما يسفر عنه كلام الشهاب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r5.claim: If masculine and feminine sound plurals signify abundance, or share that status, the objection disappears; only a few scholars held this view.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r5.anchor: جمع السلامة المؤنث والمذكر موضوع للكثرة أو مشتركو المقام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r6.claim: The bāʾ in “by it” marks causation.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r7.speaker: الأشاعرة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r7.claim: Ashʿarīs treat such causation as customary association: water has no causal effect in producing growth; God alone acts when causes occur, not through them.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r7.anchor: والمشهور عند الأشاعرة أنها سببية عادية في أمثال هذا الموضع فلا تأثير للماء عندهم أصلا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r8.speaker: الأشاعرة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r8.claim: They say belief that God placed the power to quench thirst in water makes one a sinner, with two views on whether that belief entails unbelief; they agree on unbelief if water acts independently.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r8.anchor: ومن أعتقد أن الله تعالى أودع قوة الري في الماء مثلا فهو فاسق وفي كفره قولان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r9.speaker: الأشاعرة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r9.claim: On this account thirst is relieved directly by the originating source, coincidentally with drinking; water has no role beyond the outward coincidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r9.anchor: أن الري جاء من جانب المبدأ الفياض بلا واسطة وصادف مجيئه شرب الماء من غير أن يكون للماء دخل في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects denying causes: God has connected causes and effects in law and nature, making causes the settings for His wisdom, rule, and action.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r10.anchor: ولكني أقول : إن الله سبحانه ربط الأسباب بمسبباتها شرعا وقدرا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r11.claim: Denying causal powers rejects necessities, reason, sense, revelation, and divine reward and punishment; scripture repeatedly establishes causes.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r11.anchor: فإنكار الأسباب والقوى جحد للضروريات وقدح في العقول والفطر ومكابرة للحس وجحد للشرع والجزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r12.claim: Because God creates both cause and effect and makes the cause effective by His will, acknowledging causes neither challenges divine unity nor constitutes associationism.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p189/r12.anchor: إذا كان الله خالق السبب والمسبب وهو الذي جعل هذا سببا لهذا والأسباب والمسببات طوع مشيئته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r1.claim: Causes carry powers God placed in them, but have no effect unless He permits it; this answers the claim that acting through causes entails divine dependence.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r1.anchor: فالأسباب مؤثرة بقوى أودعها الله تعالى فيها ولكن بإذنه وإذا لم يأذن وحال بينها وبين التأثير لم تؤثر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r2.claim: The command that fire become cool and safe for Abraham is meaningful because fire has a power to burn, which God can restrain.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r2.anchor: يا نار كوني بردا وسلاما على إبراهيم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī identifies this causal account with the early righteous predecessors and accepted spiritual authorities; agreement with the Muʿtazila does not discredit truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r3.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكرناه هو ما ذهب إليه السلف الصالح وتلقاه أهل الله تعالى بالقبول ولا يوقعنك في شك منه نسبته للمعتزلة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r4.claim: The prohibition follows the command to worship: since the Lord alone is owed worship, the audience must worship Him alone and make no peer.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r4.anchor: إذا وجب عليكم عبادة ربكم فلا تجعلوا لله ندا وأفردوه بالعبادة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r5.claim: Using the explicit divine name after identifying God by His attributes specifies the true object of worship and ties unity and the impossibility of partners to divinity.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r5.anchor: وإيقاع الاسم الجليل موقع الضمير لتعيين المعبود بالذات بعد تعيينه بالصفات وتعليل الحكم بوصف الألوهية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r6.claim: One view says rabb is a universal concept while Allah names the uniquely necessary existent, so the explicit name is not a pronoun substitution.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r6.anchor: لفظ الرب مستعمل في المفهوم الكلي والله علم للجزئي الحقيقي الواجب الوجود تعالى شأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r7.claim: On that view the fāʾ suits worship linked to lordship here, whereas wāw suits the other verse that links worship and non-association directly to God's name.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r7.anchor: حيث علق العبادة بصفة الربوبية فالمناسب الفاء وبين قوله تعالى : ( أعبدوا الله ولا تشركوا به شيئا )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r8.speaker: مولانا البيضاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r8.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī parses the prohibition as subjunctive after an implicit an in response to the command.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r8.anchor: نفي منصوب بإضمار أن جواب للأمر كما قاله مولانا البيضاوي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r9.claim: An objection says this parse fails because worship cannot cause monotheism, its own foundation; the answer is that worshipping God presupposes monotheism, while worship of the Lord branches from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r9.anchor: واعترض بأنه يأباه إن ذلك فيما يكون الأول سببا للثاني ولا ريب في أن العبادة لا تكون سببا للتوحيد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī concludes that the verse describes the worshipped Lord through His manifest creation and gifts; knowing Him this way leads people not to associate anything with Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r10.anchor: والحق أن الآية تضمنت عبادة رب موصوف بما يجعله كالمشاهد من خلقه لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r11.claim: A possible parse attaches the prohibition to laʿalla and reads the fāʾ like the response in the cited construction; the sense is that creation may lead to fear of God's punishment and not likening Him to creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r11.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون متعلقا بلعل فينصب الفعل نصب ( فأطلع )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r12.claim: Another proposal treats the fāʾ as an added marker of causality and the prohibition clause as an explanatory report about the relative clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p190/r12.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون الفاء زائدة مشعرة بالسببية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r1.claim: A further parse attaches the clause to “the one who made” and takes the fāʾ as a result after an omitted condition: because He made these favors, do not make peers.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r1.anchor: الجملة متعلقة بالذي والفاء جزاء شرط محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r2.claim: Here jaʿala means to make something into something, whether by physical action or by speech and convention.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r2.anchor: والجعل هنا بمعنى التصيير وهو كما يكون بالفعل نحو صيرت الحديد سيفا ومنه ما تقدم على وجه يكون بالقول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r3.claim: The preferred meaning of nidd is a counterpart that opposes, differs from, and flees another; it is not itself an antonym.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r3.anchor: والند مثل الشيء الذي يضاده ويخالفه في أموره وينافره ويتباعد عنه وليس من الأضداد على الأصح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r4.claim: A reported lexical distinction makes nidd a partner in essence, shakl one in measure, shibh one in quality, musāwī one in quantity, and mithl general.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r4.anchor: وقيل : الند المشارك في الجوهرية فقط والشكل المشارك في القدر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r5.claim: Calling idols peers is ironic mockery: idolaters did not deem them God's equals, but worshipped them as supposed means of drawing near to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r5.anchor: إشارة إلى استعارة تهكمية حيث أستعير النظير المصادر للمناسب المقرب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r6.claim: If nidd means any counterpart, the wording instead analogizes idols to God because polytheists made them alike in worship; this exposes their folly, though the first reading is preferable.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r6.anchor: وإن أريد بالند النظير مطلقا لم يكن هناك تضاد وإنما هو من استعارة أحد المتشابهين للآخر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r7.claim: The plural intensifies the rebuke by making many peers for the One who cannot have even one.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r7.anchor: حيث جعلوا ( أندادا ) لمن يستحيل أن يكون له ند واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r8.speaker: زيد بن عمر بن نفيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r8.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl's poetry rejects divided worship, asks whether he should worship one or a thousand gods, and says a clear-sighted man abandons al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r8.anchor: أربا واحدا أم ألف رب أدين إذا تقسمت الأمور تركت اللات والعزى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r9.claim: The phrase may be a circumstantial clause with an omitted object: the audience knows God has no equal, or knows idols cannot match His works.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r9.anchor: وحالكم أنكم من أهل العلم والمعرفة والنظر وإصابة الرأي فإذا تأملتم أدنى تأمل علمتم وجود صانع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r10.claim: If it describes their general knowledge, the clause either reproaches them or restricts responsibility to people capable of knowing; with the second reading it is reproach only.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r10.anchor: والحال على الوجه الأول للتوبيخ أو التقييد إذ العلم مناط التكليف ولا تكليف عند عدم الأهلية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r11.claim: The rebuke can address some within a general audience; restricting the address to unbelievers may be preferable and fits the challenge, since believers already persist in worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r11.anchor: بل قيل : إنه أولى للخلاص من التكلف وحسن الانتظام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r12.claim: The favors display God's unique power to create and provide, making Him alone worthy of worship; idols neither create nor provide nor benefit or harm, as another verse says.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r12.anchor: أنه تعالى المنفرد بالإيجاد المستحق للعبادة دون غيره من الأنداد التي لا تخلق ولا ترزق وليس لها نفع ولا ضر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r13.claim: An allusive reading maps the body to earth, the soul to heaven, intellect to water, and intellectual and practical virtues to fruits produced through the faculties.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r13.anchor: والنفس بالسماء والعقل بالماء وما أفاض على القوابل من الفضائل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r14.claim: Another analogy makes earth the mother, heaven the father, rain the father's seed, and fruit the child, so people recognize God as creator of both children and produce.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r14.anchor: وضرب الماء النازل من السماء مثلا للنطفة التي تنزل من صلب الأب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r15.claim: The creation analogy aims to make divine formation comprehensible and guide people to single God out for divinity and worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p191/r15.anchor: فإذا وضح ذلك لهم أفردوه بالألوهية وخصوه بالعبادة وحصلت لهم الهداية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r1.claim: The earth is a spread-out surface, a place to sleep, or a level floor; God made it tractable rather than rough and impossible to settle on.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r1.anchor: أي بساطا وقيل مناما وقيل وطاء أي ذللها ولم يجعلها حزنة لا يمكن القرار عليها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r2.speaker: عبد الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r2.claim: The Prophet names associating a partner with God, despite God having created the person, as the greatest sin; next are killing a child for fear of sharing food and adultery with a neighbor's wife.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله رضي قال: سألت رسول الله عليه وسلم: أي ذنب أعظم عند الله؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r4.claim: The sky is a raised roof.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r5.claim: “From the sky” means from the clouds, and the water is rain.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r5.anchor: {وأنزل من السماء} أي من السحاب {ماء} المطر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r6.claim: The rain brings out varieties of fruits and plants as provision: food for people and fodder for their animals.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r6.anchor: {فأخرج به من الثمرات} ألوان الثمرات وأنواع النبات {رزقا لكم} طعاما لكم وعلفا لدوابكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r7.claim: Andād are likenesses or counterparts that people worship as they worship God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r8.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says nidd can mean an opposite, one of the words with opposed senses; God is free of any likeness or opposite.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r8.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: الند الضد وهو من الأضداد والله تعالى بريء من المثل والضد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r9.claim: They know that God alone is the creator of these things.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72/r9.anchor: {وأنتم تعلمون} أنه واحد خالق هذه الأشياء

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22/r1.claim: Alladhī may be a second adjective, an accusative or nominative expression of praise, or a subject whose predicate is the prohibition fa-lā tajʿalū; jaʿala itself can mean become or begin intransitively, bring into being with one object, or render with two.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22/r1.anchor: صفة ثانية، أو مدح منصوب، أو مرفوع، أو مبتدأ خبره فلا تجعلوا وجعل من الأفعال العامة يجيء على ثلاثة أوجه:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22/r2.claim: Earth is made like a spread bed because some of it was raised above the enveloping water and balanced between hardness and softness, making it suitable for sitting and sleeping; this does not require a flat rather than spherical earth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22/r2.anchor: جعل بعض جوانبها بارزا ظاهرا عن الماء، مع ما في طبعه من الإحاطة بها، وصيرها متوسطة بين الصلابة واللطافة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r1.claim: The heaven is a dome built over people, sheltering them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r1.anchor: قبة مضروبة عليكم. والسماء اسم جنس يقع على الواحد والمتعدد كالدينار والدرهم،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r2.claim: Samāʾ is a generic noun used for one or many, or is said to be the plural of samāʾah; bināʾ is a verbal noun applied to what is built, such as a house, dome, or tent, and the wedding phrase refers to setting up a new tent.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r2.anchor: والبناء مصدر، سمي به المبنى بيتا كان أو قبة أو خباء، ومنه بني على امرأته،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r3.claim: The sending down of water is coordinated with God's making the earth a bed; fruits emerge through God's power and will, with water mixed into soil serving as means and material.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r3.anchor: عطف على (جعل)، وخروج الثمار بقدرة الله تعالى ومشيئته، ولكن جعل الماء الممزوج بالتراب

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r4.claim: God either customarily imparts forms and qualities to mixed water and soil, or places active power in water and receptive power in earth; He could create things without causes or matter, but gradual creation renews lessons and steadies observers in awareness of His power.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r4.anchor: بأن أجرى عادته بإفاضة صورها وكيفياتها على المادة الممتزجة منهما، أو أودع في الماء قوة فاعلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r5.claim: The first min marks origin, whether sky means clouds (anything above is sky), the celestial sphere (rain passes from it to clouds then earth according to the apparent texts), or celestial causes lifting moisture to form rain clouds.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r5.anchor: و { من } الأولى للابتداء سواء أريد بالسماء السحاب فإن ما علاك سماء، أو الفلك فإن المطر

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r6.claim: The second min can be partitive, as 35:27 supports: not all water descends, not all fruit grows by rain, and not all sustenance consists of fruit; or it can explain the kind, with rizq meaning the provision received.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r6.anchor: و { من } الثانية للتبعيض بدليل قوله تعالى:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r7.claim: Thamarāt can denote groups of individual fruits as a collective plural; the singular reading al-thamarah supports this explanation. Plurals may also exchange places, or the definite plural may fall outside the limit of paucity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#2/r7.anchor: وإنما ساغ الثمرات والموضع موضع الكثرة، لأنه أراد بالثمرات جماعة الثمرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r1.claim: Lakum modifies rizq if it means the provision received; if rizq is a verbal noun, lakum is its object, meaning provision for you.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r1.anchor: و { لكم } صفة رزقا إن أريد به المرزوق ومفعوله إن أريد به المصدر

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r2.claim: Fa-lā tajʿalū may coordinate a prohibition with worship, be subjunctive after an implied an, or depend on laʿalla so the sense is if you are mindful, do not make rivals; it may also be a prohibitive predicate of alladhī jaʿala.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r2.anchor: متعلق باعبدوا على أنه نهي معطوف عليه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r3.claim: The causal fāʾ links the prohibition to God's having singled people out for immense blessings and signs: the One who granted them should not be associated with.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r3.anchor: والفاء للسببية أدخلت عليه لتضمن المبتدأ معنى الشرط والمعنى: أن من خصكم بهذه النعم الجسام

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r4.claim: A nidd is an opposing equal or likeness; the word is reserved for a counterpart matching in essence, while a like in degree is called a musāwī. Jarīr's verse uses nidd for a rival.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r4.anchor:
قال جرير:
أتيما تجعلون إلي ندا
وما تيم لذي حسب نديد

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r5.claim: Calling idols rivals is sarcastic censure: polytheists need not claim equality with God in essence or attributes, but worshiping and naming them gods resembles believing they are self-existent and can repel harm or grant good.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r5.anchor: وتسمية ما يعبده المشركون من دون الله (أندادا)، وما زعموا أنها تساويه في ذاته وصفاته

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r6.speaker: زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r6.claim: The pre-Islamic monotheist Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl's verse contrasts worshiping one God with a thousand and declares that he abandoned al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#3/r6.anchor: ولهذا قال موحد الجاهلية زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل: أربا واحدا أم ألف رب أدين

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r1.claim: Wa-antum taʿlamūn is circumstantial to the subject of fa-lā tajʿalū, with its object omitted: you are people of knowledge, reflection, and sound judgment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r1.anchor: حال من ضمير فلا تجعلوا، ومفعول تعلمون مطروح، أي: وحالكم أنكم من أهل العلم والنظر وإصابة الرأي،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r2.claim: Alternatively, the omitted object is that idols neither resemble God nor can do what He does, as 30:40 asks whether partners can do any such thing; the point is rebuke, not restricting the duty to the learned.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r2.anchor: أو منوي وهو أنها لا تماثله ولا تقدر على مثل ما يفعله كقوله سبحانه وتعالى:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r3.claim: The two verses command worship and forbid associating partners, then give their rationale: lordship grounds worship; God created people, their ancestors, and necessities of life, and these uniquely divine provisions witness His oneness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r3.anchor: واعلم إن مضمون الآيتين هو الأمر بعبادة الله سبحانه وتعالى، والنهي عن الإشراك به تعالى،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r4.claim: The verse can also allude to human formation: body is earth, soul heaven, intellect water, and practical and theoretical virtues produced through intellect and senses are fruits of joined celestial active and earthly receptive powers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r4.anchor: فمثل البدن بالأرض، والنفس بالسماء، والعقل بالماء، وما أفاض عليه من الفضائل العملية والنظرية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r1.claim: The command to worship is supported by creation of earlier and present peoples and the benefits that follow; visible signs make exclusive worship evident just after the account of human obstinacy.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r1.anchor: وما أحسن الأمر بالعبادة حال الاستدلال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r2.claim: Each person knows they came into existence after nonexistence, so an originator other than humanity must exist; changing cosmic things also require an unchanging cause that is neither body nor bodily.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r2.anchor: كل أحد يعرف ضرورة أنه وجد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r3.claim: The sequence recalls immense favors to awaken love of the benefactor, end disputation, and produce obedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r3.anchor: في سياق مذكر بالنعم الجسام الموجبة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r4.claim: Harali defines making as bringing something forth through a cause and transformation; earth gathers visible and hidden growth, is named for its low position opposite the elevated sky, and is like the tablet on which the pen displays its book.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r4.anchor: قال الحرالي : من الجعل وهو إظهار أمر عن سبب وتصيير

BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r5.claim: Farsh is a spread resting place for ease; the earth is the dwelling-place of living creatures and the dead, under the sky as its roof.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r5.anchor: { فراشا } وهي بساط سقفه السماء وهي مستقر الحيوان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r6.claim: The sky is a vast, finely ordered and beautiful tent that encloses a sound place of habitation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r6.anchor: أي خيمة تحيط بصلاح موضع السكن وهو لعمري بناء جليل القدر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r7.claim: The signs are ordered from the familiar human self, to earlier generations, indispensable earth, its sky-roof, then water and the sustenance produced between them.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r8.claim: Sending down is moving something from above to below by command; rain comes from the sky as winds stir clouds carrying water, a subtle body that quenches thirst and gives life to growing things.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p55/r8.anchor: قال الحرالي : من الإنزال وهو الإهواء بالأمر من علو إلى سفل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r1.claim: Bringing out means revealing what was concealed; the fāʾ confirms that the water causes the growth.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r1.anchor: من الإخراج وهو إظهار من حجاب , وفي سوقه بالفاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r2.claim: The scarce plural and indefinite provision downplay even immeasurably abundant fruits and sustenance beside God’s power, magnifying Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r2.anchor: وأتي بجمع القلة في الثمر ونكر الرزق مع المشاهدة لأنهما بالغان في الكثرة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r3.claim: Fruits are edible produce of plants and trees; min excludes husks, chaff, and pits, non-provision fruits, medicines, and poisons from the intended sustenance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r3.anchor: والثمر كما قال الحرالي : مطعومات النجم والشجر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r4.claim: The phrase for you suggests that provision completes people’s constitution and ultimately returns from them as recompense.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r4.anchor: وفي قوله : { لكم } إشعار بأن في الرزق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r5.claim: Two relative clauses describe the Lord: the second uses making because sustenance and maintenance depend on the prior act of creation; an awakened person naturally reveres whoever provides shelter, food, and drink, so the evidence presses the soul toward submission.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r5.anchor: وقد وصف الرب في هذه الآية بموصولين ذكر صلة الثاني بلفظ الجعل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r6.claim: The argument is tailored to the Arabs’ reliance on immediate, necessary knowledge rather than speculative inference: it moves from innate awareness to clearer awareness and avoids acquired proofs that can invite doubt.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p56/r6.anchor: لأن العرب لا تعدو بأنفسها العلم الضروري وليس من شأنها تكلف الأفكار

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r1.claim: Human constitution and provision parallel one another: water is the origin of human formation and the basis of its sustenance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r1.anchor: أن الماء بزر كون الإنسان كما أن الماء أصل رزقه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r2.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r2.claim: When asked who he was, the Prophet declined to identify himself and answered that they were from water.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r2.anchor: قال عليه السلام لمن سأله ممن هو فلم يرد أن يعين له نفسه : ( نحن من ماء )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r3.claim: Earth and heaven contribute to human constitution, and their roles in producing provision follow from that; naming them also encompasses their full extent.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r3.anchor: أن للأرض والسماء مدخلا في أمشاج الإنسان رتب عليه مدخلها في كون رزقه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r4.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r4.claim: The Prophet said that whoever usurps even a span of land will have it encircle him from seven earths; no grading is stated.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r4.anchor: قال عليه السلام : ( من اغتصب شبرا من أرض طوقه من سبع أرضين )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r5.claim: Earth is mentioned before heaven because people's attention turns to what is below them before what is above.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r5.anchor: وقدم الأرض لأن نظر النفوس إلى ما تحتها أسبق لها من نظرها إلى ما علا عليها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r6.claim: The manifest proof of lordship persuaded most people, while their hesitation concerned messengership, so the passage follows lordship with a warning about the message.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r6.anchor: ولوضوح آية الربوبية تقلدها الأكثر وإنما توقفوا في الرسالة ولذلك وصل ذكر الرسالة بالتهديد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r7.claim: The prohibition follows from both the command to worship and the reminder that God alone performs the acts just listed.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r7.anchor: ولما أمر بعبادته وذكرهم سبحانه بما يعلمون أنه فاعله وحده حسن النهي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r8.claim: Using the name Allah in the rebuke suits the condemnation of treating another as divine.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r8.anchor: قال معبرا بالجلالة على ما هو الأليق بالتوبيخ على تأله الغير

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r9.claim: Alternatively, the prohibition can answer the hoped-for taqwa: lā is then negative and the verb is subjunctive.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مسببا عن التقوى المرتجاة فتكون لا نافية والفعل منصوب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r10.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines an ند as a rival that competes in an attribute of standing and permanence.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r10.anchor: قال الحرالي : جمع ند وهو المقاوم في صفة القيام والدوام

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r11.claim: The verb jaʿala suggests a descent from one state to another, through which heedlessness settles over hearts.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r11.anchor: عبر بالجعل لأن بالجعل والمصير من حال إلى حال أدنى منها ترين الغفلة على القلوب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r12.claim: People who see only creatures as sources of blessings and afflictions attach their hopes and fears to powerful beings, become submissive to them, and thereby worship false powers.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r12.anchor: حتى لا تشهد في النعم والنقم إلا الخلق من ملك أو ذي إمرة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r13.claim: The rebuke targets people who claim knowledge: associating despite the proofs shows they lack sound knowledge and are like beasts.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r13.anchor: فإنه يلوح إلى أن من أشرك به مع قيام هذه الأدلة لم يكن ممن يصح منه العلم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r14.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r14.claim: Al-Ḥarālī argues that all creatures, high and low, depend on heaven, earth, and water, so making any of them God's rival contradicts necessary knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r14.anchor: كما قال الحرالي : إعلام بظهور آيات ما يمنع جعل الند لما يشاهد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r15.speaker: author
