BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r15.claim: The verse rebukes those who abandon the one capable of everything to worship what can do nothing.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r15.anchor: وفي تعقيبها لما قبلها غاية التبكيت على من ترك هذا القادر على كل شيء وعبد ما لا يقدر على شيء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r16.claim: This decisive teaching is shared by all revealed laws and scriptures and is the foundation of reverence, humility, and submission.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r16.anchor: وهذه الآية من المحكم الذي اتفقت عليه الشرائع واجتمعت عليه الكتب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r17.speaker: أبو الحسن الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r17.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the passage trains the servant to turn sincerely to God by disowning the self, surrendering, serving reverently, relying on God, and resting in Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p57/r17.anchor: قال الإمام أبو الحسن الحرالي في العروة : وجه إنزال هذا الحرف تحقيق

DURR-FULL:v1p85/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and other Companions describe the earth as a bed, resting place, and stable ground, and the sky as a dome-like roof built over it.
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة في قوله {الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا} قال: هي فراش يمشي عليها وهي المهاد والقرار

DURR-FULL:v1p85/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r2.claim: Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim reports that the Prophet rejected treating God as an intermediary, declared Him above the seven heavens on His throne, gestured to a dome, and described the throne creaking under Him like a saddle under a rider.
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r2.anchor: عن جبير بن مطعم قال جاء اعرابي إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله جهدت الأنفس وضاعت العيال

DURR-FULL:v1p85/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r3.speaker: إياس بن معاوية
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r3.claim: Iyās ibn Muʿāwiya says the sky is domed over the earth like a cupola.
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r3.anchor: عن إياس بن معاوية قال: السماء مقببة على الأرض مثل القبة

DURR-FULL:v1p85/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r4.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r4.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says the sky's edges encircle the lands and seas like the hem of a tent.
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r4.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه قال: شيء من أطراف السماء محدق بالأرضين والبحار كأطراف الفسطاط

DURR-FULL:v1p85/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r5.speaker: القاسم بن أبي برة
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r5.claim: Al-Qāsim ibn Abī Barra says the sky is not square but domed and appears green to people.
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r5.anchor: عن القاسم بن أبي برة قال: ليست السماء مربعة ولكنها مقببة يراها الناس خضراء

DURR-FULL:v1p85/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says rain comes from the sky and descends into clouds, which serve as a medium for it.
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r6.anchor: عن الحسن أنه سئل المطر من السماء أم من السحاب قال: من السماء إنما السحاب علم ينزل عليه الماء من السماء

DURR-FULL:v1p85/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r7.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r7.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says he does not know whether rain falls drop by drop from heaven into clouds or forms in clouds before falling.
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r7.anchor: عن وهب قال: لا أدري المطر أنزل قطرة من السماء في السحاب أم خلق في السحاب فأمطر

DURR-FULL:v1p85/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r8.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r8.claim: Kaʿb calls clouds a sieve for rain, saying they prevent heavenly water from damaging the ground and that seed descends from heaven.
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r8.anchor: عن كعب قال: السحاب غربال المطر ولولا السحاب حين ينزل الماء من السماء لأفسد ما يقع عليه

DURR-FULL:v1p85/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r9.speaker: خالد بن معدان
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r9.claim: Khālid ibn Maʿdān says rain comes from beneath the Throne, descends through the heavens to a reservoir in the lowest heaven, then black clouds absorb it like sponges and are driven wherever God wills.
DURR-FULL:v1p85/r9.anchor: عن خالد بن معدان قال: المطر ماء يخرج من تحت العرش فينزل من سماء إلى سماء حيث يجمع في السماء الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v1p86/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r1.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r1.claim: ʿIkrima says water descends from the seventh heaven and each drop falls onto a cloud as large as a camel.
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: ينزل الماء من السماء السابعة فتقع القطرة منه على السحابة مثل البعير

DURR-FULL:v1p86/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r2.speaker: خالد بن يزيد
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r2.claim: Khālid ibn Yazīd says rain includes heavenly water and sea water carried by clouds and sweetened by thunder and lightning; sea water does not grow plants, which grow from heavenly water.
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r2.anchor: عن خالد بن يزيد قال: المطر منه من السماء ومنه ماء يسقيه الغيم من البحر فيعذبه الرعد والبرق

DURR-FULL:v1p86/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r3.claim: ʿIkrima says every drop sent from heaven grows a plant on land or a pearl in the sea.
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: ما أنزل الله من السماء قطرة إلا أنبت بها في الأرض عشبة أو في البحر لؤلؤة

DURR-FULL:v1p86/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says rain makes shells open and God creates pearls inside; larger drops produce larger pearls.
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: يخلق الله اللؤلؤ في الأصداف من المطر تفتح الأصداف أفواهها عند المطر فاللؤلؤة العظيمة من القطرة العظيمة

DURR-FULL:v1p86/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r5.claim: Al-Muṭṭalib ibn Ḥanṭab reports the Prophet saying that rain falls at every hour of night and day and God directs it wherever He wills.
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r5.anchor: عن المطلب بن حنطب أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ما من ساعة من ليل ولا نهار إلا والسماء تمطر فيها

DURR-FULL:v1p86/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says every rain from heaven carries seed, which could be seen by spreading out a leather mat.
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: ما نزل مطر من السماء إلا ومعه البذر

DURR-FULL:v1p86/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says rain's mixture comes from Paradise, and the blessing rises or falls with that mixture even when rainfall amount differs.
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: المطر مزاجه من الجنة فإذا عظم المزاج عظمت البركة وإن قل المطر

DURR-FULL:v1p86/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r8.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan says annual rainfall totals are alike but God directs rain differently; angels descend to record where it falls, who receives it, and what grows from each drop.
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r8.anchor: عن الحسن قال: ما من عام بأمطر من عام ولكن الله يصرفه حيث يشاء وينزل مع المطر

DURR-FULL:v1p86/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says not to associate God with powerless rivals that can neither harm nor benefit, since people know that no one but Him provides for them.
DURR-FULL:v1p86/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس {فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا} أي لا تشركوا به غيره من الأنداد التي لا تضر ولا تنفع

DURR-FULL:v1p87/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses al-andād as associating partners with God.
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال الأنداد هو الشرك

DURR-FULL:v1p87/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also glosses al-andād as likenesses or equivalents.
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله الأنداد قال: أشباها

DURR-FULL:v1p87/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd explains the rivals as men obeyed in disobedience to God.
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله {فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا} قال: أكفاء من الرجال تطعيونهم في معصية الله

DURR-FULL:v1p87/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines al-andād as likenesses and examples, citing Labīd's poetry as Arabic evidence for the word nad.
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قول الله عز وجل {أندادا} قال: الأشباه والأمثال

DURR-FULL:v1p87/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {أندادا} قال: شركاء

DURR-FULL:v1p87/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r6.claim: When a caller began the prayer call, the Prophet called the declaration that God is greatest the natural disposition and the declaration of His oneness a casting off of rivals.
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r6.anchor: عن عوف بن عبد الله قال خرج النبي

DURR-FULL:v1p87/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r7.claim: When a man said what God willed and Muhammad willed, the Prophet told him he had made him God's rival and corrected him: what God alone willed.
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال قال رجل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما شاء الله وشئت فقال: جعلتني لله ندا ما شاء الله وحده

DURR-FULL:v1p87/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r8.speaker: قتيلة بنت صيفي
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r8.claim: Qutayla bint Ṣayfī reports a Jewish scholar objecting to swearing by the Kaʿba and to saying what God and Muhammad willed; the Prophet redirected oath-taking to the Lord of the Kaʿba and told them to say first God's will, then Muhammad's.
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r8.anchor: عن قتيلة بنت صيفي قال جاء حبر من الأحبار إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا محمد نعم القوم أنتم لولا أنكم تشركون

DURR-FULL:v1p87/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r9.speaker: طفيل بن صخبرة
DURR-FULL:v1p87/r9.claim: In Ṭufayl ibn Ṣakhraba's dream, Jews say Muslims are good except for saying what God and Muhammad willed, after Muslims object that Jews call ʿUzayr God's son.

DURR-FULL:v1p88/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p88/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p88/r1.claim: After Ṭufayl's dream also recounts Christians objecting to saying what God and Muhammad willed, the Prophet publicly forbids that wording and directs people to say God wills alone, with no partner.
DURR-FULL:v1p88/r1.anchor: فلما أصبح أخبر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فخطب فقال: إن طفيلا رأى رؤيا وإنكم تقولون كلمة

DURR-FULL:v1p88/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p88/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p88/r2.claim: The Prophet forbids saying what God and a person wills together, and instructs people to say what God wills, then what that person wills.
DURR-FULL:v1p88/r2.anchor: عن حذيفة ابن اليمان عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لا تقولوا ما شاء الله وشاء فلان

DURR-FULL:v1p88/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p88/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p88/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses al-andād as equals and says people know God created them and the heavens and earth.
DURR-FULL:v1p88/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا أي عدلاء {وأنتم تعلمون} قال: إن الله خلقكم وخلق السموات والأرض

DURR-FULL:v1p88/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p88/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p88/r4.claim: Mujāhid glosses al-andād as equals and says people know from the Torah and Gospel that God is one and has no rival.
DURR-FULL:v1p88/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا} أي عدلاء {وأنتم تعلمون} قال تعلمون أنه إله واحد في التوراة والإنجيل

IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r1.claim: Abu al-Aliya glosses the earth as a bed or resting place.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية : الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا قال : مهادا .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r2.speaker: السدي وقتادة والربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says the earth is spread for walking, a resting place and stable abode; Qatada and al-Rabiʿ report similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r2.anchor: عن السدى : الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا اما فراشا فهي فراش يمشي عليها وهي المهاد والقرار . وروى عن قتادة والربيع بن انس نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r3.claim: A prophetic report depicts God above His Throne, the Throne above the heavens, and the heavens above the earths, gesturing like a dome.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم : ويحك اتدري مالله ؟ ان الله على عرشه وعرشه على سماواته

IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r4.speaker: السدي وقتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r4.claim: Al-Suddi explains the heaven as a dome-like structure and roof over the earth; Qatada reports similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r4.anchor: عن السدى : والسماء بناء اما السماء بناء ، فبناء السماء على الأرض كهيئة القبة وهي سقف على الأرض وروى عن قتادة نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r5.speaker: خالد بن معدان
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r5.claim: Khalid ibn Maʿdan says rain descends from beneath the Throne through the heavens, gathers in a reservoir called al-abzam, then enters clouds that God drives where He wills.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r5.anchor: أم عبد الله يعني - ابنة خالد بن معدان عن ابيها ، قال ان المطر ماء يخرج من تحت العرش

IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says wind draws water from clouds, which fill like a she-camel’s udder and pour in separated streams like waterskins.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قال يرسل الله الريح فتسل الماء من السحاب فيمر به السحاب فتدرة كما تدر الناقة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r7.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r7.claim: Ikrima says every drop of rain God sends grows either a plant on land or a pearl in the sea.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p60/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة قال : ما انزل الله من السماء قطرة الا انبت بها في الأرض عشبة أو في البحر لؤلؤة .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Dahhak, glosses andad as likenesses.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس في قوله : فلا تجعلوا لله اندادا قال : اشباها .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas describes hidden shirk as subtler than an ant’s movement on dark stone at night and gives examples involving oaths and crediting creatures with protection.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : فلا تجعلوا لله اندادا قال : الانداد هو الشرك اخفى من دبيب النمل

IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r3.claim: He warns against saying “what God and you willed” or “if not for God and so-and-so,” because these expressions associate another with God.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : فلا تجعلوا لله اندادا قال : الانداد هو الشرك اخفى من دبيب النمل

IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r4.speaker: أبو العالية والربيع بن أنس وقتادة والسدي وأبو مالك وإسماعيل بن أبي خالد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya defines andad as an equal or partner; the other named authorities report similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r4.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله : اندادا اي عدلا شركا - وروى عن الربيع بن انس وقتادة والسدى وابي مالك واسماعيل بن أبي خالد نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says people know their rivals neither benefit nor harm, that God alone provides for them, and that the Messenger’s call to His oneness is true.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس : فلا تجعلوا لله اندادا وأنتم تعلمون اي لا تشركوا بالله غيره من الانداد التي لا تنفع ولا تضر

IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r6.claim: Mujahid says they know from the Torah and Gospel that God is one God.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : فلا تجعلوا لله اندادا وأنتم تعلمون قال ، تعلمون انه اله واحد في التوراة والانجيل .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r7.claim: Qatada argues that they know God created them and the heavens and earth, yet still assign Him rivals.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p62/r7.anchor: عن قتادة : فلا تجعلوا لله اندادا وأنتم تعلمون ان الله خلقكم وخلق السماوات والأرض ، ثم أنتم تجعلون له اندادا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr reads this as a second description of the Lord, like 2:21, adding continuous benefits and signs of power as grounds for exclusive worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r1.anchor: صفة ثانية للرب لأن مساقها مساق قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r2.claim: Earth as a bed means a stable, comfortable surface for settling or reclining, midway between painful rock and yielding mud in which creatures sink.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r2.anchor: ومعنى جعل الأرض فراشا أنها كالفراش في التمكن من الاستقرار والاضطجاع عليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r3.claim: In customary Arab singular usage, al-samāʾ is the visible blue dome, meaning the atmospheric sphere surrounding Earth, as in 2:19.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r3.anchor: المراد بالسماء هنا إطلاقها العرفي عند العرب وهو ما يبدو للناظر كالقبة الزرقاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r4.claim: The atmosphere resembles a building because it separates Earth from the aether and protects against harms, including inundation and dangerous celestial airs; its dome-like appearance reinforces the image.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r4.anchor: جعلها الله حاجزة بين الكرة الأرضية وبين الكرة الأثيرية فهي كالبناء فيما يراد له البناء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r5.claim: In Arabic, bināʾ is a raised shelter for protection, whether stone, leather, or hair; the term also applies to a domed leather tent, and building over a wife means marrying her.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p331/r5.anchor: والبناء في كلام العرب ما يرفع سمكه على الأرض للوقاية سواء كان من حجر أو من أدم أو من شعر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p332/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p332/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p332/r1.claim: The benefit of the sky was accessible to the first audience in general terms through the analogy with a protective building; each generation can infer according to its understanding, with later generations developing the detail.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p332/r1.anchor: ويكفي في الامتنان بخلق السماء إشعار السامعين لهذه الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p332/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p332/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p332/r2.claim: The second لكم is omitted before mention of the sky for concision; the earlier لكم with the earth also governs it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p332/r2.anchor: عند ذكر السماء إيجازا لأن ذكره في قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p332/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p332/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p332/r3.claim: If jaʿala means create, the blessing is the present condition of earth and sky; if it means transform, geological strata support their transition through stages, yielding blessings and signs in both their state and development, as in 21:30–32.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p332/r3.anchor: إن كانت بمعنى أوجد فحمل الامتنان هو إن كانتا على هذه الحالة وإن كانت بمعنى صير فهي دالة على أن الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r1.claim: Earth and sky are singled out as the closest, most obvious, life-essential benefits; earth comes first as what one sees before looking to the surrounding sky, and their mention prepares for rain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r1.anchor: وابتدأ بالأرض لأنها أول ما يخطر ببال المعتبر ثم بالسماء لأنه بعد أن ينظر لما بين يديه ينظر إلى ما يحيط به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r2.claim: Rain and produce preserve life by replacing bodily strength consumed by innate heat and nerve and brain activity; food from the earth sustains the body.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r2.anchor: وهو خلقة لما تتلفه الحرارة الغريزية والعمل العصبي والدماغي من القوة البدنية ليدوم قوام البدن بالغذاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r3.claim: Solar heat evaporates water from seas, rivers, damp earth, and plants; vapor cools aloft, condenses into clouds, and grows heavy into rain, as described in 13:12.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r3.anchor: فإن الجو ممتلىء دائما بالأبخرة الصاعدة إليه بواسطة حرارة الشمس من مياه البحار والأنهار ومن نداوة الأرض ومن النبات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r4.claim: Heat and low pressure increase vapor's ascent and expansion, while cold and high pressure liquefy it; evaporation is stronger near the equator and diminishes farther away.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r4.anchor: ومن القواعد أن الحرارة وقلة الضغط يزيدان في صعود البخار وفي قوة انبساطه والبرودة وكثرة الضغط يصيران البخار مائعا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr cites a hadith saying that a sea-originating weather front turning toward Sham brings abundant rain; he gives no grading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r5.anchor: إذا أنشأت بحرية ثم تشاءمت فتلك عين غديقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r6.claim: He cites an ungraded hadith that rain descends from a rock beneath the Throne.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r6.anchor: وإلى بعض هذا يشير ما ورد في الحديث أن المطر ينزل من صخرة تحت العرش

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r7.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr interprets the Throne as one of the heavens and the rock as an approximation of a cold place: cooling condenses vapor and initiates rain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p333/r7.anchor: فإن العرش هو اسم لسماء من السماوات والصخرة تقريب لمكان ذي برودة وقد علمت أن المطر تنشئه البرودة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r1.claim: Min is not partitive, which would not suit the blessing context; it is either explanatory of the provision produced or an extra particle emphasizing extraction from fruits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r1.anchor: ليست للتبعيض إذ ليس التبعيض مناسبا لمقام الامتنان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r2.claim: The fa makes the prohibition follow from the preceding evidence and the command to worship: the one who commanded worship alone deserves it uniquely.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r2.anchor: أتت الفاء لترتيب هاته الجملة على الكلام السابق وهو مترتب على الأمر بالعبادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r3.claim: Lā is prohibitive and makes the verb jussive, rather than negative with a subjunctive verb as the result of the earlier imperative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r3.anchor: ناهية والفعل مجزوم وليست نافية حتى يكون الفعل منصوبا في جواب الأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r4.claim: Associating others in worship resembles withholding worship from God during the times devoted to partners, so avoiding association amounts to the opposite of shirk.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r4.anchor: ولكن لما كان الإشراك للمعبود في العبادة يشبه ترك العبادة جعل ترك الإشراك مساويا لنقيض العبادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r5.claim: Nidd means an equal or peer in glory or warfare.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r5.anchor: والند بكسر النون المساوي والمماثل في أمر من مجد أو حرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r6.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r6.claim: Some lexicographers require a nidd to be a hostile opponent, deriving it from flight and resistance; Ibn ʿĀshūr says hostility is not essential because peerhood conventionally entails rivalry, and nidd may be a fixed noun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r6.anchor: بعض أهل اللغة أن يكون مناوئا أي معاديا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r7.claim: Calling the idols peers is ironic: they are not God's equals, but the pagans' conduct treats them as such, exposing inconsistency between actions and professed beliefs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r7.anchor: والمعنى لاتثبتوا لله أندادا تجعلونها جعلا وهي ليست أندادا وسماها أندادا تعريضا بزعمهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r8.claim: The pagans claimed their gods were intercessors and that they worshipped them only to draw near to God, though they also called God the creator of the gods.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r8.anchor: وإن كان أهل الجاهلية يقولون إن الآلاهة شفعاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r9.claim: Their worship, shrine visits, vows, and festivals displaced worship of God; conduct therefore reveals practical equality despite their claims, including the contradictory talbiya that excepts an owned partner.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p334/r9.anchor: لكنهم لما عبدوها ونسوا بعبادتها والسعي إليها والنذور عندها وإقامة المواسم حولها عبادة الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r1.claim: The circumstantial clause leaves the object of taʿlamūn unstated because the verb asserts the subjects' state of being knowledgeable rather than taking an object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r1.anchor: متروك لأن الفعل لم يقصد تعليقه بمفعول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r2.claim: Here knowledge means sound, mature judgment, contrasted with ignorance, as in 39:9.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r2.anchor: والمراد بالعلم هنا العقل التام وهو رجحان الرأي المقابل عندهم بالجهل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r3.claim: The clause is the focus of the prohibition: affirming their capacity while rebuking shirk both stirs their ambition and reproaches their neglected reasoning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r3.anchor: وقد جعلت هاته الحال محط النهي والنفي تمليحا في الكلام للجمع بين التوبيخ وإثارة الهمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr draws an educational lesson: recognize a learner's remaining strengths to avoid despair, while also pointing out deficiencies that motivate further effort.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r4.anchor: أن يعمد المربي فيجمع لمن يربيه بين ما يدل على بقية كمال فيه حتى لا يقتل همته باليأس من كماله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r5.claim: The wording implies that the pagans knew God had no equal but feigned blindness and forgot this when they said there was a partner belonging to Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p335/r5.anchor: إلى أنهم يعلمون أن الله لا ند له ولكنهم تعاموا وتناسوا فقالوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r3.claim: The reasons for worship in 2:21–22 are paired with reasons against disbelief here: creation and provision are followed by life, death, resurrection, return, and creation of what is on earth, preparing for the account of human origins and stages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r3.anchor: ومن بديع المناسبة وفائق التفنن في ضروب الانتقالات في المخاطبات أن كانت العلل التي قرن بها الأمر بعبادة الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid says يا أيها الناس occurs in Meccan revelations, whereas يا أيها الذين آمنوا occurs in Medinan ones.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يا أيها الناس حيث وقع في القرآن مكي، ويا أيها الذين آمنوا مدني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya notes that this sūra was already established as entirely Medinan, so يا أيها الناس can occur in a Medinan revelation; he accepts Mujāhid’s claim for يا أيها الذين آمنوا.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r4.anchor: قد تقدم في أول السورة أنها كلها مدنية، وقد يجيء في المدني يا أيها الناس، وأما قوله في يا أيها الذين آمنوا فصحيح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r11.claim: The second الذي is accusative by coordination with the preceding الذي, though it may be nominative as a detached clause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r11.anchor: وقوله تعالى: الذي جعل نصب على إتباع الذي المتقدم، ويصح أن يكون مرفوعا على القطع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya considers Makkī’s analyses, supplying an implicit أعني or making الذي the object of تتقون, weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r12.anchor: وما ذكر مكي من إضمار أعني أو مفعول ب تتقون فضعيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r13.claim: Jaʿala means “made” or “rendered” here, since it governs two objects.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r13.anchor: وجعل بمعنى صير في هذه الآية لتعديها إلى مفعولين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r14.claim: Firāsh means a place you spread out on and settle upon; mountains and seas also serve the earth’s habitability, like tent pegs and navigable routes to other benefits.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r14.anchor: وفراشا معناه تفترشونها وتستقرون عليها، وما في الأرض مما ليس بفراش كالجبال والبحار فهو من مصالح ما يفترش منها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r15.claim: Samāʾ is explained either as a singular whose plural is سماوات, or as a collective whose singular is سماوة; anything elevated above one is called sky, including the air.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r15.anchor: والسماء قيل هو اسم مفرد جمعه «سماوات» ، وقيل هو جمع واحده «سماوة»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r16.claim: Anything elevated above a person is called sky, and the air itself is also called sky.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r16.anchor: كل ما ارتفع عليك في الهواء فهو سماء، والهواء نفسه علوا يقال له «سماء»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r1.claim: A hadith cited here describes Adam as sixty cubits tall, illustrating the use of sky for the elevated air.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r1.anchor: «خلق الله آدم طوله في السماء ستون ذراعا»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r2.claim: The word samāʾ derives from sumū and its related forms, denoting height.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r2.anchor: «خلق الله آدم طوله في السماء ستون ذراعا» ، واللفظة من السمو وتصاريفه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r3.claim: Calling the sky a structure is an analogy to something familiar, as in the linked description of heaven being built.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى: بناء تشبيه بما يفهم، كما قال تعالى: والسماء بنيناها بأيد [الذاريات: 47]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r4.speaker: بعض الصحابة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r4.claim: Some Companions say God built the sky over the earth like a dome.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r4.anchor: وقال بعض الصحابة: «بناها على الأرض كالقبة»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r5.claim: Here السماء means clouds, a figurative use based on their closeness to the sky; rain was also called “sky” by association, as the cited verse shows.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r5.anchor: وأنزل من السماء يريد السحاب، سمي بذلك تجوزا لما كان يلي السماء ويقاربها وقد سموا المطر سماء للمجاورة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r6.claim: The cited poem says that when “the sky” (rain) falls, they graze it; رعيناه is also figurative, since rain produces the grass called sky.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r6.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر: [الوافر] . إذا نزل السماء بأرض قوم ... رعيناه وإن كانوا غضابا فتجوز أيضا في رعيناه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r7.claim: The form māʾ comes from māh, as shown by its plurals مياه and أمواه and diminutive مويه.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r7.anchor: وأصل ماء موه يدل على ذلك قولهم في الجمع مياه وأمواه، وفي التصغير مويه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r8.claim: The fruits are called provision before anyone owns them because they are prepared for possible benefit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r8.anchor: وانطلق اسم الرزق على ما يخرج من الثمرات قبل التملك، أي هي معدة أن يصح الانتفاع بها فهي رزق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r9.speaker: المعتزلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r9.claim: The verse is used against the Muʿtazilite claim that provision must be capable of ownership and that unlawful things are not provision.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r9.anchor: ورد بهذه الآية بعض الناس قول المعتزلة إن الرزق ما يصح تملكه، وليس الحرام برزق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r10.claim: The singular of andād is nidd: a counterpart or peer, whether likeness, opposite, or adversary; resistance and comparison entail a kind of equivalence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r10.anchor: وواحد الأندادند، وهو المقاوم والمضاهي كان مثلا أو خلافا أو ضدا، ومن حيث قاوم وضاهى فقد حصلت مماثلة ما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة معمر والمفضل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r11.claim: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar and al-Mufaḍḍal identify a peer with an opposite.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r11.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة معمر والمفضل: الضد الند، وهذا التخصيص منهما تمثيل لا حصر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says their equation is an example, not an exhaustive definition of nidd.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r12.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة معمر والمفضل: الضد الند، وهذا التخصيص منهما تمثيل لا حصر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r13.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r13.claim: One group says the address is to all polytheists; their knowledge is specifically that God created, sent water, and brought forth provision, without denying their general ignorance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r13.anchor: فقالت جماعة من المفسرين: المخاطب جميع المشركين. فقوله على هذا: وأنتم تعلمون يريد العلم الخاص

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r14.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r14.claim: Another view makes the addressees the unbelieving Israelites, who know from their scriptures that God has no peer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r14.anchor: وقيل المراد كفار بني إسرائيل، فالمعنى تعلمون من الكتب التي عندكم، أن الله لا ند له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r15.speaker: ابن فورك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r15.claim: Ibn Fūrak says the verse may also address believers: do not apostatize and make peers for God after knowing His oneness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r15.anchor: وقال ابن فورك: «يحتمل أن تتناول الآية المؤمنين» ، فالمعنى لا ترتدوا أيها المؤمنون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r16.claim: The verse shows that God’s blessings suffice humanity; one who makes himself dependent on another person out of greed, hope, or worldly desire follows the path of assigning God a peer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r16.anchor: وهذه الآية تعطي أن الله تعالى أغنى الإنسان بنعمه هذه عن كل مخلوق، فمن أحوج نفسه إلى بشر مثله بسبب الحرص والأمل والرغبة في زخرف الدنيا، فقد أخذ بطرق من جعل لله ندا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r1.claim: One proposed etymology links ard, earth, to breadth, as in the phrase for a wound that has spread.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r1.anchor: إنما سميت الأرض أرضا لسعتها من قولهم أرضت القرحة إذا اتسعت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r2.claim: Another explanation is that earth is so named because it lies below the sky; anything lower is called earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r2.anchor: وقيل لانحطاطها عن السماء وكل ما سفل أرض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r3.claim: A third explanation connects earth's name with people treading or flattening it beneath their feet.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r4.claim: The sky is named for its height; al-Zajjaj says anything raised above earth is called a building.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج وكل ما علا على الأرض فاسمه بناء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says anything raised above the earth is called binaʾ, a structure or building.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج وكل ما علا على الأرض فاسمه بناء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets binaʾ here as a roof.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس البناء هاهنا بمعنى السقف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r7.claim: Here “from the sky” means from the clouds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r7.anchor: يعني من السحاب ماء معنى المطر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r9.claim: Andad means partners or equals; one counterpart may be called the nad of another.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r9.anchor: يعني شركاء أمثالا يقال هذا ند هذا ونديده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the andad as idols.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r10.anchor: وفيما أريد بالأنداد هاهنا قولان أحدهما الأصنام قاله ابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r11.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r11.claim: Al-Suddi identifies them as men whom people obey in disobedience to God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r11.anchor: والثاني رجال كانوا يطيعونهم في معصية الله قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r12.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r12.claim: They understand “you know” to mean that people know God created the sky, sent down water, and did the acts just described.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r12.anchor: هذا المعنى مروي عن ابن عباس وقتادة و مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r13.claim: A second Ibn Abbas interpretation says the People of the Book know these claims are absent from their Torah and Gospel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r13.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أيضا وهو يخرج على قول من قال الخطاب لأهل الكتاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r14.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r14.claim: Mujahid says they know that God has no equal.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r14.anchor: والثالث وأنتم تعلمون أنه لا ند له قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r15.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r15.claim: Ibn Qutayba says knowledge here means reason or intellect.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r15.anchor: العلم هاهنا بمعنا العقل قاله ابن قتبية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r16.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r16.claim: Ali ibn Ubayd Allah says they know that no one but God can perform the acts described.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r16.anchor: والخامس وأنتم تعلمون أنه لا يقدر على فعل ما ذكره أحد سواه ذكره شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r17.speaker: أبو محمد بن الخشاب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r17.claim: Abu Muhammad ibn al-Khashshab says they know the supposed partners are stones.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p48/r17.anchor: وأنتم تعلمون أنها حجارة سمعته من الشسيخ أبي محمد بن الخشاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r2.claim: God made earth a level bed anchored by high mountains, heaven a roof, and clouds a source of timely rain that produces food for people and livestock; 21:32 and 40:64 parallel this description.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r2.anchor: الأرض فراشا، أي: مهدا كالفراش مقررة موطأة مثبتة بالرواسي الشامخات، {والسماء بناء} وهو السقف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r3.claim: As creator, provider, and owner of the world and its inhabitants, God alone deserves worship and must have no associate.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r3.anchor: ومضمونه: أنه الخالق الرازق مالك الدار، وساكنيها، ورازقهم، فبهذا يستحق أن يعبد وحده ولا يشرك به غيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r4.claim: Ibn Masud asks the Prophet for the greatest sin; he answers, assigning a partner to God who created you.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r4.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عن ابن مسعود، قال: قلت: يا رسول الله، أي الذنب أعظم؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r5.claim: In the report from Muadh, the Prophet says God’s right over servants is that they worship Him and associate nothing with Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r5.anchor: يا رسول الله، أي الذنب أعظم؟ قال: "أن تجعل لله ندا، وهو خلقك" الحديث (4) . وكذا حديث معاذ: "أتدري ما حق الله على عباده؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r6.claim: The Prophet forbids saying ‘as God and so-and-so willed’; say ‘as God willed, then so-and-so willed.’
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث الآخر: "لا يقولن أحدكم: ما شاء الله وشاء فلان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r7.speaker: الطفيل بن سخبرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r7.claim: Tufayl reports a dream in which Jews and Christians objected to Muslims’ phrasing ‘as God and Muhammad willed’; he told the Prophet, who then forbade it and commanded ‘God alone.’
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r7.anchor: عن الطفيل بن سخبرة، أخي عائشة أم المؤمنين لأمها، قال: رأيت فيما يرى النائم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas addresses worship to both disbelievers and hypocrites, calling them to worship the Lord who created them and those before them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: قال الله تعالى: {يا أيها الناس اعبدوا ربكم}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, as does Qatada, explains that people must not associate powerless partners with God, since they know He alone provides and the Messenger’s call to monotheism is true.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r2.anchor: وبه عن ابن عباس: {فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا وأنتم تعلمون} أي: لا تشركوا بالله غيره من الأنداد التي لا تنفع ولا تضر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas calls shirk subtler than an ant on a dark stone at night, including oaths by others’ lives, crediting a dog or ducks with protection, and saying ‘as God and you willed’ or ‘if not for God and so-and-so.’
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r3.anchor: حدثنا عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، في قول الله، عز وجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r4.claim: When a man says ‘as God and you willed,’ the Prophet asks whether he has made him God’s equal and instructs him to say ‘God alone.’
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث: أن رجلا قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r5.claim: Another Prophetic report praises the people except that they assign equals when saying ‘as God and so-and-so willed.’
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r5.anchor: قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما شاء الله وشئت، فقال: "أجعلتني لله ندا". وفي الحديث الآخر: "نعم القوم أنتم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r6.claim: Abu al-Aliya, al-Rabi, Qatada, al-Suddi, Abu Malik, and Ismail ibn Abi Khalid explain andad as equals or partners.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r6.anchor: أبو العالية: {فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا} أي عدلاء شركاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir says these teachings preserve and protect the sanctity of divine oneness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p195/r7.anchor: وهذا كله صيانة، وحماية لجناب التوحيد، والله أعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p196/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p196/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p196/r1.claim: Mujahid says they know from the Torah and Gospel that God is one.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p196/r1.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا وأنتم تعلمون} قال: تعلمون أنه إله واحد في التوراة والإنجيل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p196/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p196/r2.speaker: الحارث الأشعري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p196/r2.claim: Al-Harith al-Ashʿari reports that God charged John to teach Israel five practices: worship alone, prayer without turning, fasting, charity, and abundant remembrance, illustrated by loyalty to one’s master, divine attention, musk, ransom, and refuge from Satan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p196/r2.anchor: حدثنا يحيى بن أبي كثير، عن زيد بن سلام، عن جده ممطور، عن الحارث الأشعري، أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r1.claim: The Prophet adds five duties: congregation, hearing, obedience, migration, and jihad; abandoning the community or invoking pagan identity incurs a threat, and Muslims should be called by God’s names even if they pray and fast.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r1.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "وأنا آمركم بخمس الله أمرني بهن: الجماعة، والسمع، والطاعة، والهجرة، والجهاد في سبيل الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir grades the report hasan and identifies its relevance here as the command to worship God alone because He created and provided for people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r2.anchor: هذا حديث حسن، والشاهد منه في هذه الآية قوله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r3.claim: The verses establish worship of God alone and, a fortiori, prove the Creator exists: reflecting on the ordered, varied, useful upper and lower worlds reveals His power, wisdom, knowledge, and sovereignty.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r3.anchor: وهذه الآية دالة على توحيده تعالى بالعبادة وحده لا شريك له، وقد استدل به كثير من المفسرين كالرازي وغيره على وجود الصانع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r4.speaker: أعرابي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r4.claim: A Bedouin argues that dung points to a camel and footprints to a traveler, so a constellated sky, furrowed earth, and wavy seas point to the Subtle, All-Aware Creator.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r4.anchor: كما قال بعض الأعراب، وقد سئل: ما الدليل على وجود الرب تعالى؟ فقال: يا سبحان الله، إن البعرة لتدل على البعير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r5.speaker: مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r5.claim: Al-Razi transmits that Imam Malik answered Harun al-Rashid’s question about the Creator by pointing to the diversity of languages, voices, and tones.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r5.anchor: وحكى فخر الدين عن الإمام مالك أن الرشيد سأله عن ذلك فاستدل باختلاف اللغات والأصوات والنغمات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r6.claim: Abu Hanifa compares belief in an unguided universe to believing that a laden ship sails itself; the skeptics concede the absurdity, then accept the same reasoning about creation and convert.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r6.anchor: وعن أبي حنيفة أن بعض الزنادقة سألوه عن وجود الباري تعالى، فقال لهم: دعوني فإني مفكر في أمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r1.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r1.claim: Al-Shafiʿi points to one mulberry leaf producing silk, honey, dung, and musk through different animals as evidence for the Creator.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r1.anchor: وعن الشافعي: أنه سئل عن وجود الصانع، فقال: هذا ورق التوت طعمه واحد تأكله الدود فيخرج منه الإبريسم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r2.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r2.claim: Ahmad compares an egg to a sealed, shining fortress that splits and yields a hearing, seeing, beautifully formed, melodious creature, the chicken.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r2.anchor: وعن الإمام أحمد بن حنبل أنه سئل عن ذلك فقال: هاهنا حصن حصين أملس، ليس له باب ولا منفذ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r3.speaker: أبو نواس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r3.claim: Abu Nuwas’s poem reads plants and their crafted forms as signs that the Maker has no partner.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r3.anchor:
وسئل أبو نواس عن ذلك فأنشد:
تأمل في نبات الأرض وانظر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r4.speaker: ابن المعتز
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz’s verses ask how God can be disobeyed or denied when every thing bears a sign that He is One.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r4.anchor:
وقال ابن المعتز:
فيا عجبا كيف يعصى الإله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r5.claim: Contemplating the high heavens and stars, surrounding seas, diverse mountains, rivers, animals, and varied plants despite shared soil and water demonstrates the Creator’s power, wisdom, mercy, and kindness; the mountain colors are cited at 35:27–28.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r5.anchor: وكذلك هذه الأنهار السارحة من قطر إلى قطر لمنافع العباد وما زرأ في الأرض من الحيوانات المتنوعة والنبات المختلف الطعوم

JISHUMI:v1p281/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r1.speaker: بعضهم
JISHUMI:v1p281/r1.claim: The agreed reading has the plural andādan; some read the singular niddan.
JISHUMI:v1p281/r1.anchor: المجمع عليه في القراءة أندادا على الجمع، وعن بعضهم ندا على الواحد

JISHUMI:v1p281/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p281/r2.claim: Jaʿala, created, and originated are treated as synonymous verbs here.

JISHUMI:v1p281/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p281/r3.claim: Firāsh, mihād, and bisāṭ are near-synonyms; firāsh is the verbal noun of spreading a bed or carpet.
JISHUMI:v1p281/r3.anchor: والفراش والمهاد والبساط نظائر، والفرش مصدر فرش يفرش فرشا

JISHUMI:v1p281/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r4.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v1p281/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the earth is a spread for people to build upon and that anything on earth can be called a structure; building joins something to a foundation.
JISHUMI:v1p281/r4.anchor: الأرض بساط الأنام للبناء، قال الزجاج: كل ما على الأرض فاسمه بناء

JISHUMI:v1p281/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p281/r5.claim: Water's old form is maw; its plural is amwāh and its diminutive muwayh.
JISHUMI:v1p281/r5.anchor: والماء معروف، وأصله موه، ولذلك يجمع على أمواه، ويصغر على مويه

JISHUMI:v1p281/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r6.speaker: علي بن عيسى
JISHUMI:v1p281/r6.claim: ʿAlī b. ʿĪsā defines water as a flowing substance on which animal life depends.
JISHUMI:v1p281/r6.anchor: ويحد الماء بأنه جوهر سيال به قوام الحيوان، عن علي بن عيسى

JISHUMI:v1p281/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p281/r7.claim: Jishumi rejects proposed definitions of water because water is more familiar than anything used to define it.
JISHUMI:v1p281/r7.anchor: والتحديد في مثل هذا باطل؛ لأن الغرض بالتحديد التعريف، وكل شيء يحد به الماء فالماء أعرف وأشهر منه

JISHUMI:v1p281/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p281/r8.claim: إخراج is the opposite of إدخال; kharāj is named for money that comes out annually, and the root extends to revealing evidence or moving from unbelief to faith.
JISHUMI:v1p281/r8.anchor: والإخراج نقيض الإدخال، خرج يخرج، وأخرجه غيره، وسمي الخراج كذلك؛ لأنه يخرج في كل سنة

JISHUMI:v1p281/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p281/r9.claim: Thamara is a tree's produce; thamarāt is its plural, and a tree is fruitful when it bears fruit.
JISHUMI:v1p281/r9.anchor: والثمرة: حمل الشجرة، والثمرات الجمع، أثمرت الشجرة فهي مثمرة إذا حملت الثمرة

JISHUMI:v1p281/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p281/r10.claim: Nidd means a counterpart or likeness; its root family denotes a match or rival.
JISHUMI:v1p281/r10.anchor: والند: المثل، وقيل: الضد، عن أبي عبيدة، وقيل: حقيقة المثل المناوئ

JISHUMI:v1p281/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
JISHUMI:v1p281/r11.claim: Abū ʿUbayda also takes nidd to mean an opposite.

JISHUMI:v1p281/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p281/r12.claim: Alladhī is accusative as an adjective of rabbikum: worship your Lord, the one who made the earth and sky for you.
JISHUMI:v1p281/r12.anchor: (الذي): موضعه نصب؛ لأنه من صفة الرب، تقديره: اعبدوا ربكم الذي جعل لكم

JISHUMI:v1p281/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p281/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed concerning the two groups of unbelievers and hypocrites; Jishumi prefers this over the view that it concerns Jews.
JISHUMI:v1p281/r13.anchor: قيل: نزلت في الفريقين من الكفار والمنافقين، عن ابن عباس، وقيل: في اليهود

JISHUMI:v1p281/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r14.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v1p281/r14.claim: Mujāhid explains that they knew the truth from the Torah and Gospel.
JISHUMI:v1p281/r14.anchor: (تعلمون) يعني: تعلمون أن ذلك في التوراة والإنجيل، عن مجاهد

JISHUMI:v1p281/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p281/r15.claim: After pointing to human creation, God turns to heaven and earth as evidence of divine oneness and craftsmanship and as reminders of blessings.
JISHUMI:v1p281/r15.anchor: لما ذكر الله تعالى الاحتجاج على الكفار بدأ بأنفسهم منبها على ما فيها من عجيب خلقه

JISHUMI:v1p281/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p281/r16.claim: The earth is a stable spread that lets people move about on it, and the sky is a raised, constructed roof.
JISHUMI:v1p281/r16.anchor: يعني: بساطا ساكنا دائم السكون ليمكنكم التصرف عليه، والسماء بناء يعني سقفا مرفوعا مبنيا

JISHUMI:v1p281/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r17.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p281/r17.claim: Rain comes from the direction of the sky, meaning clouds; another view takes it as literally from the sky.
JISHUMI:v1p281/r17.anchor: قيل: من نحو السماء، يعني: من السحاب، وقيل: من السماء حقيقة

JISHUMI:v1p281/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p281/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p281/r18.claim: God brings fruits out through rainwater as provision for people.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r1.claim: Creation is ordered from living humans, to their earthly dwelling, to the sky above, then rain and fruits; these blessings invite gratitude and reflection leading to recognition of the one Creator and rejection of equals.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r1.anchor: قدم سبحانه من موجبات عبادته وملزمات حق الشكر له خلقهم أحياء قادرين أولا لأنه سابقة أصول النعم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r2.claim: The relative clause may be accusative as an adjective to الذي خلقكم, accusative for praise, or nominative as a new subject; the nominative also conveys praise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r2.anchor: والموصول مع صلته إما أن يكون في محل النصب وصفا كالذي خلقكم أو على المدح والتعظيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r3.speaker: يزيد الشامي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r3.claim: Yazīd al-Shāmī reads بساطا in place of فراشا.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r4.speaker: طلحة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r4.claim: Talḥa reads مهادا in place of فراشا.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r5.claim: Earth is a bed, carpet, or resting place because people sit, sleep, and move about on it as on bedding.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r5.anchor: ومعنى جعلها فراشا وبساطا ومهادا للناس أنهم يقعدون عليها وينامون ويتقلبون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r6.claim: The wording does not prove a flat earth: people can spread bedding on either a plane or a sphere because Earth's size and distance hide its curvature.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r6.anchor: ليس فيه إلا أن الناس يفترشونها كما يفعلون بالمفارش وسواء كانت على شكل السطح أو شكل الكرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r7.claim: Bināʾ is originally a verbal noun for building and also names the resulting structure, such as a house, dome, tent, or awning; Arabs called their tents abniya.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r7.anchor: والبناء مصدر سمي به المبني بيتا كان أو قبة أو خباء أو طرافا وأبنية العرب أخبيتهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r8.claim: The idiom بنى على امرأته comes from erecting a new tent for a wedding.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124#2/r8.anchor: ومنه بنى على امرأته لأنهم كانوا اذا تزوجوا ضربوا عليها خباء جديدا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125/r1.claim: Water is the made cause and material for fruits, like semen for offspring; God can create without causes, but gradual stages renew lessons, sound reflection, and reassurance in His power and wisdom.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125/r1.anchor: المعنى أنه جعل الماء سببا في خروجها ومادة لها كماء الفحل في خلق الولد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125/r2.claim: Min is partitive: only some water, fruits, and provision are meant, as confirmed by other verses and the indefinite nouns around it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125/r2.anchor: للتبعيض بشهادة قوله ﴿ فأخرجنا به من كل الثمرات ﴾ الأعراف 57

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125/r3.claim: Min may instead be explanatory, as in “I spent a thousand of the dirhams.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون لبيان كقولك أنفقت من الدراهم ألفا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r1.claim: If min is partitive, rizqan is an object of purpose; if min explains the category, rizqan is the direct object of أخرج.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r1.anchor: للتبعيض كان انتصابه بأنه مفعول له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r2.claim: One explanation for الثمرات rather than ثمر or ثمار is that a plural can denote the many individual fruits of a garden collectively; the singular reading supports this.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r2.anchor: أن يقصد بالثمرات جماعة الثمرة التي في قولك فلان أدركت ثمره بستانه تريد ثماره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r3.claim: Another explanation is that plural forms can substitute for one another because all express plurality, as in other Qur'anic and legal usages.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r3.anchor: والثاني أن الجموع يتعاور بعضها موقع بعض لالتقائها في الجمعية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r4.speaker: محمد بن السميفع
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Sumayfa reads من الثمرة in the singular, supporting the collective-fruit explanation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r4.anchor: ويعضد الوجه الأول قراءة محمد بن السميفع من الثمرة على التوحيد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r5.claim: Lakum is an adjective to rizq if rizq means food or goods; if it means the act of provision, lakum is its object.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p125#2/r5.anchor: صفة جارية على الرزق إن أريد به العين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r1.claim: One parse attaches فلا تجعلوا to the command عبادوا: worship your Lord and do not assign Him equals, since monotheism is worship's foundation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r1.anchor: قلت فيه ثلاثة اوجه ان يتعلق بالأمر اي اعبدوا ربكم فلا تجعلوا له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r2.claim: A second parse attaches it to لعل with a subjunctive result, as in “so I may reach ... and see”; the meaning is that creation aims at piety and fear of punishment, not resemblance to creatures.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r2.anchor: أو بلعل على ان ينتصب تجعلوا انتصاب فاطلع في قوله عز وجل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r3.claim: A third parse attaches the prohibition to the clause الذي جعل لكم when it is a new subject: these signs testify to oneness, so do not take partners.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r3.anchor: أو بالذي جعل لكم إذا رفعته على الابتداء أي هو الذي خصكم بهذه الآيات العظيمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r4.claim: Nidd means an equal, specifically a rival or opponent; the root nadda means to flee, and nadadtu denotes opposing someone.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r4.anchor: والند المثل ولا يقال الا للمثل المخالف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r5.speaker: جرير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r5.claim: Jarīr's verse uses ندا for a rival, as lexical evidence for the word's sense.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r5.anchor: قال جرير ( أتيما يجعلون الي ندا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r6.claim: The phrase “no equal or opposite” denies both anything that could replace God and anything that could oppose Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r6.anchor: ومعنى قولهم ليس لله ند ولا ضد نفي ما يسده مسده ونفي ما ينافيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r7.claim: Although polytheists claimed idols were intercessors rather than God's rivals, worshipping and naming them as gods made their conduct like belief in equals; the wording sarcastically shames them for multiplying equals for the One who can have none.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r7.anchor: لما تقربوا إليها وعظموها وسموها آلهة أشبهت حالهم حال من يعتقد أنها آلهة مثله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r8.speaker: زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r8.claim: When leaving his people's religion, Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl posed the choice between one God and a thousand gods, underscoring monotheism.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r8.anchor: وفي ذلك قال زيد بن عمرو ابن نفيل حين فارق دين قومه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r9.speaker: محمد بن السميفع
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r9.claim: Ibn al-Sumayfa reads ندا in the singular.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126/r9.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن السميفع فلا تجعلوا لله ندا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126#2/r1.claim: The omitted object of “you know” makes the rebuke stronger: they are addressed as people of discernment and knowledge.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126#2/r1.anchor: متروك كأنه قيل وأنتم من اهل العلم والمعرفة والتوبيخ فيه آكد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126#2/r2.claim: Arabs, especially Quraysh and Kinana in the sanctuary, were renowned for sound judgment, deep knowledge, and keen understanding.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126#2/r2.anchor: وهكذا كانت العرب خصوصا ساكنو الحرم من قريش وكنانة لا يصطلي بنارهم في استحكام المعرفة بالأمور

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126#2/r3.claim: Despite their discernment, making idols partners of God is the height of ignorance and foolishness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126#2/r3.anchor: ثم إن ما أنتم عليه في امر ديانتكم من جعل الأصنام لله اندادا هو غاية الجهل ونهاية سخافة العقل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126#2/r4.claim: The implied knowledge may be that God has no equal, that He differs greatly from idols, or that they cannot do what He does.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p126#2/r4.anchor: ويجوز ان يقدر وأنتم تعلمون انه لا يماثل أو وأنتم تعلمون ما بينه وبينها من التفاوت

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.claim: Ibn Masud explains andad as peers or equals.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.anchor: أحدها : أن الأنداد الأكفاء , وهذا قول ابن مسعود .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains andad as likenesses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.anchor: والثاني : الأشباه , وهو قول ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada understand the clause as: you know that God created you.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r4.anchor: أحدها : وأنتم تعلمون أن الله خلقكم , وهذا قول ابن عباس وقتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r5.claim: Mujahid takes it to mean that people know God has no equal or opposite.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r5.anchor: والثاني : معناه وأنتم تعلمون أنه لا ند له ولا ضد , وهذا قول مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r6.claim: The phrase can also mean that people reason, with knowledge used in the sense of intellect.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p83#2/r6.anchor: والثالث : معناه وأنتم تعقلون فعبر عن العقل بالعلم .

BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r1.speaker: أهل اللغة
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r1.claim: The language authorities call earth the world's carpet and give its circumference as 24,000 farsakhs, each three miles; Bursevi also records the detailed measures of the arm and barley-grain.
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r1.anchor: قال أهل اللغة الأرض بساط العالم وبسيطها من حيث يحيط بها البحر الذي هو البحر المحيط أربعة وعشرون ألف فرسخ كل فرسخ ثلاثة أميال

BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r2.claim: Al-Malakut divides the distances among the Sudanese, white lands, Persians, and Arabs as 12,000, 8,000, 3,000, and 1,000 farsakhs respectively.
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r2.anchor: فللسودان اثنا عشر ألف فرسخ وللبياض ثمانية وللفرس ثلاثة وللعرب ألف كذا في "كتاب الملكوت"

BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r3.claim: Al-Malakut places the center of the inhabited earth at the Kaaba and the center of all earth, inhabited and barren, at Qubbat al-Ard, where seasons and day and night remain balanced.
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r3.anchor: وسمت وسط الأرض المسكونة حضرة الكعبة وأما وسط الأرض كلها عامرها وخرابها فهو الموضع الذي يسمى قبة الأرض

BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r4.speaker: علي
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r4.claim: ʿAli explains the name earth by saying it consumes what lies in its interior.
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r4.anchor: وروي عن علي كرم الله وجهه أنه قال : إنما سميت الأرض أرضا لأنها تتأرض ما في بطنها

BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r5.claim: Another etymology says earth is called so because hooves and feet wear or tread upon it.
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم لأنها تتأرض بالحوافر والأقدام

BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r6.claim: Making earth a bed means exposing some of it from water and giving it a middle firmness and softness fit for sitting and sleeping, like a spread carpet; this does not require a flat surface, since its great spherical form allows it to be spread.
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r6.anchor: ومعنى جعلها فراشا جعل بعضها بارزا من الماء مع اقتضاء طبعها الرسوب وجعلها متوسطة بين الصلابة واللين صالحة للقعود عليها والنوم فيها

BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r7.speaker: أبو الليث
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r7.claim: The sky is what rises above and shades people, built as a dome; each heaven lies over another, and the edges of the lowest heaven adjoin the earth, according to Abu al-Layth.
BURSEVI:v1p58#2/r7.anchor: {السماء} وهو ما علاك وأظلك {بناء} قبة مضروبة عليكم وكل سماء مطبقة على الأخرى مثل القبة

BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r1.claim: The water is rain descending from heaven onto clouds and from them to earth, rejecting the claim that it comes from the sea.
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r1.anchor: {وأنزل من السمآء مآء} أي : مطرا ينحدر منها على السحاب ومنه على الأرض

BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r2.speaker: التيسير
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r2.claim: Here fruits include all edible produce that grows from earth and trees, such as grains and fruit.
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r2.anchor: {من الثمرات} هي ههنا المأكولات كلها من الحبوب والفواكه وغيرها مما يخرج من الأرض والشجر كما في "التيسير"

BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r3.claim: God grows produce through the water: its active force interacts with earth's receptive force, like a marriage of sky and earth yielding fruit as offspring.
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r3.anchor: وذلك بأن أودع في الماء قوة فاعلية وفي الأرض قوة منفعلة فتولد من تفاعلهما أصناف الثمار فبين المظلة والمقلة شبه عقد النكاح

BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r4.claim: Min is explanatory and rizq means food for people and fodder for their animals; these gifts should lead them to recognize God as creator and provider and affirm His oneness.
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r4.anchor: ومن للبيان ورزقا أي : طعاما وعلفا لكم ولدوابكم والمعنى أن الله تعالى أنعم عليكم بذلك كله لتعرفوه

BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r5.claim: Andad is the plural of nidd, a counterpart: do not worship supposed equals along with God or call them His partners.
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r5.anchor: {فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا} جمع ند وهو المثل أي : أمثالا تعبدونهم كعبادة الله يعني لا تقولوا له شركاء

BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas warns against attributing protection to others with statements such as that without a certain person or the barking dog, harm or theft would have occurred.
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : لا تقولوا لولا فلان لأصابني كذا ولولا كلبنا يصيح على الباب لسرق متاعنا

BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r7.claim: The Prophet warns against saying law, since hypocrites said that those who stayed with them would not have died or been killed.
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r7.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : "إياكم ولو فإنه من كلام المنافقين قالوا لو كانوا عندنا ما ماتوا وما قتلوا"

BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r8.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r8.claim: Saʿdi's couplet says that honor and glory or abasement and bondage are known to come from God, not from people such as ʿAmr and Zayd.
BURSEVI:v1p58#3/r8.anchor: قال السعدي : اكر عز وجاهست اكر ذل وقيد من أزحق شناسم نه از عمرو وزيد

BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r1.claim: People know God created them, their predecessors, heaven, earth, and provision, whereas idols neither harm nor benefit; the knowledge makes worship of rivals indefensible.
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r1.anchor: {وأنتم تعلمون} أن الله هو الذي خلقكم ومن قبلكم وخلق السماء والأرض وخلق الأرزاق

BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r2.claim: The universal favor prompts a question at resurrection: if God says He did all this for you, what will you say you did for Him?
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r2.anchor: والوعظ الكلي أنه قال في الآية : {جعل لكم} وقال : {رزقا لكم} فلو قال لك في القيامة

BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r3.speaker: أبو الحسين النوري
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r3.claim: When al-Shibli's sermon on the terrors of resurrection made listeners weep, Abu al-Husayn al-Nuri said not to frighten them: the reckoning is two questions, whether one was for God and whom one served.
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r3.anchor: وعن الشبلي رحمه الله أنه وعظ يوما الناس فأبكاهم لما ذكر من القيامة وأهوالها فمر بهم أبو الحسين النوري قال : لا تفزعهم

BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r4.claim: The verse calls for sincere worship: abandon regard for all besides God and witness the creator of night and day.
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r4.anchor: وأفادت الآية أنه ينبغي الإخلاص في العبادة بترك ملاحظة الأغيار وبشهود خالق الليل والنهار

BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r5.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r5.claim: Saʿdi's couplet stresses that without the root of sincerity, one is deprived at the door of devotion.
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r5.anchor:
قال السعدي :
جزء : 1 رقم الصفحة : 74
كرت بيخ إخلاص در بوم نيست

BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r6.claim: In advice to Muʿadh, the Prophet says seven angels existed before the heavens and earth, one gatekeeper was assigned to each heaven, and the servant's deeds ascend from morning to evening, radiant and magnified.
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r6.anchor: وفي توصية رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لمعاذ

BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r7.claim: The first heaven's gatekeeper refuses the deed and strikes its owner's face because the servant backbit people; the accompanying verse says the tongue is for gratitude, while backbiting makes one ungrateful to God.

BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r8.claim: The second heaven's gatekeeper rejects a good deed because its owner sought worldly display and prided himself over people in their gatherings.
BURSEVI:v1p58#4/r8.anchor: ثم يأتي الحفظة بعمل صالح من أعمال العبد فتزكيه وتكثره حتى تبلغ به إلى السماء الثانية فيقول لهم الملك الموكل بالسماء الثانية

BURSEVI:v1p60/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p60/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p60/r4.claim: The making of earth and heaven reveals perfect power and favor to humanity: the wording for you means they were created especially for people, and all creation is subjected to them, as 45:13 says.
BURSEVI:v1p60/r4.anchor: وأما منته على عباده فقوله تعالى : {لكم الأرض فراشا والسماء بناء} أي : خلق هذه الأشياء لكم خاصة

BURSEVI:v1p60/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p60/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p60/r5.claim: Because the heavens and earth exist for humanity, their existence follows humanity's; this explains God's command that angels prostrate to Adam and His prohibition of prostrating to anyone but God, marking Adam as most honored and followed.
BURSEVI:v1p60/r5.anchor: فكان وجود السموات والأرض تبعا لوجودهم وما كان وجوده تبعا لوجود شيء لا يكون مقصودا وجوده لذاته ولهذا السر أمر الله تعالى ملائكته بسجود آدم

BURSEVI:v1p60/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p60/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p60/r6.claim: In the inward reading, water is the Quran and its fruits are guidance, piety, light, mercy, healing, knowledge, wisdom, virtue, certainty, salvation, and every good; these grow from the hearts of God's servants.
BURSEVI:v1p60/r6.anchor: تحقيقه أن الماء هو القرآن وثمراته الهدى والتقى والنور والرحمة والشفاء والبركة واليمن والسعادة والقربة والحق اليقين

BURSEVI:v1p60/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p60/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p60/r7.claim: As physical fruit is provision for animals through their subordination to humans, the Quran's spiritual fruits are a gift grasped by minds supported by divine grace rather than illusion.
BURSEVI:v1p60/r7.anchor: فأخرج بماء القرآن هذه الثمرات من أرض قلوب عباده فكما أن الله تعالى من على عباده بإخراج الثمرات رزقا لكم

BURSEVI:v1p60#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p60#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p60#2/r1.claim: First, since God alone made people, the heavens, earth, and everything for them, they must not make rivals in worship.
BURSEVI:v1p60#2/r1.anchor: أولها : إن هذا الذي جعلت لكم من خلق أنفسكم وخلق السموات والأرض وما فيها لكم ليس من شأن أحد غيري

BURSEVI:v1p60#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p60#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p60#2/r2.claim: Second, the heavens, earth, sun, and moon are means of sustenance, but God alone provides; do not turn these means into rivals or prostrate to sun and moon.
BURSEVI:v1p60#2/r2.anchor: وثانيها : إني جعلت السموات والأرض والشمس والقمر كلها واسطة أرزاقكم وأسبابها وأنا الرزاق

BURSEVI:v1p60#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p60#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p60#2/r3.claim: Third, every creature has a share in something, and the human share is love and knowledge of God; rival beloveds sever that share and lead to ruin, as 2:165 describes.
BURSEVI:v1p60#2/r3.anchor: وثالثها : إني خلقت الموجودات وجعلت لكل شيء حظا في شيء آخر وجعلت حظ الإنسان في محبتي ومعرفتي

BURSEVI:v1p60#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p60#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p60#2/r4.claim: Bursevi identifies rivals as beloveds other than God; people who love them as they should love God lack true faith despite claiming belief, while true believers love God more intensely, as 2:165 says.
BURSEVI:v1p60#2/r4.anchor: فالأنداد هي الأحباب غير الله ثم وصف الذين لم ينقطعوا عن حظ محبته بالإيمان وقال : {والذين ءامنوا أشد حبا}
