MUQATIL:2:21-22/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r4.claim: God made the earth a spread-out carpet and the sky a roof.
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r4.anchor: يعنى بساطا، { والسماء بنآء } ، يعنى سقفا

MUQATIL:2:21-22/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r5.claim: Rain from heaven brings varieties of fruit from the earth as provision for people.
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r5.anchor: يقول: فأخرج بالمطر من الأرض أنواعا

MUQATIL:2:21-22/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r6.claim: Do not assign God partners: people know these signs are all His work, so Muqatil asks how they can worship anyone else.
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r6.anchor: وأنتم تعلمون } [آية: 22] أن هذا الذى ذكر كله من صنعه، فكيف تعبدون غيره

NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r1.anchor: أى صير ومحل الذى نصب على المدح

NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r2.claim: Alladhī may be accusative as a praise construction or nominative as the subject of an understood huwa.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r2.anchor: ومحل الذى نصب على المدح أو رفع باضمار هو

NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r3.claim: Firāsh means a spread-out resting place for sitting, sleeping, and moving; it is the second object of jaʿala.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r3.anchor: بساطا تقعدون عليها وتنامون وتتقلبون وهو مفعول ثان لجعل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r4.claim: Calling earth a spread does not prove it flat rather than spherical, since spreading and resting on it are possible on either account.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r4.anchor: وليس فيه دليل على أن الأرض مسطحة أو كرية إذ الافتراش ممكن على التقديرين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r5.claim: The sky is a roof; bināʾ is a verbal noun used for the built structure. He links this to 21:32.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r5.anchor: سقفا كقوله تعالى وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا وهو مصدر سمى به المبنى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r6.claim: The water sent down from the sky is rain.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r7.claim: Fruits emerge through God’s power, will, and creation; He makes water a cause, like reproductive fluid in a child’s creation, though He can create without causes, which He created along with matter.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r7.anchor: ولكن جعل الماء سببا فى خروجها كماء الفحل فى خلق الولد وهو قادر على إنشاء الكل بلا سبب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r8.claim: Creating things gradually through successive states and stages contains wisdom and lessons for observers with insight.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r8.anchor: ولكن له فى إنشاء الأشياء مدرجا لها من حال إلى حال وناقلا من مرتبة إلى مرتبة حكما وعبرا للنظار

NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r9.claim: Min is partitive or explanatory; rizqan is a purpose object with the partitive reading and a direct object of akhraja with the explanatory reading.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r9.anchor: للتبعيض أو للبيان ﴿ رزقا ﴾ مفعول له إن كانت للتبعيض

NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r10.claim: Thamarāt is used instead of thamar or thimār because the intended sense is a collection of fruits and plural forms interchange where both indicate collectivity.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r10.anchor: لأن المراد جماعة الثمرة و لأن الجموع يتعاور بعضها موقع بعض لالتقائها فى الجمعية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r11.claim: Lakum modifies rizq if rizq means the provision itself; if it means the act of providing, it is an object, ‘providing you.’
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r11.anchor: صفة جارية على الرزق إن أريد به العين وإن جعل اسما للمعنى فهو مفعول به

NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r12.claim: The prohibition follows the command to worship: tawḥīd is the basis of worship, so no equal or partner may be assigned to God.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r12.anchor: هو متعلق بالأمر أى اعبدوا ربكم فلا تجعلوا له أندادا لأن أصل العبادة وأساسها التوحيد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r13.claim: Alternatively, alladhī is a subject whose predicate is the prohibition; the fāʾ introduces the consequence implicit in the discourse: since God surrounded them with signs, they should not take partners.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r13.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الذى رفعا على الابتداء وخبره فلا تجعلوا ودخول الفاء لأن الكلام يتضمن الجزاء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r14.claim: A nidd is an equal, specifically an opposing rival; denying God a nidd or ḍidd denies both an equivalent substitute and an antagonist.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r14.anchor: والند المثل ولا يقال إلا للمثل المخالف والمناوئ ومعنى قولهم ليس لله ند ولا ضد نفى ما يسد مسده

NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r15.claim: The audience knows idols neither create nor provide while God is creator and provider; alternatively, the object of ‘know’ is omitted, meaning they are people of knowledge and idolatry is utter ignorance.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p26/r15.anchor: انها لا تخلق شيئا ولا ترزق والله الخالق الرازق أو مفعول تعلمون متروك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r1.claim: Here jaʿala means “made” or “rendered,” since it governs two objects.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { الذي جعل } معناه هنا صير لتعديه إلى مفعولين.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r2.claim: Jaʿala can mean “created,” as in the verses about God’s creation of livestock categories and darkness and light.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r2.anchor:
ويأتي بمعنى خلق ومنه قوله تعالى:
ما جعل الله من بحيرة ولا سائبة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r3.claim: Jaʿala can mean “called” or “named,” as in calling the Qur’an Arabic and calling a share or gender for God.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r3.anchor: ويأتي بمعنى سمى ومنه قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r4.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r4.claim: Jaʿala can mean “took” or “began to,” as a poet says he made himself grow accustomed to a bite.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r4.anchor:
ويأتي بمعنى أخذ كما قال الشاعر:
وقد جعلت نفسي تطيب لضغمة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r5.speaker: آخر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r5.claim: Some treat jaʿala as an extra particle, supported by a poet who sees double because of old age and by a reported reading of 6:1.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r5.anchor:
وقد تأتي زائدة كما قال الآخر:
وقد جعلت أرى الاثنين أربعة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r6.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r6.claim: Jaʿala and ijtʿala may have the same meaning, as the cited verse describes the night becoming like a stretched rope.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22/r6.anchor:
وجعل واجتعل بمعنى واحد قال الشاعر:
ناط أمر الضعاف واجتعل اللي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r1.claim: Farash means a spread-out bed or floor on which people lie and settle.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r1.anchor: { فراشا } أي وطاء يفترشونها ويستقرون عليها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r2.claim: Mountains, rough ground, and seas also serve human interests; mountains are stakes and seas enable useful travel.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r2.anchor: وما ليس بفراش كالجبال والأوعار والبحار فهي من مصالح ما يفترش منها لأن الجبال كالأوتاد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r3.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r3.claim: Shafiʿi jurists say one who swears not to sleep on a bed or use a lamp does not break the oath by sleeping on the ground or sitting in sunlight.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r3.anchor: قال أصحاب الشافعي: لو حلف رجل ألا يبيت على فراش أو لا يستسرج بسراج فبات على الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r4.speaker: المالكية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r4.claim: Malikis interpret oaths first by intention, cause, or context, and otherwise by customary usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r4.anchor: وأما المالكية فبنوه على أصلهم في الأيمان أنها محمولة على النية أو السبب أو البساط

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r5.claim: The sky is the earth’s roof, and whatever rises overhead and gives shade is called a sky.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى: { والسماء بناء } السماء للأرض كالسقف للبيت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r6.claim: Pausing at binaʾ is preferable to pausing at tattaqun because “who made the earth a bed” modifies the Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r6.anchor:
والوقف على «بناء» أحسن منه على «تتقون» لأن قوله:
الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r7.claim: Bana means to build a house; banaʾ can also describe a wedding consummation, originally associated with pitching a tent over the bride.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r7.anchor: ويقال: بنى فلان بيتا، وبنى على أهله بناء فيهما أي زفها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r8.claim: The passage explains forms of bana and its image of laying one brick over another until a wall stands.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r8.anchor: وبنى مقصورا شدد للكثرة، وابنتى دار وبنى بمعنى ومنه بنيان الحائط

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r9.speaker: أبو الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r9.claim: Water derives from maw-h, with sound changes to its waw and h; plurals and diminutives restore the root, while Basran spelling permits two or three alifs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r9.anchor: وأصل الماء موه، قلبت الواو ألفا لتحركها وتحرك ما قبلها فقلت ماه، فالتقى حرفان خفيان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r10.speaker: أبو الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r10.claim: Abu al-Hasan says Basrans spell water with two alifs, or optionally three; the passage analyzes the first as the root’s middle radical, hamza as a replacement for h, and the final alif as tanwin.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r10.anchor: قال أبو الحسن: لا يجوز أن يكتب إلا بألفين عند البصريين، وإن شئت بثلاث

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r11.claim: Thamarāt is the plural of thamarah; thamar and thimār have several collective or plural patterns, and thimār can also mean the knotted ends of whips.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r11.anchor: الرابعة: قوله تعالى: { فأخرج به من الثمرات رزقا لكم } الثمرات جمع ثمرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r12.claim: The verse describes God bringing out many kinds of fruit and kinds of plants.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r12.anchor: والمعنى في الآية أخرجنا لكم ألوانا من الثمرات، وأنواعا من النبات.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r13.claim: The produce is provision: food for people and fodder for their animals, as the passage about rain and crops clarifies.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#2/r13.anchor: { رزقا } طعاما لكم، وعلفا لدوابكم وقد بين هذا قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r1.speaker: محمد بن السميقع
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Sumayqa reads the word in the singular, nad.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r2.claim: Fruit can be called provision before ownership because it is prepared to be owned and is available for use.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r2.anchor: لأنها معدة لأن تملك ويصح بها الانتفاع فهي رزق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r3.claim: The verse shows that God has made people independent of every creature for their basic needs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r3.anchor: ودلت هذه الآية على أن الله تعالى أغنى الإنسان عن كل مخلوق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r4.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r4.claim: Muslim transmits the Prophet’s teaching that gathering firewood with one’s own rope is better than asking another person for charity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r4.anchor:
قال عليه السلام مشيرا إلى هذا المعنى:
" والله لأن يأخذ أحدكم حبله فيحتطب على ظهره خير له من أن يسأل أحدا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r5.claim: The firewood example extends to crafts and work; making oneself dependent on people through greed and worldly ambition takes on something of making God a rival.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r5.anchor: ويدخل في معنى الاحتطاب جميع الأشغال من الصنائع وغيرها فمن أحوج نفسه إلى بشر مثله بسبب الحرص

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r6.speaker: علماء الصوفية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r6.claim: Sufi teachers read the verse as a path of poverty: earth for bedding, sky for cover, water and grass for necessities, and no worship of people for worldly gain.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r6.anchor: وقال علماء الصوفية: أعلم الله عز وجل في هذه الآية سبيل الفقر وهو أن تجعل الأرض وطاء والسماء غطاء،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r7.speaker: نوف البكالي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r7.claim: Nawf al-Bikali recounts Ali describing the ascetics: earth is their carpet, soil their bed, water their seasoning, and Qur’an and prayer their inner and outer garments.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r7.anchor: وقال نوف البكالي: رأيت علي بن أبي طالب خرج فنظر إلى النجوم فقال: يا نوف، أراقد أنت أم رامق؟

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r9.claim: Andad are peers, equals, or counterparts; nad is the singular.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#3/r9.anchor: { لله أندادا } أي أكفاء وأمثالا ونظراء واحدها ند

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses andad as opposites.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r2.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r2.claim: Al-Nahhas parses andadan as the first object and li-llah as the second.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r2.anchor: النحاس: «أندادا» مفعول أول، و «لله» في موضع الثاني.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r3.speaker: حسان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r3.claim: Hassan uses nad to mean an equal or counterpart in his rebuke to a poet.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r3.anchor:
أتهجوه ولست له بند
فشركما لخيركما الفداء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r4.speaker: لبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r4.claim: Labid uses nadida for a rival or counterpart, and the passage notes intensive forms nadid and nadida.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r4.anchor: ويقال: ند ونديد ونديدة على المبالغة قال لبيد:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r5.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r5.claim: Al-Jawhari records other senses: a raised mound, a non-Arabic perfume, a camel bolting, and publicizing someone.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r5.anchor: الجوهري: والند بفتح النون: التل المرتفع في السماء. والند من الطيب ليس بعربي.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r6.claim: “While you know” is a nominal sentence functioning as a circumstantial clause.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r6.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وأنتم تعلمون } ابتداء وخبر، والجملة في موضع الحال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the address “you” is directed to the unbelievers and hypocrites.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r7.anchor: والخطاب للكافرين والمنافقين عن ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r8.claim: The first answer is that they know specifically that God created them, sent rain, and provided crops, so He—not their rivals—is their benefactor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r8.anchor: يريد العلم الخاص بأن الله تعالى خلق الخلق وأنزل الماء وأنبت الرزق فيعلمون أنه المنعم عليهم دون الأنداد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r9.claim: Alternatively, they have the capacity to know God’s oneness if they reflect and reason.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r9.anchor: الثاني: أن يكون المعنى وأنتم تعلمون وحدانيته بالقوة والإمكان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r10.claim: The verse requires using rational proofs and invalidates blind imitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r10.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على الأمر باستعمال حجج العقول وإبطال التقليد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r11.speaker: ابن فورك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r11.claim: Ibn Furak says the address may include believers, warning them not to apostatize and assign partners after knowing God is one.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r11.anchor: وقال ابن فورك: يحتمل أن تتناول الآية المؤمنين فالمعنى لا ترتدوا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r12.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r12.claim: Al-Jawhari also gives nadda for a camel bolting and naddada for publicizing someone; some read yawm al-tanad with this root.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:22#4/r12.anchor: وند البعير يند ندا وندادا وندودا: نفر وذهب على وجهه ومنه قرأ بعضهم «يوم التناد». وندد به أي شهره وسمع به

RAZI-FULL:v2p74#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p74#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p74#2/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī introduces the following verses as an argument establishing divine unity, prophethood, and resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v2p74#2/r3.anchor: القول في إقامة الدلالة على التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد

RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r1.claim: After describing believers, unbelievers, and hypocrites, God shifts from speaking about them to addressing them directly, an iltifāt also seen in 1:5.
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r1.anchor: أقبل عليهم بالخطاب ، وهو من باب الالتفات المذكور في قوله تعالى : { إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين }

RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r2.claim: Direct address stirs and moves the hearer more than continuing to speak about that person in the third person.
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r2.anchor: أن فيه مزيد هز وتحريك من السامع

RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r3.claim: The shift honors and draws the addressee near: after initially making the Messenger an intermediary, God now addresses the person without an intermediary.
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r3.anchor: كأنه سبحانه وتعالى يقول . جعلت الرسول واسطة بيني وبينك أولا ثم الآن أزيد في إكرامك وتقريبك

RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r4.claim: The move from third to direct address suggests that a servant engaged in worship is continually ascending.
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r4.anchor: أنه مشعر بأن العبد إذا كان مشتغلا بالعبودية فإنه يكون أبدا في الترقي

RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r5.claim: Because the earlier verses narrated their condition and these verses impose difficult commands, God’s direct personal address gives relief and makes the burden pleasant.
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r5.anchor: الآيات المتقدمة كانت في حكاية أحوالهم ، وأما هذه الآيات فإنها أمر وتكليف ، ففيه كلفة ومشقة فلا بد من راحة

RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r6.speaker: علقمة والحسن
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r6.claim: ʿAlqama and al-Ḥasan say that Qur’anic addresses “O people” are Meccan, while “O you who believe” is Medinan.
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r6.anchor: حكي عن علقمة والحسن أنه قال : كل شيء في القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r7.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r7.claim: Al-Qāḍī accepts that distinction if it rests on transmitted reports, but rejects deriving it merely from the larger number of believers in Medina: believers may be addressed as people, and unbelievers may be commanded to worship just as believers are told to persist and increase in worship.
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r7.anchor: هذا الذي ذكروه إن كان الرجوع فيه إلى النقل فمسلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r1.claim: Words normally denote linguistic or nonlinguistic things; the vocative particle is different, functioning as an act that draws attention rather than denoting another thing.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r1.anchor: لفظ النداء لم يجعل دليلا على شيء آخر ، بل هو لفظ يجري مجرى عمل يعمله عامل لأجل التنبيه

RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r2.claim: “O Zayd” cannot mean “I call Zayd”: the latter is a truth-apt report, does not itself make Zayd the addressee, may be spoken to a third party, and reports rather than performs the call.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r2.anchor: أن قولنا . أنادي زيدا ، خبر يحتمل التصديق والتكذيب

RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r3.claim: Though names are strongest and particles weakest, a name can join a particle in calling; by analogy, a human can serve the transcendent Lord through invocation and humble supplication.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r3.anchor: قد يأتلف الاسم مع الحرف في حال النداء ، فكذا البشر يصلح لخدمة الرب حال النداء والتضرع

RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r4.claim: Yā originally calls someone distant; hamza (a-) calls someone near. Using yā for someone nearby treats an inattentive or heedless person as distant.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r4.anchor: ( ياء ) حرف وضع في أصله لنداء البعيد وإن كان لنداء القريب لكن لسبب أمر مهم جدا

RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r5.claim: Although God is nearer than the jugular vein, a supplicant says “O Lord” either from humility and self-reproach, distancing himself from the stations of intimacy, or because answering prayer is supremely important.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r5.anchor: هو استبعاد لنفسه من مظان الزلفى وما يقربه إلى منازل المقربين هضما لنفسه وإقرارا عليها بالتنقيص

RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r1.claim: Ay connects the vocative to a noun bearing the definite article, just as dhū and alladhī connect generic nouns to descriptions and definite nouns to clauses; ay is ambiguous and needs a noun or equivalent adjective to specify it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r1.anchor: ( أي ) وصلة إلى نداء ما فيه الألف اللام كما أن ( ذو ) و ( الذي ) وصلتان إلى الوصف بأسماء الأجناس

RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r2.claim: The vocative particle governs ay, while the following noun is its adjective, as in “O Zayd, the courteous”; unlike Zayd, ay cannot stand independently and therefore remains joined to its adjective and described noun.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r2.anchor: فالذي يعمل فيه حرف النداء هو أي والاسم التابع له صفة كقولك يا زيد الظريف

RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r3.claim: The inserted attention particle reinforces the call and compensates for the genitive construction expected with ay.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r3.anchor: التنبيه المقحمة بين الصفة وموصوفها ففيها فائدتان

RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r4.claim: The emphatic formula is frequent in the Qur’an because its commands, prohibitions, promises, threats, and momentous histories must awaken listeners who are heedless.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r4.anchor: إن كل ما نادى الله تعالى به عباده من الأوامر والنواهي ، والوعد والوعيد ، واقتصاص أخبار المتقدمين بأمور عظام

RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r4.claim: Rāzī identifies five proofs of the Creator in these verses: creating accountable people, their predecessors, heaven, earth, and fruits from rain sent down from heaven.
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r4.anchor: أولها : ما ذكر ههنا من الدلائل الخمسة وهي خلق المكلفين وخلق من قبلهم ، وخلق السماء وخلق الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r5.claim: The Qur’an’s other signs in the heavens and earth likewise aim to establish the Creator’s existence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r5.anchor: وكل ما ورد في القرآن من عجائب السماوات والأرض ، فالمقصود منه ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r9.claim: Different fruits and animals arising despite shared four-element natures show that God is powerful and freely choosing, not acting by intrinsic necessity.
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r9.anchor: حدوث الثمار المختلفة والحيوانات المختلفة مع استواء الكل في الطبائع الأربع

RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r10.claim: Rāzī turns to Qur’anic proofs of divine transcendence, maintaining that God is neither a body nor located in space.
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r10.anchor: وأما التنزيه فالذي يدل على أنه ليس بجسم ، ولا في مكان قوله :

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r1.claim: As evidence for transcendence, Rāzī cites God’s proof given to Abraham against his people.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r1.anchor: وتلك حجتنا ءاتيناها إبراهيم على قومه } ( الأنعام : 82 ) وثانيها : حاله مع أبيه

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r2.claim: Abraham challenged his father’s worship of an idol that could neither hear, see, nor help him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r2.anchor: ياأبت لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغنى عنك شيئا

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r3.claim: Abraham verbally challenged his people about the statues to which they were devoted.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r3.anchor: أما بالقول فقوله : { ما هاذه التماثيل التى أنتم لها عاكفون }

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r4.claim: Abraham demonstrated the idols’ impotence by smashing them all except the largest, so that the people might turn to it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r4.anchor: فجعلهم جذاذا إلا كبيرا لهم لعلهم إليه يرجعون

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r5.claim: Before the ruler, Abraham argued that his Lord gives life and death, exposing the ruler’s claim to do the same.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r5.anchor: { ربي الذى يحى ويميت قال أنا أحى وأميت } ( البقرة : 258 ) إلى آخره

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r6.claim: Rāzī says sound minds recognize that kalām merely presents these prophetic proofs and answers objections to them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r6.anchor: وكل من سلمت فطرته علم أن علم الكلام ليسي إلا تقرير هذه الدلائل ودفع الأسئلة والمعارضات عنها

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r7.claim: Abraham also asked God to show him how He revives the dead, addressing the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r7.anchor: { رب أرنى كيف تحى الموتى } ( البقرة : 26 ) إلى آخره

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r8.claim: Moses answered Pharaoh with the Lord who gave each thing its form and guidance, the same creation-and-guidance proof Abraham used of God creating and guiding him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r8.anchor: قال ربنا الذى أعطى كل شىء خلقه ثم هدى

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r9.claim: Moses’ appeal to the Lord of Pharaoh’s forefathers echoes Abraham’s argument that his Lord gives life and death.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r9.anchor: ربكم ورب ءابائكم الاولين } ( الشعراء : 26 ) وهذا هو الذي قاله إبراهيم

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r10.claim: When Pharaoh demanded another proof, Moses named the Lord of the East and West.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r10.anchor: فلما لم يكتف فرعون بذلك وطالبه بشيء آخر قال موسى : { رب المشرق والمغرب }

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r11.claim: These proofs belong to the prophets’ practice: they reasoned them out and inherited them from their purified predecessors.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r11.anchor: التمسك بهذه الدلائل حرفة هؤلاء المعصومين وأنهم كما استفادوها من عقولهم فقد توارثوها

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r12.claim: Moses also argued for his prophethood by offering a clear miracle as evidence of his truthfulness.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r12.anchor: ففي قوله : { أو * لو * جئتك بشىء مبين } وهذا هو الاستدلال بالمعجزة على الصدق

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r13.claim: Muhammad’s argument for monotheism, prophethood, and resurrection is unmistakable because the Qur’an is full of such proofs.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r13.anchor: اشتغاله بالدلائل على التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد أظهر من أن يحتاج فيه إلى التطويل

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r14.claim: The Qur’an refutes materialists who say only time destroys by presenting various proofs.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r14.anchor: الدهرية الذين كانوا يقولون : { وما يهلكنا إلا الدهر } ( الجاثية : 24 ) والله تعالى أبطل قولهم بأنواع الدلائل

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r15.claim: Varied plants and animals arising despite shared natural temperaments and celestial influences refute those who deny a freely choosing Creator.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r15.anchor: حدوث أنواع النبات وأصناف الحيوانات مع اشتراك الكل في الطبائع وتأثيرات الأفلاك

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r16.claim: Abraham’s argument when night covered him refutes those who make celestial bodies partners by claiming they influence the world.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r16.anchor: والله تعالى أبطله بدليل الخليل في قوله : { فلما جن عليه اليل }

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r17.claim: The Qur’an also refutes lower partners: Christians claim divinity for Christ and idolaters for their idols.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r17.anchor: وأما الشريك السفلي فالنصارى قالوا بإلاهية المسيح وعبدة الأوثان قالوا : بإلاهية الأوثان

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r18.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r18.claim: One group denied prophethood altogether, asking whether God would send a human messenger.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r18.anchor: الذين طعنوا في أصل النبوة وهم الذين حكى الله عنهم أنهم قالوا : { أبعث الله بشرا رسولا }

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r19.claim: Another group, including Jews and Christians, accepted prophethood in general but challenged Muhammad’s prophethood; the Qur’an answers their objections.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r19.anchor: والثاني : الذين سلموا أصل النبوة وطعنوا في نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وهم اليهود والنصارى

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r20.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r20.claim: When critics objected to Qur’anic parables, God replied that He is not ashamed to give even a mosquito as an example.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r20.anchor: فأجاب الله بقوله : { إن الله لا * يستحى أن يضرب مثلا ما بعوضة }

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r21.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r21.claim: When critics demanded further miracles, including a spring from the earth, the Qur’an answered their challenge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r21.anchor: وقالوا لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r22.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r22.claim: When critics objected to gradual revelation as grounds for suspicion, God explained that it strengthened the Prophet’s heart.

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r1.claim: The Qur’an answers those who dispute resurrection with many proofs for the resurrection and against its deniers.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r1.anchor: الخامس : الذين نازعوا في الحشر والنشر ، والله تعالى أورد على صحة ذلك وعلى إبطال قول المنكرين

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r2.claim: To those who say obligations bring no benefit, God replies that good or evil deeds return to the doer.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r2.anchor: إن أحسنتم أحسنتم لأنفسكم وإن أسأتم فلها

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r3.claim: To the claim that determinism invalidates obligation, God replies that He is not questioned about what He does, while people are questioned.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r3.anchor: { لا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون } ( الأنبياء : 23 )

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r4.claim: Rāzī abbreviates these examples because their full treatment appears elsewhere in the book.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r4.anchor: اكتفينا في هذا المقام بهذه الإشارات المختصرة لأن الاستقصاء فيها مذكور

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r5.claim: Since every prophet practiced this discipline, Rāzī concludes that its critic is either an unbeliever or ignorant.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r5.anchor: ثبت أن هذه الحرفة هي حرفة كل الأنبياء والرسل علمنا أن الطاعن فيها إما أن يكون كافرا أو جاهلا

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r6.claim: Rationally, taqlīd cannot justify choosing one authority: following everyone entails following unbelievers, choosing only some has no basis, and rejecting all imitation leaves rational inquiry.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r6.anchor: فهو أنه ليس تقليد البعض أولى من تقليد الباقي ، فأما أن يجوز تقليد الكل فيلزمنا تقليد الكفار

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r7.claim: Scripture commands calling to God with wisdom and good admonition and debating in the best manner; Rāzī interprets wisdom as proof and demonstration.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r7.anchor: ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة وجادلهم بالتي هي أحسن

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r8.claim: The commanded debate concerns monotheism and prophethood, not legal branches: such branches are pointless to those rejecting prophecy, while those accepting it would not dispute the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r8.anchor: لا فائدة في الخوض معه في تفاريع الشرع ، ومن أثبت نبوته فإنه لا يخالفه

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r9.claim: Because Muslims are commanded to follow Muhammad and take him as their example, they too must engage in the debate he was commanded to conduct.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r9.anchor: ثم إنا مأمورون باتباعه عليه السلام لقوله : { فاتبعوني يحببكم الله }

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r10.claim: The Qur’an condemns arguing about God without knowledge, which implies that argument grounded in knowledge is not blameworthy and is praiseworthy.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r10.anchor: ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم } ( الحج : 3 ، 8 لقمان : 20 ) ذم من يجادل في الله بغير علم

RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r4.claim: The possibility of attributes is inferred from the heavens and earth’s created arrangement; Rāzī specifically points to the earth as a resting-place and sky as a structure.
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r4.anchor: ثانيها : الاستدلال بإمكان الصفات وإليه الإشارة بقوله : { خلق * السماوات والارض }

RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r9.claim: Rāzī treats the earth and sky as cosmic evidence that natural bodies themselves depend on a maker; changes such as thunder, lightning, winds, clouds, and seasons are signs of the horizons.
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r9.anchor: ذكر الله تعالى عقيبه ما يدل على افتقار هذه الأشياء إلى المحدث والموجد

RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r10.claim: Celestial and elemental bodies share corporeality, so their differing quantities, shapes, and locations cannot be explained by corporeality or any property necessarily belonging to it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r10.anchor: أن الأجسام الفلكية والأجسام العنصرية مشتركة في الجسمية

RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r5.claim: The relative phrase alladhī jaʿala may be accusative as an adjective of the earlier alladhī or as praise; it may instead be nominative as a subject, likewise carrying praise.
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r5.anchor: لفظ ( الذي ) وهو موصول مع صلته ، إما أن يكون في محل النصب وصفا للذي خلقكم

RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r6.claim: Alladhī introduces a known proposition to identify a singular referent; thus the verse presupposes that its audience knows who made earth a bed and heaven a structure.
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r6.anchor: كلمة موضوعة للإشارة إلى مفرد عند محاولة تعريفه بقضية معلومة

RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r7.claim: This presupposed recognition matches the claim that, when asked who created heaven and earth, the audience answers Allah.
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r7.anchor: يقتضي أنهم كانوا عالمين بوجود شيء جعل الأرض فراشا والسماء بناء وذلك تحقيق قوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r1.claim: For earth to serve as a bed, it must be still; Rāzī argues that a descending or rotating earth would frustrate ordinary jumping or travel.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r1.anchor: اعلم أنه سبحانه وتعالى ذكر ههنا أنه جعل الأرض فراشا ، ونظيره قوله

RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r2.claim: If earth fell straight down, its greater weight would make it descend faster than a jumper; if it rotated east faster than a person moving west, the person could not reach a destination. Since people can move, it is still.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r2.anchor: فلما أمكنه ذلك علمنا أن الأرض غير متحركة لا بالاستدارة ولا بالاستقامة فهي ساكنة

RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r3.claim: The claim that earth does not fall because it is limitless below is rejected: bodies have been proved finite.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r3.anchor: أحدها : أن الأرض لا نهاية لها من جانب السفل ، وإذا كان كذلك لم يكن لها مهبط فلا تنزل وهذا فاسد لما ثبت بالدليل تناهي الأجسام .

RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r4.claim: The flat-hemisphere theory, with its underside resting on water and air, fails because the support of water and air also needs explanation and it does not explain why earth is flat below but convex above.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r4.anchor: الذين سلموا تناهي الأجسام قالوا الأرض ليست بكرة بل هي كنصف كرة

RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r5.claim: The theory that celestial attraction pulls earth equally from all directions fails because it does not explain why smaller bodies are not pulled faster, or why upward-thrown dust returns.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r5.anchor: وثالثها : الذين قالوا سبب سكون الأرض جذب الفلك لها من كل الجوانب فلم يكن انجذابها إلى بعض الجوانب أولى من بعض

RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r6.claim: A fourth account attributes rest to equal pressure from all sides, like dust held at the center of a rapidly spun bottle.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94/r6.anchor: في قنينة ثم أديرت القنينة على قطبها إدارة سريعة

RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r1.claim: Against equal celestial pressure as earth's support, Rāzī asks why a pressure strong enough to hold it is not felt.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r1.anchor: الدفع إذا بلغ في القوة إلى هذا الحد فلم لا يحس به الواحد منا

RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r2.claim: The equal-pressure theory cannot explain why clouds and winds do not move in one fixed direction.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r2.anchor: ما بال هذا الدفع لا يجعل حركة السحب والرياح إلى جهة بعينها

RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r3.claim: It cannot explain why motion toward the west is not easier than motion toward the east.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r3.anchor: ما باله لم يجعل انتقالها إلى المغرب أسهل من انتقالها إلى المشرق

RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r4.claim: On this pressure theory, a heavier body should move more slowly because the restraining pressure acts more forcefully on it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r4.anchor: يجب أن يكون الثقيل كلما كان أعظم أن تكون حركته أبطأ

RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r5.claim: The theory predicts that a falling heavy body should initially move faster, farther from the celestial sphere, than near the end of its fall.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r5.anchor: يجب أن تكون حركة الثقيل النازل من الابتداء أسرع من حركته عند الانتهاء

RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r6.claim: Aristotle and most followers say earth naturally seeks the celestial center; Rāzī calls this weak because bodies are equally corporeal and the differentiating property requires a freely choosing agent.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r6.anchor: وخامسها : أن الأرض بالطبع تطلب وسط الفلك ، وهو قول أرسطاطاليس وجمهور أتباعه ، وهذا أيضا ضعيف ؛ لأن الأجسام متساوية في الجسمية

RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r7.speaker: أبو هاشم
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r7.claim: Abū Hāshim says upward tendencies in earth's lower half and downward tendencies in its upper half counterbalance to keep it still.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r7.anchor: وسادسها : قال أبو هاشم : النصف الأسفل من الأرض فيه اعتمادات صاعدة ، والنصف الأعلى فيه اعتمادات هابطة فتدافع الاعتمادان فلزم الوقوف .

RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r8.claim: Rāzī objects that assigning opposite tendencies to the two halves requires a freely choosing agent, so it does not explain earth's rest independently of God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r8.anchor: أن اختصاص كل واحد من النصفين بصفة مخصوصة لا يمكن إلا بالفاعل المختار

RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r9.claim: After rejecting the proposed causes, Rāzī concludes that God alone makes earth stationary and cites His holding heaven and earth lest they depart.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r9.anchor: فثبت بما ذكرنا أن سكون الأرض ليس إلا من الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r10.claim: God's sustaining the unsupported heavens and earth is expressly affirmed in 35:41.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r10.anchor: ولهذا قال الله تعالى : { إن الله يمسك السماوات والأرض أن تزولا ولئن زالتا إن أمسكهما من أحد من بعده } ( فاطر : 41 )

RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r11.claim: A useful bed cannot be excessively hard: walking or sleeping on stone hurts, while gold would impede cultivation, digging, and construction.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r11.anchor: فإن النوم والمشي عليه مما يؤلم البدن

RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r12.claim: Earth also cannot be excessively soft, like water, into which feet would sink.

RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r13.claim: Earth cannot be transparent: light would not rest on it and it would not warm from sun and stars; God made it opaque and dusty so it warms and suits animals.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r13.anchor: فإن الشفاف لا يستقر النور عليه

RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r14.claim: Earth must emerge from water; although its nature would sink and seas might cover it, God raised part like an exposed island for habitation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r14.anchor: الشرط الرابع : أن تكون بارزة من الماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r15.claim: The claim that earth must be non-spherical to be a bed is far-fetched: on a sufficiently large sphere, a piece is like a flat surface for standing, as mountains further secure it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p94#2/r15.anchor: وهذا بعيد جدا ، لأن الكرة إذا عظمت جدا كانت القطعة منها كالسطح

RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r1.claim: Earth contains minerals, plants, animals, and upper and lower phenomena whose details only God knows.
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r1.anchor: الأشياء المتولدة فيها من المعادن والنبات والحيوان والآثار العلوية والسفلية لا يعلم تفاصيلها إلا الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r2.claim: Earth ripens moisture, producing cohesion in composite bodies.
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r2.anchor: أن يتخمر الرطب بها فيحصل التماسك في أبدان المركبات

RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r3.claim: Earth's neighboring regions differ as loose, hard, sandy, saline, and lava-like terrain; good land yields growth while bad land yields little.
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r3.anchor: الثالثة : اختلاف بقاع الأرض ، فمنها أرض رخوة ، وصلبة ، ورملة ، وسبخة ، وحرة ، وهي قوله تعالى : { وفى الارض قطع متجاورات }

RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r4.claim: The differing colors of the earth and its mountains are another sign, including white, red, black, gray, and dusty hues.
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r4.anchor: الرابعة : اختلاف ألوانها فأحمر ، وأبيض ، وأسود ، ورمادي اللون ، وأغبر ، على ما قال تعالى : { ومن الجبال جدد بيض وحمر مختلف ألوانها وغرابيب سود }

RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r5.claim: Earth cracks open to bring forth plants.
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r5.anchor: الخامسة : انصداعها بالنبات ، قال تعالى : { والارض ذات الصدع } ( الطارق : 12 )

RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r6.claim: Earth stores water sent down from heaven, while God could remove it or cause it to sink beyond reach.
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r6.anchor: السادسة : كونها خازنة للماء المنزل من السماء وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r7.claim: Earth has springs and great rivers, a provision signaled by the verse about mountains and rivers placed in it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r7.anchor: السابعة : العيون والأنهار العظام التي فيها وإليه الإشارة بقوله ) { وجعل فيها رواسى وأنهارا } .

RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r8.claim: Its minerals and metals are among its benefits; the text notes that God keeps their stores and sends them down in measured amounts.
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r8.anchor: الثامنة : ما فيها من المعادن والفلزات ، وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى : { والارض مددناها وألقينا فيها رواسي وأنبتنا فيها من كل شىء موزون }

RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r9.claim: Earth brings hidden seeds and kernels forth; one seed can return seven hundredfold, showing its generous yield.

RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r10.claim: Water brings dead earth back to life, yielding crops and grain for people; Rāzī links this to two verses on revival by water.
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r10.anchor: العاشرة : حياتها بعد موتها ؛ قال تعالى : { أو لم * يروا أنا نسوق الماء إلى الارض الجرز * فنخرج به زرعا }

RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r11.claim: Earth bears animals of varied colors, forms, and kinds.
RAZI-FULL:v2p95/r11.anchor: الحادية عشرة : ما عليها من الدواب المختلفة الألوان والصور والخلق

RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r1.claim: Plants differ in color, taste, scent, kind, and benefit; those variations themselves are signs, and plants feed both people and livestock.
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r1.anchor: ما فيها من النبات المختلف ألوانه وأنواعه ومنافعه

RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r2.claim: Human plant foods include staples, relishes, medicines, and fruits with varied sweet and sour tastes; earth also supplies animal feed and people's food allotments.
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r2.anchor: أما مطعوم البشر ، فمنها الطعام ، ومنها الأدام ، ومنها الدواء ، ومنها الفاكهة ، ومنها الأنواع المختلفة في الحلاوة والحموضة .

RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r3.claim: Earth supplies clothing both through plants such as cotton and linen and through animals that provide hair, wool, silk, and hides; food and clothing both come from it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r3.anchor: فمنها كسوة البشر ، لأن الكسوة إما نباتية ، وهي القطن والكتان ، وإما حيوانية وهي الشعر والصوف والإبريسم والجلود

RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r4.claim: The phrase 'He creates what you do not know' points to many benefits of earth that only God knows.
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r4.anchor: ثم قال : { ويخلق ما لا تعلمون } وفيه إشارة إلى منافع كثيرة لا يعلمها إلا الله تعالى .

RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r5.claim: Earth covers the shameful remains of the dead; the cited passages call it a container for living and dead and say people return to it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r5.anchor: ثم إنه سبحانه وتعالى جعل الأرض ساترة لقبائحك بعد مماتك ، فقال : { ألم نجعل الارض كفاتا * أحياء وأمواتا * منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم }

RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r6.claim: The great benefits of heaven and earth are gathered together in the statement that God has subjected what is in both realms for people.
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r6.anchor: ثم إنه سبحانه وتعالى جمع هذه المنافع العظيمة للسماء والأرض فقال : { وسخر لكم ما فى السماوات وما فى الارض }

RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r7.claim: Small stones can adorn rings and large ones provide building material; abundant fire-producing stone is more useful than rare red ruby.
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r7.anchor: ففي صغارها ما يصلح للزينة فتجعل فصوصها للخواتم وفي كبارها ما يتخذ للأبنية

RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r8.claim: Though humans extract fine crafts, fish from the sea, and birds from the air, they cannot make gold or silver; their value depends on rarity, so God preserves the wisdom and blessing by withholding them while permitting harmless substitutes such as copper and glass.
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r8.anchor: البشر استخرجوا الحرف الدقيقة والصنائع الجليلة واستخرجوا السمكة من قعر البحر

RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r9.claim: Mountains and lands carry abundant trees suitable for construction, roofing, and firewood needed for baking and cooking.
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r9.anchor: الخامسة عشرة : كثرة ما يوجد على الجبال والأراضي من الأشجار التي تصلح للبناء ، والسقف ، ثم الحطب .

RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r10.claim: The Qurʾan describes earth's signs and benefits in language beyond the reach of eloquent speakers, exemplified by its account of the stretched land, mountains, rivers, and paired fruits.
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r10.anchor: نبه الله تعالى على دلائل الأرض ومنافعها بألفاظ لا يبلغها البلغاء ويعجز عنها الفصحاء

RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r11.claim: Rivers large and small carry fresh water for drinking, irrigation, agriculture, and other uses; named great rivers include the Nile, Sayḥūn, Jayḥūn, and Euphrates.
RAZI-FULL:v2p96/r11.anchor: وأما الأنهار فمنها العظيمة كالنيل ، وسيحون ، وجيحون ، والفرات ، ومنها الصغار ، وهي كثيرة

RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r1.claim: Some prefer heaven because it is where angels worship and no place in it has seen anyone disobey God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : السماء أفضل لوجوه : أحدها : أن السماء متعبد الملائكة ، وما فيها بقعة عصى الله فيها أحد

RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r2.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r2.claim: A second argument for heaven's superiority is that Adam's sin led to his expulsion, since God does not host those who disobey him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r2.anchor: وثانيها : لما أتى آدم عليه السلام في الجنة بتلك المعصية قيل له اهبط من الجنة ، وقال الله تعالى لا يسكن في جواري من عصاني

RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r3.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r3.claim: A third argument favors heaven because scripture calls it a protected roof and says it has constellations, with no comparable description of earth.
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى : { وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا }

RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r4.claim: A fourth argument is that scripture most often mentions heaven before earth.
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r4.anchor: ورابعها : أن في أكثر الأمر ورد ذكر السماء مقدما / على الأرض في الذكر .

RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r5.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r5.claim: Others prefer earth because God singled out several earthly places as blessed: Mecca, the blessed spot at the tree, Jerusalem's surroundings, and the lands of Syria.
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل الأرض أفضل لوجوه ( ا ) أنه تعالى وصف بقاعا من الأرض بالبركة بقوله : { إن أول بيت وضع للناس للذى ببكة مباركا } ( آل عمران : 96 )

RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r6.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r6.claim: They also cite God's description of the earth as blessed overall; even empty deserts shelter and feed wild animals and serve people when needed.
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r6.anchor: وخامسها : وصف جملة الأرض بالبركة فقال : { قل * أئنكم * لتكفرون } ( فصلت : 9 )

RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r7.claim: Razi explains that the earth's signs are called signs for the certain because only they benefit from them, honoring them as in the description guidance for the God-fearing.
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r7.anchor: فلهذه البركات قال تعالى : { وفى الارض ءايات للموقنين } ( الذاريات : 20 )

RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r8.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r8.claim: They argue that prophets were made from earth, as scripture says humans were created from it and returned to it, while heaven is only a protected roof.
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r8.anchor: وسادسها : أنه سبحانه وتعالى خلق الأنبياء المكرمين من الأرض على ما قال : { منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم } ( طه : 55 )

RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r9.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r9.claim: They add that God honored the Prophet by making the whole earth a place of prayer and its soil a means of purification.
RAZI-FULL:v2p97/r9.anchor: وسابعها : أن الله تعالى أكرم نبيه بها فجعل الأرض كلها مساجد له وجعل ترابها طهورا .

RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r1.claim: Frequent mention of the heavens and earth in scripture signals their great importance and the immense secrets and wisdoms beyond human understanding.
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r1.anchor: أنه تعالى ذكر أمر السماوات والأرض في كتابه في مواضع ، ولا شك أن إكثار ذكر الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r2.claim: Heaven is adorned with seven things: lamps, moon, sun, Throne, Kursi, Preserved Tablet, and Pen; three are visible and four are known through revealed evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r2.anchor: الأول : أن الله تعالى زينها بسبعة أشياء بالمصابيح { ولقد زينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح } ( الملك : 5 )

RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r3.claim: The Qur'an gives the heavens exalted names, then describes their end and their beginnings in detail; this attention shows their creation serves profound wisdom.
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r3.anchor: سمى السموات بأسماء تدل على عظم شأنها : سماء ، وسقفا محفوظا ، وسبعا طباقا ، وسبعا شدادا .

RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r4.claim: The account of the heavens' beginning and dissolution supports the principle that God created the heavens, earth, and what lies between them for wisdom, not in vain.
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r4.anchor: فهذا الاستقصاء الشديد في كيفية حدوثهما وفنائهما يدل على أنه سبحانه خلقهما لحكمة بالغة

RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r5.claim: Heaven is the direction toward which hands rise in supplication and faces turn, and it is the source of light, clarity, purity, and freedom from corruption.
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r5.anchor: الثالث : أنه تعالى جعل السماء قبلة الدعاء : فالأيدي ترفع إليها ، والوجوه تتوجه نحوها ، وهي منزل الأنوار

RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r6.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r6.claim: Some describe heaven as active and earth as receptive; because an active cause is nobler than its recipient, this explains why heaven is usually mentioned first.
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم السماوات والأرضون على صفتين ، فالسماوات مؤثرة غير متأثرة . والأرضون متأثرة غير مؤثرة / والمؤثر أشرف من القابل

RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r7.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r7.claim: Some say the plural heavens are needed for varied planetary conjunctions and changing angles of radiation, while one receptive earth suffices.
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r7.anchor: وأيضا ففي أكثر الأمر ذكر السموات بلفظ الجمع ، والأرض بلفظ الواحد ، فإنه لا بد من السموات الكثيرة

RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r8.claim: The sky's blue is beneficial to eyesight; physicians advise people with eye pain to look at blue, so God made the sky's surface that color for viewers' benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r8.anchor: الخامس : تفكر في لون السماء وما فيه من صواب التدبير ، فإن هذا اللون أشد الألوان موافقة للبصر

RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r9.claim: Razi calls the sky's luminous color the most beneficial and its round form the best; he reads the statement that it has no rifts in light of its encompassing form.
RAZI-FULL:v2p98/r9.anchor: فهو سبحانه وتعالى جعل لونها أنفع الألوان ، وهو المستنير

RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r1.claim: Sunrise makes human livelihoods possible, while sunset gives people the rest needed for recovery, digestion, and nourishment to reach the limbs.
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r1.anchor: فلولا ذلك لبطل أمر العالم كله ، فكيف كان الناس يسعون في معايشهم ، ثم المنفعة في طلوع الشمس ظاهرة

RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r2.claim: Night is a necessary rest period; scripture calls it a time of stillness and clothing, and daytime a time for activity and livelihood.
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r2.anchor: تأمل النفع في غروبها فلولا غروبها لم يكن للناس هدو ولا قرار مع احتياجهم إلى الهدو والقرار

RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r3.claim: Without sunset, continual solar heat would burn the earth, destroy animals, and kill plants; God's timing makes light and darkness cooperate for the world's good.
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r3.anchor: حتى يحترق كل ما عليها من حيوان ، ويهلك ما عليها من نبات

RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r4.claim: The sun's changing height produces four useful seasons: winter builds fruit matter and rain, spring brings growth, summer ripens fruit, and autumn eases bodies gradually into winter.
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r4.anchor: أما ارتفاع الشمس وانحطاطها فقد جعله الله تعالى سببا لإقامة الفصول الأربعة ففي الشتاء تغور الحرارة في الشجر والنبات

RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r5.claim: The sun's daily motion spreads its light over every exposed place; if it stayed in one spot, that region would overheat while others remained cold.
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r5.anchor: فإنها لو كانت واقفة في موضع / واحد لاشتدت السخونة في ذلك الموضع واشتد البرد في سائر المواضع

RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r6.claim: Razi pictures God's rotation of the sun as ensuring even a poor person gets light when a rich neighbor's building blocks the sun from his window.
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r6.anchor: وأيضا كأن الله تعالى يقول لو وقفت في جانب الشرق والغنى قد رفع بناءه على كوة الفقير ، فكان لا يصل النور إلى الفقير

RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r7.claim: The sun's tilted motion distributes effects among regions and seasons; without it, climates would be permanently winterlike, summerlike, or transitional, while too little or too much motion would frustrate benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v2p99/r7.anchor: لو لم يكن للكواكب حركة في الميل لكان التأثير مخصوصا ببقعة واحدة فكان سائر الجوانب يخلو عن المنافع

RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r1.claim: Moonless darkness can conceal a fugitive from pursuers; Razi cites al-Mutanabbi's verse as showing that darkness disproves the Manichaean view.
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r1.anchor: فوكم لظلام الليل عندي من يد … تخبر أن المانوية تكذب

RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r2.speaker: أعرابي
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r2.claim: A story tells of a Bedouin who found his lost camel when the moon rose, praised its light, and composed verses thanking it for joy and beauty.
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r2.anchor: ومن الحكايات : أن أعرابيا نام عن جمله ليلا ففقده ، فلما طلع القمر وجده

RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r3.speaker: بعض العرب
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r3.claim: Some Arabs disparage the moon for exposing thieves and lovers, catching fugitives, wearing linen, aging the young, making people forget loved ones, and bringing debt and death nearer.
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r3.anchor: ولقد كان في العرب من يذم القمر ويقول : القمر يقرب الأجل ، ويفضح السارق

RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r4.speaker: بعض العرب
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r4.claim: Some favor the moon because its grammatical gender is masculine while the sun is feminine.
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r4.anchor: وكان فيهم أيضا من يفضل القمر على الشمس من وجوه : أحدها : أن القمر مذكر . والشمس مؤنث

RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r5.speaker: المتنبي
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r5.claim: Al-Mutanabbi counters that feminine gender is no defect for the sun, and masculine gender gives the crescent no honor.
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r5.anchor: لكن المتنبي طعن فيه بقوله : ففما التأنيث لاسم الشمس عيب … ولا التذكير فخر للهلال

RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r6.speaker: بعض العرب
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r6.claim: Some infer the moon's superiority from the paired expression the two moons, which makes the sun seem secondary to the moon.
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r6.anchor: وثانيها : أنهم قالوا : القمران ، فجعلوا الشمس تابعة للقمر

RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r7.claim: Some favor the sun because the Qur'an names it before the moon, but Razi rejects word order as proof of merit and lists passages that place the lesser item first.
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r7.anchor: ومنهم من فضل الشمس على القمر بأن الله تعالى قدمها على القمر في قوله : { الشمس والقمر بحسبان }

RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r8.claim: Stars serve as missiles against devils, help determine the direction of prayer, and guide travelers across land and sea.
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r8.anchor: أما النجوم : ففيها منافع . المنفعة الأولى : كونها رجوما للشياطين ، والثانية : معرفة القبلة بها ، والثالثة : أن يهتدي بها المسافر

RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r9.claim: Stars include those that set and never rise, those that rise and never set, and those that both rise and set.
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r9.anchor: ثم النجوم على ثلاثة أقسام : غاربة لا تطلع كالكواكب الجنوبية ، وطالعة لا تغرب كالشمالية ، ومنها ما يغرب تارة ويطلع أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r10.claim: Razi separately distinguishes fixed stars from wandering stars.

RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r11.claim: He also distinguishes stars that are eastern from those that are western.

RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r12.speaker: الفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r12.claim: Razi introduces philosophers' claim to know the celestial bodies and their distances.
RAZI-FULL:v2p100/r12.anchor: أما الذي تدعيه الفلاسفة من معرفة الأجرام والأبعاد

RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r1.claim: Razi answers claims of detailed knowledge about remote celestial things by citing revelation that only God knows the unseen, human knowledge is limited, and the Prophet does not claim the unseen or God's stores.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r1.anchor: قال تعالى : { عالم الغيب فلا يظهر على غيبه أحدا * إلا من ارتضى من رسول } ( الجن : 26 ، 27 ) وقال : { وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا }

RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r2.claim: Humans cannot fully know their own essence and qualities, so they cannot claim detailed knowledge of the most distant things.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r2.anchor: فقد عجز الخلق عن معرفة ذواتهم وصفاتهم فكيف يقدرون على معرفة أبعد الأشياء عنهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r3.speaker: قائلهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r3.claim: An unnamed Arab poet says people may know today and yesterday but remain blind to what tomorrow holds.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r3.anchor: قال قائلهم : فوأعرف ما في اليوم والأمس قبله … ولكنني عن علم ما في غد عمي

RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r4.speaker: لبيد
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r4.claim: Labid says diviners using pebbles and bird omens do not know what God will bring about.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r4.anchor: وقال لبيد : ففوالله ما تدري الضوارب بالحصى … ولا زاجرات الطير ما الله صانع

RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r5.speaker: الجاحظ
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r5.claim: Al-Jahiz compares the world to a prepared house: heaven is its roof, earth its carpet, stars its lamps, humans its steward, and plants and animals are arranged for their benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r5.anchor: قال الجاحظ : إذا تأملت في هذا العالم وجدته كالبيت المعد فيه كل ما يحتاج إليه ، فالسماء مرفوعة كالسقف

RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r6.speaker: الجاحظ
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r6.claim: Al-Jahiz says the world's order shows complete planning, comprehensive measure, profound wisdom, and unlimited power.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101/r6.anchor: فهذه جملة واضحة دالة على أن العالم مخلوق بتدبير كامل وتقدير شامل وحكمة بالغة وقدرة غير متناهية

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r1.claim: Razi portrays earth as a mother that God prepared to meet human needs; it is like a pearl-bearing shell containing Adam and his descendants.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r1.anchor: لما خلق الأرض وكانت كالصدف والدرة المودعة فيه آدم وأولاده ، ثم علم الله أصناف حاجاتهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r2.claim: He points to the scriptural image of rain poured down and earth split open as part of the earth's provision for people.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r2.anchor: فقال : { أنا * صببنا الماء صبا * ثم شققنا الأرض شقا } ( عبس : 25 ، 26 )

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r3.claim: Gold and silver would not provide the earth's many benefits, and the earthly world is itself a prison; this makes God's provision here a sign of greater gifts in paradise.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r3.anchor: فانظر يا عبدي أن أعز الأشياء عندك الذهب والفضة ، ولو أني خلقت الأرض من الذهب والفضة هل كان يحصل منها هذه المنافع

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r4.claim: Earth is more tender than a human mother: a mother gives one kind of milk, while earth supplies many kinds of food.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r4.anchor: والأرض تطعمك كذا وكذا لونا من الأطعمة

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r5.claim: Razi reads the statement that humans return to earth as a return to their mother, not a threat, since no one threatens a person with his mother.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r5.anchor: ثم قال : { منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم } ( طه : 55 ) معناه نردكم إلى هذه الأم ، وهذا ليس بوعيد ؛ لأن المرء لا يوعد بأمه

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r6.claim: The earth is a larger womb than the mother's, where a fetus spent nine months without hunger or thirst; Razi invites the reader to hope for similar care in earth's womb.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r6.anchor: ثم إنك كنت في بطن الأم تسعة أشهر فما مسك جوع ولا عطش ، فكيف إذا دخلت بطن الأم الكبرى

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r7.claim: The comparison requires entering earth's womb as one entered the first womb without sin: the fetus obeyed God's call to emerge, whereas people now fail to answer repeated calls to prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r7.anchor: لأنك حين كنت في بطن الأم الصغرى ما كانت لك زلة ، فضلا عن أن تكون لك كبيرة / بل كنت مطيعا لله

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r8.claim: Razi likens rain joining sky and earth to a marriage bond and the fruits emerging from earth to offspring, prompting reflection on human and cosmic conditions.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r8.anchor: لما ذكر الأرض والسماء بين ما بينهما من شبه عقد النكاح بإنزال الماء من السماء على الأرض والإخراج به من بطنها

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r9.claim: Because only a creator unlike created things in essence and attributes can form rain and fruits, their production points to the wise Maker.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#2/r9.anchor: ويعرفوا أن شيئا من هذه الأشياء لا يقدر على تكوينها وتخليفها إلا من كان مخالفا لها في الذات والصفات

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r1.claim: Whether God creates fruits by customary direct action or through powers in water and receptive earth, both accounts require a wise maker; God can also create fruits and their qualities directly.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r1.anchor: لا بد من الصانع الحكيم وأما التفصيل فنقول : لا شك أنه تعالى قادر على خلق هذه الثمار ابتداء

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r2.claim: A fruit is a body bearing taste, color, smell, and moisture; because God can create bodies and these possible qualities, he can produce fruit without intermediaries.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r2.anchor: لأن الثمرة لا معنى لها إلا جسم قام به طعم ولون ورائحة ورطوبة ، والجسم قابل لهذه الصفات ، وهذه الصفات مقدورة لله تعالى ابتداء

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r3.claim: A transmitted report that God creates the reward of paradise without intermediaries reinforces the rational proof of his ability to create directly.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r3.anchor: ومما يؤكد هذا الدليل العقلي من الدلائل النقلية ما ورد الخبر بأنه تعالى يخترع نعيم أهل الجنة للمثابين من غير هذه الوسائط

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r4.claim: Direct creation does not preclude creation through powers God places in bodies; later theologians apparently deny such powers, but Razi says that denial needs proof.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r4.anchor: وظاهر قول المتأخرين من المتكلمين إنكار ذلك ولا بد فيه من دليل

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r5.claim: God's choice to bring fruit about gradually is sufficient reason; one wisdom is that the hardship of farming teaches people to endure lesser religious duties for greater afterlife rewards.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r5.anchor: أحدها : أنه تعالى إنما أجرى العادة بأن لا يفعل ذلك إلا على ترتيب وتدريج ، لأن المكلفين إذا تحلوا المشقة في الحرث والغرس طلبا

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r6.claim: As bitter medicine is endured to avoid illness, people should accept the lesser hardship of religious obligations to avoid punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r6.anchor: كما قلنا أنه تعالى قادر على خلق الشفاء من غير تناول الدواء لكنه أجرى عادته بتوقيفه عليه لأنه إذا تحمل مرارة الأدوية

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r7.claim: Gradual production makes people infer the wise creator through careful thought; immediate creation would make that attribution necessary knowledge and undermine moral testing.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r7.anchor: أنه تعالى لو خلقها دفعة من غير هذه الوسائط لحصل العلم الضروري بإسنادها إلى القادر الحكيم ، وذلك كالمنافي للتكليف والابتلاء

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r8.claim: The ordered processes of nature also provide angels and perceptive people with material for reflection.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r8.anchor: وثالثها : أنه ربما كان للملائكة ولأهل الاستبصار عبر في ذلك وأفكار صائبة .

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r9.claim: Since sky means what is elevated, rain that falls from clouds can be called water sent down from heaven.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r9.anchor: أن السماء إنما سميت سماء لسموها فكل ما سماك فهو سماء فإذا نزل من السحاب فقد نزل من السماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r10.claim: A second answer is that elevated moist particles drive the moist particles rising from the earth's depths, so the water's process begins with influence from above.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r10.anchor: وثانيها : أن المحرك لإثارة تلك الأجزاء الرطبة من عمق الأرض الأجزاء الرطبة { أنزل من السماء مآء }

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r11.claim: A third answer preserves both the verse and observation: God truthfully says he sends rain from heaven, and rain descends from heaven to cloud and then from cloud to earth.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r11.anchor: فإذا علمنا أنه مع ذلك ينزل من السحاب فيجب أن يقال ينزل من السماء إلى السحاب ، ومن السحاب إلى الأرض .

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r12.claim: The preposition min can be partitive: some water comes down and some fruits emerge to become some of people's provision.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r12.anchor: أحدهما : التبعيض لأن المنكرين أعني ماء ورزقا يكتنفانه وقد قصد بتنكيرهما معنى البعضية

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r13.claim: Alternatively, min is explanatory, as in spending money from coins; on the partitive reading rizqan is an object of purpose, and on the explanatory reading it is the object of akhraja.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r13.anchor: والثاني : أن يكون للبيان كقولك أنفقت من الدراهم إنفاقا ، فإن قيل فيم انتصب رزقا ؟

RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r14.claim: The plural thamarat, rather than a generic singular or another plural, highlights how limited worldly fruit is and points to the greater abundance of the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v2p101#3/r14.anchor: تنبيها على قلة ثمار الدنيا وإشعارا بتعظيم أمر الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r1.claim: One construction links do not make rivals to the command to worship: monotheism is the foundation and basis of worship.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r1.anchor: أحدها : أن يتعلق بالأمر ، أي أعبدوا فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا فإن أصل العبادة وأساسها التوحيد

RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r2.claim: A second construction links the prohibition to so that you may become God-fearing: do not set up a rival, one of the gravest causes of punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r2.anchor: وثانيها : بلعل ، والمعنى خلقكم لكي تنقوا وتخافوا عقابه فلا تثبتوا له ندا فإنه من أعظم موجبات العقاب

RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r3.claim: A third construction links the prohibition to the one who made earth a resting place: the giver of these clear signs must not be assigned partners.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r3.anchor: وثالثها : بقوله : { الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا } أي هو الذي خلق لكم هذه الدلائل الباهرة فلا تتخذوا له شركاء
