RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r4.claim: A nidd is an equal rival or opponent; the root connotes flight and mutual opposition, as each of two rivals turns away from and contends with the other.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r4.anchor: أنه المثل المنازع وناددت الرجل نافرته من ند ندودا إذا نفر كأن كل واحد من الندين يناد صاحبه

RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r5.claim: Although idolaters did not say idols contested God, worshiping and naming them gods makes their stance resemble belief in rivals able to contend with him; the wording taunts them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r5.anchor: لما عبدوها وسموها آلهة أشبهت حالهم حال من يعتقد أنها آلهة قادرة على منازعته فقيل لهم ذلك على سبيل التهكم

RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r6.claim: The plural rivals also rebukes them for setting many equals beside the one God, who is wholly without an equal.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r6.anchor: وكما تهكم بلفظ الند شنع عليهم بأنهم جعلوا أندادا كثيرة لمن لا يصلح أن يكون له ند قط

RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r7.speaker: محمد بن السميّفع
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa is reported to read the phrase with singular nidd rather than plural andad.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r7.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن السميّفع فلا تجعلوا لله ندا

RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r8.claim: You know by your full rational capacity that created things cannot rightly be God's equals, so you must not say so; knowingly making a vile claim is worse.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103/r8.anchor: معناه إنكم لكمال عقولكم تعلمون أن هذه الأشياء لا يصح جعلها أندادا لله تعالى ، فلا تقولوا ذلك فإن القول القبيح ممن علم قبحه يكون أقبح

RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r1.claim: Rāzī says no group asserts a fully equal partner with God in existence, power, knowledge, and wisdom.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r1.anchor: ليس في العالم أحد يثبت لله شريكا يساويه في الوجود والقدرة والعلم والحكمة

RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r2.speaker: الثنوية
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r2.claim: Dualists posit two gods: one mild and responsible for good, the other foolish and responsible for evil.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r2.anchor: الثنوية يثبتون إلهين : أحدهما : حليم يفعل الخير والثاني : سفيه يفعل الشر

RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r3.speaker: الصابئة
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r3.claim: The Sabeans say God created the planets, which administer the world; they worship them, while the planets worship God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r3.anchor: الفريق الأول : عبدة الكواكب وهم الصابئة ، فإنهم يقولون إن الله تعالى خلق هذه الكواكب

RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r4.speaker: النصارى
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r4.claim: Christians are another group that worships Jesus.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r4.anchor: الفريق الثاني : النصارى الذين يعبدون المسيح عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r5.claim: Idol worship predates the earliest prophet whose history is known, Noah, and remains widespread; Noah's people already defended their idols.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r5.anchor: لا دين أقدم من دين عبدة الأوثان ، وذلك لأن أقدم الأنبياء الذين نقل إلينا تاريخهم هو نوح عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r6.claim: Since everyone knows a stone carved now did not create its worshipper or the heavens and earth, the durability of idol worship implies another motive.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r6.anchor: العلم بأن هذا الحجر المنحوت في هذه الساعة ليس هو الذي خلقني وخلق السموات والأرض علم ضروري

RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r7.speaker: أبو معشر جعفر بن محمد المنجم البلخي
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r7.claim: Abu Maʿshar says some Chinese and Indians imagined God and angels as beautiful bodies veiled in heaven, making attractive statues of them to seek closeness.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r7.anchor: ما ذكره أبو معشر جعفر بن محمد المنجم البلخي في بعض مصنفاته أن كثيرا من أهل الصين والهند

RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r8.speaker: أكثر العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r8.claim: Most scholars trace planet worship to people linking seasonal and worldly changes with the planets' positions and movements.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r8.anchor: ما ذكره أكثر العلماء وهو أن الناس رأوا تغيرات أحوال هذا العالم مربوطة بتغيرات أحوال الكواكب

RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r9.speaker: أصحاب الأحكام
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r9.claim: One astrologically minded group regarded planets as self-existent beings that created the worlds and thus as gods in truth.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r9.anchor: فمنهم من اعتقد أنها أشياء واجبة الوجود لذواتها وهي التي خلقت هذه العوالم

RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r10.speaker: أصحاب الأحكام
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r10.claim: Another group held that planets were created by the greater God but create this world as intermediaries between God and humanity.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r10.anchor: ومنهم من اعتقد أنها مخلوقة للإله الأكبر لكنها خالقة لهذا العالم

RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r11.claim: Because planets were usually invisible, people made idols to represent them; over time they forgot the planets and worshipped only the statues.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r11.anchor: ثم لما طالت المدة ألغوا ذكر الكواكب وتجردوا لعبادة تلك التماثيل

RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r12.speaker: أصحاب الأحكام
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r12.claim: Astrologers prescribed talismans made at particular times in long cycles, believing them to bring benefits such as prosperity and protection; accumulated veneration became worship after the origin was forgotten.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r12.anchor: كانوا يعينون أوقاتا في السنين المتطاولة نحو الألف والألفين ويزعمون أن من اتخذ طلسمًا في ذلك الوقت

RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r13.claim: Another explanation is that people made images of revered deceased figures as intercessors with God on Judgment Day.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r13.anchor: متى مات منهم رجل كبير يعتقدون فيه أنه مجاب الدعوة ومقبول الشفاعة عند الله تعالى اتخذوا صنما على صورته

RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r14.claim: Some may have treated idols as prayer niches, prostrating toward them as Muslims face the qibla; ignorant people later mistook this for worship of the idols.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r14.anchor: يسجدون إليها لا لها كما أنا نسجد إلى القبلة لا للقبلة ولما استمرت هذه الحالة ظن الجهال من القوم أنه يجب عبادتها

RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r15.speaker: المجسمة
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r15.claim: Some corporealists may have believed that God could indwell an idol and worshipped it on that interpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p103#2/r15.anchor: لعلهم كانوا من المجسمة فاعتقدوا جواز حلول الرب فيها فعبدوها على هذا التأويل

RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r1.claim: Earth and heaven share corporeality with other bodies, so their distinct forms and properties require a determiner; if that determiner were bodily, it too would need a determiner, proving the creator is not a body.
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r1.anchor: فلا بد وأن يكون اختصاص كل واحد منهما بما اختص به من الأشكال والصفات والأخبار بتخصيص مخصص وبينا أن ذلك المخصص لو كان جسما

RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r2.claim: The argument that idols resemble God fails because the proof establishes that God is not corporeal.
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r2.anchor: أما قول من ذهب إلى عبادة الأوثان بناء على اعتقاد الشبه فلما دللنا بهذه الدلالة على نفي الجسمية فقد بطل قوله

RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r3.claim: Planets cannot be deities or world-governors: every body's attributes depend on a freely acting agent, so planets are servants, not lords.
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r3.anchor: كل جسم يفتقر في اتصافه بكل ما اتصف به إلى الفاعل المختار بطل كونها آلهة / وثبت أنها عبيد لا أرباب

RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r4.claim: Talismans work through planetary powers; proving the planets originated therefore defeats the talisman theory.
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r4.anchor: تأثير الطلسمات إنما يكون بواسطة قوى الكواكب

RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r5.claim: Reason alone neither establishes nor excludes worship directed toward revered dead people or images faced in prayer, but revelation forbids it, so Muslims must refrain.
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r5.anchor: وأما القول الرابع والخامس : فليس في العقل ما يوجه أو يحيله ، لكن الشرع لما منع منه وجب الامتناع عنه

RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r6.claim: The corporealist explanation for worshipping idols is also invalid because it depends on likening God to bodies.
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r6.anchor: وأما القول السادس : فهو أيضا بناء على التشبيه فثبت بما قدمنا

RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r7.claim: Showing that the world depends on a freely choosing creator who is transcendent beyond bodies refutes idol worship under every proposed explanation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p105/r7.anchor: إلى الصانع المختار المنزه عن الجسمية يبطل القول بعبادة الأوثان على كل التأويلات

RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r1.claim: Before Alexander, Greeks built temples to spiritual powers and luminous celestial bodies and worshipped them; several divine principles had round temples.
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r1.anchor: اليونانيين كانوا قبل خروج الإسكندر عمدوا إلى بناء هياكل لهم معروفة بأسماء القوى الروحانية والأجرام النيرة واتخذوها معبودا لهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r2.claim: Rāzī lists temples shaped as hexagons for Saturn, triangles for Jupiter, rectangles for Mars, and squares for the Sun.
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r2.anchor: وكان هيكل زحل مسدسا . وهيكل المشتري مثلثا . وهيكل المريخ مستطيلا

RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r3.claim: He adds that Venus's temple was triangular around a square, Mercury's triangular around a rectangle, and the Moon's octagonal.
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r3.anchor: وهيكل عطارد مثلثا في جوفه مستطيل ، وهيكل القمر مثمنا

RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r4.speaker: أصحاب التاريخ
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r4.claim: Historians say ʿAmr b. Luḥayy saw idol worshippers in al-Balqāʾ who called idols gods that brought victory and rain, received Hubal from them, and installed it in the Kaaba in Mecca, urging people to venerate it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r4.anchor: زعم أصحاب التاريخ أن عمرو بن لحي لما ساد قومه وترأس على طبقاتهم وولي أمر البيت الحرام اتفقت له سفرة إلى البلقاء

RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r5.claim: Among famous idol shrines were Ghumdan in Sana'a, built by al-Dahhak for Venus and destroyed by Uthman, and Nawbahar in Balkh, built by Manūshahr for the Moon.
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r5.anchor: من بيوت الأصنام المشهورة ( غمدان ) الذي بناه الضحاك على اسم الزهرة

RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r6.claim: Rāzī names Arab idols and their tribes or locations: Wadd for Kalb, Suwaʿ for Hudhayl, Yaghuth for Madhhij, Yaʿuq for Hamdan, Nasr for Dhu al-Kilaʿ in Himyar, al-Lat for Thaqif, Manat for Khazraj, al-ʿUzza for Kinana, and Asaf and Na'ila at Safa and Marwa.
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r6.anchor: مثل ( ود ) بدومة الجندل لكلب و ( سواع ) لبني هذيل و ( يغوث ) لبني مذحج

RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r7.speaker: زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r7.claim: Qusayy and Zayd opposed idol worship; Zayd's poem rejects al-Lat and al-ʿUzza and asks whether one God or a thousand should be worshipped.
RAZI-FULL:v2p105#2/r7.anchor: زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل وهو الذي يقول : فأربا واحدا أم ألف رب … أدين

IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r11.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r11.speaker: حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r11.claim: Hamza pauses before the hamza in الأرض، الأسماء، الآخرة and similar forms; other readers do not pause.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r11.anchor: وكذلك يسكت على اللام من ﴿ الأرض ﴾ البقرة 22 و ﴿ الأسماء ﴾ البقرة 31

IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r12.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r12.speaker: ورش عن نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r12.claim: Warsh transfers the hamza’s vowel to the preceding consonant and drops it, both within words and across word boundaries.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r12.anchor: وروى ورش عن نافع أنه كان يلقي حركة الهمزة على اللام التي قبلها مثل ﴿ الأرض ﴾ و ﴿ الآخرة ﴾
